definition_zh: 内陆的；内地的（名词）内陆；内地；向内陆地
definition_en: situated in the interior of a country, far away from the sea or from the coast, or toward the inside of a country
core_image: 渔船驶离海岸，一路向着陆地深处的那片腹地
scene: 许多内陆城镇远离海岸，货物要靠铁路转运才能出口。Many inland towns lie far from the sea, so their goods travel by rail to reach the ports.
sceneCN: 这里 inland 是「内陆的、内地的」（第 1 个义项：远离海洋的内陆位置）；句意：许多内陆城镇远离海岸，货物要靠铁路转运才能出口。

collocations.zh: 国内税收（并不专指内陆）

derivatives.zh: 由 inland 加表人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「内地人；内陆居民」
罕见形式，inland 加后缀 -ish，义为「内陆的；带内陆特征的」
复合词 land 加 locked，义为「被陆地包围的；内陆的」，是 inland 的近义表达
固定搭配，指内河航运，与内陆水域的交通有关

senses.title: Lying far from the sea
senses.definition: located in the middle of a country, away from the coast or the sea
senses.definitionCN: 位于某个国家的中部、远离海岸或海洋
senses.example: Kansas is an inland state with no ocean coastline.
senses.exampleCN: 堪萨斯是一个没有海岸线的内陆州。
senses.why: In gives the direction toward the inside and land names the ground, so inland is land turned away from the sea.
senses.whyCN: in 指出方向朝内，land 点出土地，于是 inland 就是背向海洋的那片土地。

senses.title: Moving toward the interior
senses.definition: traveling or extending from the coast toward the middle of a country
senses.definitionCN: 从海岸向国家中部行进或延伸
senses.example: After the storm, they sailed inland along the wide river.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，他们沿着宽阔的河流向内陆航行。
senses.why: The same words that name an inner place also name motion toward it, as in go inland.
senses.whyCN: 同一组字既可直接指内陆的地点，也可指朝内陆移动的方向，如 go inland。

senses.title: The interior region itself
senses.definition: the parts of a country that lie away from the coast, taken as a region
senses.definitionCN: 作为一整片区域，指远离海岸的国家腹地
senses.example: People from the inland speak a softer dialect.
senses.exampleCN: 内地来的人说话口音更柔和。
senses.why: Once a place word can name a place, the compound is used as a noun for that region.
senses.whyCN: 一个表示地点的复合词一旦能指地点，就可以直接当名词，指这一整片地区。

senses.title: Domestic rather than foreign
senses.definition: belonging to a country itself rather than to its coastline trade or foreign dealings
senses.definitionCN: 属于本国本身，而不涉及沿海贸易或对外事务
senses.example: The old term inland revenue referred to taxes collected within the country.
senses.exampleCN: 旧称 inland revenue 指的是在本国境内征收的税，并不专指内陆。
senses.why: Because inland marks what is inside the country, it was once stretched to mean domestic, which is now mainly a historical use.
senses.whyCN: 因为 inland 标记「国境之内」，旧时被引申为「国内的」；这一用法如今主要见于历史语境与专名。

senses.title: Descriptive of geography and climate
senses.definition: used to describe places like seas, waters, or climates that belong to the interior
senses.definitionCN: 用来形容属于内陆腹地的海域、水域或气候
senses.example: The Caspian Sea is the largest inland body of water on Earth.
senses.exampleCN: 里海是地球上最大的内陆水域。
senses.why: Geographers apply the compound to water and weather that sit inside continents rather than at their edges.
senses.whyCN: 地理学者把这个复合词用于位于大陆内部、而非边缘的水体与气候。

intro.en: Inland is an English compound of the preposition in and the noun land, built in the Middle Ages and first recorded in the thirteenth century.
intro.cn: inland 是古英语以来由介词 in 与名词 land（土地）组合而成的复合词，大约在十三世纪见于文字。

items.en: In and land are both Old English words, land going back to a Germanic root for open country.
items.cn: in 与 land 都是古英语词，land 又可上溯到日耳曼语中表示「开阔土地」的词根。

items.en: Compounds of in and land appear in Middle English, first for land inside a country.
items.cn: 中古英语中，in 与 land 的组合开始出现，最初指位于国家内部的土地。

items.en: The word comes to describe towns, roads, and goods that are away from the coast.
items.cn: 随后这个词开始形容远离海岸的城镇、道路与货物。

items.en: A provincial meaning of inland as domestic, as opposed to foreign, appears in law and trade writing.
items.cn: 十六至十七世纪，inland 在法律与贸易文中出现「国内的（相对外国的）」这一引申义。

items.en: Modern use keeps the adjective, noun, and adverb forms, and inland revenue survives mainly as a name.
items.cn: 现代英语保留形容词、名词、副词三种词性，inland revenue 主要以专名形式留存。

note.en: Inland pairs in and land inside the country, and it stands beside nearby words for land and sea.
note.cn: inland 把 in 与 land 组合成「国境内部」，与一批表示陆地与海洋的词相邻。

entries.definition: people who live in the interior of a country
entries.definitionCN: 内地人；内陆居民，是 inlander 的复数

entries.definition: the first sight or arrival of land after a voyage by sea
entries.definitionCN: 航海中首次见到或登陆陆地，与 inland 共享 land 这一成分

entries.definition: surrounded by land and having no sea coast
entries.definitionCN: 被陆地环绕、没有海岸的，是 inland 的近义复合词

entries.definition: a piece of land with water all around it
entries.definitionCN: 岛屿，与 inland 只差首字母，词源不同，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: the inside part of a country or region, away from the coast
entries.definitionCN: 内地；腹地，与 inland 常可互换

entries.definition: near or along the sea coast
entries.definitionCN: 沿海的；海岸的，与 inland 语义相反

entries.definition: in the interior of a country, away from the coast
entries.definitionCN: 在内地；向内地，是 inland 的口语化同义说法

normalIntro.en: Inland is simply in plus land: the land that is inside a country, away from where the sea begins.
normalIntro.cn: inland 就是 in 加 land：一个「往里」的 land，也就是远离海洋、处在国境内部的那片土地。

normal.en: Read inland as in plus land, in the sense of the inside of a country.
normal.cn: 把 inland 拆成 in 加 land，in 指「国家的内部」。

normal.en: Inland is the opposite of coastal.
normal.cn: inland 的对立面是 coastal（沿海的）。

normal.en: Go inland means travel away from the coast, so inland also works as an adverb.
normal.cn: go inland 表示向内陆走，所以 inland 还能当副词。

normal.en: An inland sea lies inside the continent, like a lake with no exit.
normal.cn: inland sea 指位于大陆内部的海，像没有出口的湖。

normal.en: Compare island: island is land in the sea, inland is land inside the country.
normal.cn: 对比 island：island 是海中的陆地，inland 是国境内部的陆地。

abstract.en: Picture a fishing boat leaving the coast and moving toward dry hills.
abstract.cn: 想象一条渔船离开海岸，朝着干燥的山丘前进。

abstract.en: Picture a map where the blue edge fades into brown plains.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，蓝色的海岸线渐渐过渡成褐色平原。

abstract.en: Picture a lake far from any port, ringed by fields.
abstract.cn: 想象一个远离港口的湖，四周被田野环绕。

examples.en: The company moved its factory to an inland region to cut costs.
examples.cn: 公司把工厂迁到内陆地区以降低成本。

examples.en: Rain seldom reaches this inland valley in winter.
examples.cn: 冬天，雨水很少到达这条内陆谷地。

examples.en: They walked inland for hours before they found a village.
examples.cn: 他们向内陆走了好几个小时才找到一座村庄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因兰」——因为离海岸远、四周都是兰色的田野，所以是内陆；谐音只帮助记形，与词源无关。

root: 古英语介词 in（向内）+ 名词 land（土地）→ 中古英语内陆复合词 inland，字面意思是「处于在内的土地」。与 landfall、landlocked、mainland 共享 land 这一成分。

sensesIntro.en: From one spatial core of land inside a country, inland spreads from place to motion, then to the region as a noun, and finally to domestic and geographic uses.
sensesIntro.cn: inland 从一个空间核心「国境内部的土地」出发，先指地点，再指移动方向，接着当名词指这片地区，最后延伸到国内与地理用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: land lying far inside the country, far from the sea.
core.cn: 核心意象：远离海洋、位于国境深处的土地。

branches.en: The static place where something lies inside the country.
branches.cn: 指静态的地点，即处在国境内部某处。

branches.en: The same word turned into a direction of travel, as in go inland.
branches.cn: 同一组字转成移动方向，如 go inland（向内陆走）。

branches.en: The noun sense names the whole interior as a region.
branches.cn: 名词义指整片腹地这片地区。

branches.en: Geographers use the place sense for inland seas and inland climates.
branches.cn: 地理学沿用地点义，说 inland seas 与内陆气候。

branches.en: Because it marks what is inside the country, inland once meant domestic.
branches.cn: 因为 inland 标记「国境之内」，旧时曾表示「国内的」。

intro.en: Inland is a native English compound of in and land, with a small modern family of inlander and inlandish.
intro.cn: inland 是英语本土复合词，由 in 与 land 组成，现代衍生出 inlander、inlandish 等少量同族词。

latinIntro.en: The compound is native English, but land and in go back to Germanic roots; the Latin entries below are the remote ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词是土生土长的英语词，但 in 与 land 都上溯到日耳曼语词根；下方拉丁语条目是更远的源头。

items.example: The first element in- points inside the country.
items.exampleCN: 首成分 in- 指出方向是国境之内。

items.meaning: the solid surface of the earth
items.example: Land is the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: land 是复合词的后一半。

items.example: The suffix -er forms inlander.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 inlander。

items.example: Inlander names a person of the interior.
items.exampleCN: inlander 指住在内地的人。

items.meaningCN: 具有……特征的（形容词后缀）
items.example: The suffix -ish forms inlandish.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ish 构成 inlandish。

items.example: Landlocked uses -locked after land.
items.exampleCN: landlocked 在 land 后接 -locked。

items.meaning: surrounded by land with no coast
items.example: Landlocked is the near neighbour of inland.
items.exampleCN: landlocked 是 inland 的近邻词。

items.meaning: first arrival at land after a voyage
items.example: Landfall pairs land with fall.
items.exampleCN: landfall 把 land 与 fall 组合起来。

items.meaning: the main mass of land, as opposed to an island
items.example: Mainland is the bigger land mass.
items.exampleCN: mainland 指更大的陆块。

items.example: Upcountry is the informal partner of inland.
items.exampleCN: upcountry 是 inland 的口语化说法。

latinEntries.example: Latin in is the remote ancestor of the English in.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语介词 in 是英语 in 的远祖。

latinEntries.example: Terra shows the Latin word for land in other English forms.
latinEntries.exampleCN: terra 是拉丁语里「土地」的说法，其他英语词中仍能看到它。

definition_zh: 小湾；水湾；入口；进水口
definition_en: a small narrow bay or opening where water comes in from the sea
core_image: 海水从狭窄的缺口涌进岸线，形成受风浪较少的静水小湾
scene: 沿海小镇的渔民把船停在礁石间的小湾里，避开外海的风浪。The fishermen kept their boats in a sheltered inlet among the rocks.
sceneCN: 这里 inlet 是「小湾」（第 1 个义项：海水进入陆地的小型湾口）；句意：渔民把船停泊在礁石之间受遮蔽的小湾里。

derivatives.zh: 由构词部分 let（让）与 in（进入）反向组合成名词，义为「嵌入部分；镶入件」
由 in 加 coming 构成，义为「进来的；新来的」，与 inlet 共享「进入」的方位核心
由 enter 加名词后缀构成，义为「进入；入口」，与 inlet 的入口义项呼应

senses.title: A small narrow bay
senses.definition: a small narrow bay of water leading into the land from the sea or a lake
senses.definitionCN: 从海或湖伸入陆地的狭小海湾
senses.example: The village lies at the head of a narrow inlet.
senses.exampleCN: 那个村庄位于一条狭窄小湾的尽头。
senses.why: The core frame of in plus let shows water being let in through a narrow opening, and that shape is exactly a small bay.
senses.whyCN: in（进入）加 let（让）的框架表示「让水进来」的狭窄通道，这个形状正是一条小湾，所以地理学与日常用法都用它指小海湾。

senses.title: An arm of the sea reaching inland
senses.definition: a long narrow stretch of sea water that runs inland along a coast
senses.definitionCN: 沿海岸伸入内陆的狭长海水水域
senses.example: Mudflats line the shores of the tidal inlet.
senses.exampleCN: 潮汐水道两岸是泥滩。
senses.why: When the opening is long instead of round, the same let-in frame stretches into an arm of the sea, so a fjord or tidal channel also counts as an inlet.
senses.whyCN: 当缺口狭长而非圆形时，「让水进来」的框架被拉长成一条伸入内陆的水臂，因此峡湾与潮汐水道也都算 inlet。

senses.title: An opening where water enters
senses.definition: an opening through which water or another fluid enters a place, pipe, or body of water
senses.definitionCN: 水或其他流体进入某处、某管道或某水体的开口
senses.example: Clean the inlet of the pump every month.
senses.exampleCN: 每月清理一次水泵的进水口。
senses.why: Engineering simply keeps the literal reading: the spot where fluid is let in, whether into a basin, a machine, or a body of water.
senses.whyCN: 工程语境保留了这个词的字面读法：流体被「让进来」的那个位置，不论进入的是水盆、机器还是水体。

senses.title: An opening for air or fuel
senses.definition: a narrow opening through which air, gas, or fuel is drawn into an engine or a room
senses.definitionCN: 空气、气体或燃料被吸入发动机或房间的狭小开口
senses.example: Clogged air inlets reduce the efficiency of the engine.
senses.exampleCN: 堵塞的进气口会降低发动机的效率。
senses.why: Once let in is extended beyond water to air and fuel, the word names the mouth of any intake, so car parts and ventilation systems use it too.
senses.whyCN: 当「让进来」的对象从水扩展到空气和燃料，这个词就指任何进气系统的开口，汽车零件和通风系统也沿用它。

senses.title: A narrow passage into a place
senses.definition: a narrow way into a place, often an enclosed or hidden one
senses.definitionCN: 进入某地、尤其封闭或隐蔽之处的狭窄通道
senses.example: A stone inlet led from the courtyard into the cellar.
senses.exampleCN: 一条石砌窄道从庭院通向地窖。
senses.why: The spatial picture of a narrow opening that leads inward is used more broadly for any narrow entrance, not only for water.
senses.whyCN: 「通向内部的狭口」这一空间画面被推广到任何狭窄入口，这时指的可以是人的通道而不是水。

intro.en: Inlet joins the Old English adverb inn (into) with the verb lettan (to let), giving the plain sense a place where water is let in.
intro.cn: inlet 由古英语副词 inn（进入）与动词 lettan（让、放行）组合而成，字面意思是「让水进来的地方」。

items.en: The preposition inn means into, and lettan means to let or allow.
items.cn: 古英语里 inn 表示「进入」，lettan 意为让、放行。

items.en: The compound is first recorded for a narrow passage of water running into land.
items.cn: 这个复合词最早记录用于指伸入陆地的狭窄水道。

items.en: The same word is applied to mechanical intakes for air and water.
items.cn: 同一个词被用于指空气和水的机械入口。

items.en: Geographers use inlet as a general term for any small coastal indentation.
items.cn: 地理学家把 inlet 用作任何小型海岸凹入处的通称。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the coastal and the engineering senses side by side.
items.cn: 现代英语让地理义与工程义并存。

note.en: Inlet belongs to a set of in plus verb compounds, and it sits next to coastal and mechanical intake words.
note.cn: inlet 属于「in 加动词」的复合词族，并与海岸水域词、机械入口词相邻。

entries.definition: a point where something flows out
entries.definitionCN: 出口；排放口

entries.definition: a pipe that brings fluid in
entries.definitionCN: 进水管

entries.definition: to allow someone or something to enter
entries.definitionCN: 让……进来

entries.definition: a small sheltered bay
entries.definitionCN: 小海湾；隐蔽的小湾

entries.definition: a broad part of the sea enclosed by land
entries.definitionCN: 海湾（通常比 inlet 大）

entries.definition: an opening where air or liquid is taken in
entries.definitionCN: 进气口；进水口

normalIntro.en: Inlet is a picture-word: in plus let, the sea is let in through a narrow gap.
normalIntro.cn: inlet 是一个画面词：in 加 let，海水被「让进」一道窄缝。

normal.en: In plus let makes inlet, the place that lets water in.
normal.cn: in 加 let 得 inlet，就是让水进来的地方。

normal.en: A sheltered inlet keeps fishing boats safe from rough seas.
normal.cn: 避风的小湾能保护渔船不受风浪侵袭。

normal.en: Air inlet and water inlet are standard terms in engines and pipes.
normal.cn: air inlet 与 water inlet 是发动机和管道里的标准术语。

normal.en: Compare outlet, the compound with the opposite direction.
normal.cn: 对比 outlet：方向相反的复合词。

normal.en: Coves and bays are neighbors; inlets are usually narrow.
normal.cn: cove 与 bay 是近邻词，而 inlet 通常更狭窄。

abstract.en: See a narrow blue finger of sea pushing between two cliffs.
abstract.cn: 想象一条狭长的蓝色海水伸进两座悬崖之间。

abstract.en: Hear the engine breathing through its air inlet.
abstract.cn: 想象发动机通过进气口「呼吸」。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway in a wall that is just wide enough to let a river in.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上有一道刚够让河流通过的窄门。

examples.en: We swam across the shallow inlet before the tide turned.
examples.cn: 涨潮前我们游过了那片浅浅的小湾。

examples.en: The factory draws cooling water from a neighbouring inlet.
examples.cn: 工厂从邻近的水口抽取冷却水。

examples.en: Several estuaries drain into this long coastal inlet.
examples.cn: 好几条河口流入这条狭长的海岸水道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「引（in）来（let）」——让水引进来的小湾，谐音只是拆字联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 inn（进入）+ lettan（让、放行）→ 中古英语 let-in（让进来）→ 现代英语 inlet：核心义「让水进入的狭窄通道」。

sensesIntro.en: Inlet starts from the literal picture of water being let in through a gap, then widens to water passages, machine intakes, and narrow entrances in general.
sensesIntro.cn: inlet 从「水被让进窄口」的字面画面出发，再扩展到水道、风机进水口，以及一般的狭窄入口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sea water pressed into a narrow gap in the coast and held there.
core.cn: 核心意象：海水从海岸的窄缝涌进去，停留在那里。

branches.en: The small bay is the everyday coastal sense.
branches.cn: 小湾是日常的海岸义项。

branches.en: A long arm of the sea is the stretched version of the bay.
branches.cn: 伸入内陆的狭长水臂是拉长版的小湾。

branches.en: The fluid intake is the literal machine sense.
branches.cn: 进水口是字面意义上的机械义项。

branches.en: Air and fuel intakes extend the opening to gas.
branches.cn: 进风口把入口义扩展到气体。

branches.en: Both a bay and a narrow passage are openings that lead inward.
branches.cn: 小湾与窄入口都是通向内部的开口。

intro.en: Inlet is a native English compound, built from the Ancient English in-word for into and the verb to let.
intro.cn: inlet 是英语本土复合词，由古英语中表示「进入」的 in 与动词 let 组成。

latinIntro.en: Inlet has no Latin root, but let itself goes back to a Proto-Germanic verb reconstructed as laitijan.
latinIntro.cn: inlet 没有拉丁词根；不过 let 可追溯到重构的原始日耳曼语动词 laitijan。

items.example: The first part names the direction of entry.
items.exampleCN: 前半部分指出进入的方向。

items.example: Inn is the ancestor of modern in.
items.exampleCN: inn 是现代 in 的祖先。

items.example: The verb gives the sense of being allowed to pass.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词带来「被允许通过」的含义。

items.example: Let survives unchanged in one set of uses.
items.exampleCN: let 在一组用法中保持不变。

items.example: The compound keeps the literal picture.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词保留了字面画面。

items.example: Though -et seems a suffix, the t belongs to let.
items.exampleCN: 虽然 -et 看起来像词尾，但 t 其实属于 let。

items.example: The opposite compound follows the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: 反义复合词用了同样的构词方式。

items.example: Out- mirrors in- in outlet.
items.exampleCN: 在 outlet 里 out- 与 in- 相对。

items.example: Native words sometimes take -age for places.
items.exampleCN: 本土词有时用 -age 表示地点。

definition_zh: 天生的；固有的；内在的
definition_en: existing in a person or thing from birth, rather than learned or acquired
core_image: 婴儿出生时自带的、刻在身体里的原始程序
scene: 小鸭子破壳后不久就跟着眼前移动的东西走，研究人员认为这是天生行为。Researchers believe this behaviour is innate in young ducks.
sceneCN: 这里 innate 是「天生的」（第 1 个义项：出生即有的、非学来的）；句意：研究人员认为刚孵化的小鸭具有这种天生行为。

derivatives.zh: 由 innate 加 -ly 构成，义为「天生地；固有地」
由 innate 加 -ness 构成，义为「先天性；固有性」
由 natus 同源家族加 -ity 构成，义为「出生；诞生」
与 innate 共用 nascor 词根的形容词，义为「本土的；出生的」

senses.title: Present from birth
senses.definition: present in a living thing from birth and not learned through experience
senses.definitionCN: 与生俱来、并非通过经验学会的
senses.example: Gull chicks have an innate fear of shadows from above.
senses.exampleCN: 海鸥幼鸟天生害怕上方掠过的影子。
senses.why: The Latin verb innasci means to be born in, so the word points to whatever a creature is born with: the word names what was born in, not what was put in later.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 innasci 意为「生于其中」，所以这个词指向生物一出生就带着的东西，指「出生就长在里面」而不是后天加进去的部分。

senses.title: Natural rather than taught
senses.definition: coming naturally to a person and not the result of teaching or training
senses.definitionCN: 自然而然地具有，并非教出来的或练出来的
senses.example: She showed an innate talent for drawing as a child.
senses.exampleCN: 她小时候就表现出绘画天赋。
senses.why: In philosophy and education, the born-in idea becomes a contrast with learning, so innate names the part of an ability that arrives naturally.
senses.whyCN: 在哲学与教育学中，「生于其中」的意思与学习形成对照，于是 innate 专门指能力中自然获得的那部分。

senses.title: Belonging to the nature of something
senses.definition: forming an essential part of the nature of a thing
senses.definitionCN: 构成事物本质、不可剥离的部分
senses.example: Tension is almost innate to the relationship between the two branches.
senses.exampleCN: 两部门间的紧张几乎内在于它们的关系。
senses.why: The born-in frame stretches from a creature to an object or relationship, so anything built into its nature can be called innate.
senses.whyCN: 「生于其中」的框架从生物拓展到物体或关系上，凡属本质内建的都可以叫 innate。

senses.title: Present at the start of a process
senses.definition: existing already at the beginning of a process or in a system by default
senses.definitionCN: 在某一过程或系统一开始就存在、作为默认设置存在的
senses.example: An innate capacity for language learning seems shared by young children.
senses.exampleCN: 幼儿似乎共有一种与生俱来的语言学习能力。
senses.why: The word occasionally describes what a system or a young learner already carries at its start, but this sense is rare and literary.
senses.whyCN: 这个词偶尔描述系统或年幼学习者一开始就带着的东西，但这一义项较少见，偏书面。

intro.en: Innate comes from Latin innatus, born in, from innasci, built on in plus nasci, to be born.
intro.cn: innate 来自拉丁语 innatus（生在其中），源于 innasci，由 in 与 nasci（出生）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root genh means to be born or to give birth.
items.cn: 重构的印欧词根 genh 意为「出生」或「生育」。

items.en: Nasci means to be born, and innasci means to be born in or to arise in.
items.cn: nasci 意为出生，innasci 意为生在……之中或产生于……。

items.en: The participle innatus records being born in, and the adjective innatus means natural.
items.cn: 分词 innatus 记录「生于其中」，形容词 innatus 意为天然的。

items.en: Innate enters English through the learned Latin form and is first used in philosophy and theology.
items.cn: innate 经由书面拉丁语形式进入英语，最初用于哲学与神学。

items.en: Natural science takes the word for behaviours and traits that need no teaching.
items.cn: 自然科学用这个词指不需要教就有的行为与特性。

items.en: Modern English also uses innate for qualities that belong to the nature of a thing.
items.cn: 现代英语也用 innate 指属于事物本性的特质。

note.en: Innate shares the Latin born root with a large family, and it is often contrasted with learned, acquired, or inborn.
note.cn: innate 与一大族词共享拉丁语「出生」词根，并常与 learned、acquired、inborn 等词对照。

entries.definition: connected with where one was born
entries.definitionCN: 出生地的；本土的

entries.definition: the basic qualities of a thing
entries.definitionCN: 本性；天性

entries.definition: before birth
entries.definitionCN: 产前的；出生前的

entries.definition: just beginning to exist
entries.definitionCN: 初生的；新生的

entries.definition: present from birth, especially of qualities
entries.definitionCN: 天生的（尤指性质）

entries.definition: based on instinct rather than thought
entries.definitionCN: 本能的

entries.definition: passed from parents to children through genes
entries.definitionCN: 遗传的

normalIntro.en: Innate wraps in (within) around the Latin verb nasci (to be born): born into you.
normalIntro.cn: innate 用 in（在内）包裹拉丁语动词 nasci（出生）：生下来就在你身体里。

normal.en: In plus natus means born in, which gives innate.
normal.cn: in 加 natus 表示「生于其中」，这正是 innate。

normal.en: Innate ability and innate talent describe what arrives with birth.
normal.cn: innate ability 与 innate talent 都描述出生就带来的能力。

normal.en: Innate immunity is the defence you have before any infection.
normal.cn: innate immunity 是感染发生之前的天然防御。

normal.en: Ballet dancers practise until steps look innate, yet the speed is trained.
normal.cn: 芭蕾演员练到动作看似天生，但那份速度其实是练出来的。

normal.en: Compare inborn and native; all share the Latin born root.
normal.cn: 对比 inborn 与 native：它们共享拉丁语「出生」词根。

abstract.en: Picture a newborn opening its mouth to feed before anyone teaches it.
abstract.cn: 想象新生儿在没人教的情况下就张嘴吃奶。

abstract.en: See a label stamped inside a product at the factory, not added later.
abstract.cn: 想象产品出厂时内壁就有的印记，而不是后来贴上去的。

abstract.en: Hear a baby cry in every language on earth without instruction.
abstract.cn: 想象世界各地的婴儿在被教之前都会哭。

examples.en: Researchers disagree about how much of language is innate.
examples.cn: 研究者对语言有多少成分是天生的问题看法不一。

examples.en: Some birds build their nests by innate skill rather than observation.
examples.cn: 有些鸟凭天生技能而非观察来筑巢。

examples.en: An innate curiosity drove him to open every machine in the house.
examples.cn: 与生俱来的好奇心驱使他拆开家里每一台机器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因内特」——原因在内，即天生内建；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（在内）+ nasci（出生）→ innasci（生于其中）→ 拉丁分词 innatus（生的）→ 英语 innate，核心义「生来就在里面的」。

sensesIntro.en: Innate begins with what a creature is born with, moves to natural ability against learning, stretches to the essential nature of things, and rarely marks what exists at a process start.
sensesIntro.cn: innate 从生物出生即有的属性出发，转到与学习相对的自然能力，再扩展到事物的本质属性，偶尔指某过程一开始就存在的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a program already inside a newborn when it arrives.
core.cn: 核心意象：新生儿降生时体内就有的程序。

branches.en: What is present at birth is the biological sense.
branches.cn: 出生即有的属性是生物学义项。

branches.en: Natural talent is the sense opposed to learning.
branches.cn: 自然才能是与学习相对的义项。

branches.en: Belonging to the nature of a thing is the essential sense.
branches.cn: 属于事物本质是本质义项。

branches.en: What exists from a process start is the rare extension.
branches.cn: 过程一开始就有的东西是少见的外延。

branches.en: Both born-in traits and natural gifts need no teacher.
branches.cn: 与生俱来的特质与自然天赋都不需要老师。

intro.en: Innate is a single Latin participle with an in- prefix and the born root; the English family grows through -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: innate 由带 in- 前缀的拉丁分词直接而来，英语再借 -ly 与 -ness 扩充词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin nasci and natus supply the born root found in native, nature, natal, and innate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nasci 与 natus 提供「出生」词根，native、nature、natal 与 innate 都从这个词根长出。

items.example: In- places the born quality inside the person.
items.exampleCN: in- 把「生下来的性质」放进了人里面。

items.example: The verb is the heart of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的核心。

items.example: The participle supplies the stem of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 分词提供了形容词的词干。

items.example: The compound verb adds the inside position.
items.exampleCN: 复合动词加上了「在内部」的位置。

items.example: The adjective passes directly into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词直接进入英语。

items.example: It forms innately.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 innately。

items.example: It forms innateness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 innateness。

items.example: Native keeps the place of birth.
items.exampleCN: native 保留了「出生地」的意思。

items.example: Natal appears in prenatal and postnatal.
items.exampleCN: natal 出现在 prenatal 与 postnatal 中。

derivatives.zh: 由 innate 加 -ly 构成，义为「天生地；固有地」
由 innate 加 -ness 构成，义为「先天性；固有性」
由同源词根 natus 构成，义为「本土的；出生地的」

definition_zh: 无数的；数不清的
definition_en: too many to be counted or numbered
core_image: 夜空里挤满的星点，一次次点下去怎么也点不完
scene: 沙滩上的沙粒太多，用放大镜一颗颗数也数不完。The grains of sand on the beach are innumerable.
sceneCN: 这里 innumerable 是「数不清的」（第 1 个义项：多到无法计数）；句意：沙滩上的沙粒多得数不清。

derivatives.zh: 由 innumerable 加 -ly 构成，义为「无数地；数不清地」
由 innumerable 加 -ity 构成，义为「数不清；无数」

senses.title: Too many to count
senses.definition: so many that they cannot be counted
senses.definitionCN: 多到无法逐一数清
senses.example: The sky was full of innumerable stars.
senses.exampleCN: 天空布满了无数星星。
senses.why: The in- prefix negates numerare (to count), so the adjective literally says not countable, and a crowd too large for counting is exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 否定 numerare（数），所以这个词字面上就是「不可数的」，多到无法计数的事物正合此义。

senses.title: Beyond calculation
senses.definition: too many or too great in quantity to be calculated precisely
senses.definitionCN: 数量太多或太大，无法精确估算
senses.example: Innumerable tiny organisms live in the upper layer of the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋上层生活着数不尽的微小生物。
senses.why: Away from crowds and stars, the same not-countable idea covers quantities that science can only estimate, such as grains or microbes.
senses.whyCN: 离开人群与星空，同一个「不可数」的观念延伸到科学只能估算的数量，例如沙粒或微生物。

senses.title: Countless occasions
senses.definition: used for something that has happened very many times and cannot be counted
senses.definitionCN: 用于发生过极多次、难以计数的事情
senses.example: He has explained the rule innumerable times.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规则他已经解释过无数次了。
senses.why: Counting is also done in time, so innumerable times simply means too many occasions to count.
senses.whyCN: 计数也可以作用于时间次数，所以 innumerable times 就是次数多到数不清。

senses.title: Too many to list
senses.definition: used in formal writing for examples or details too many to mention one by one
senses.definitionCN: 正式写作中用于例子或细节太多、无法逐一列举
senses.example: Innumerable instances could be cited from the records.
senses.exampleCN: 从档案中可以举出不胜枚举的实例。
senses.why: In formal prose the not-countable force turns into a rhetorical device: the writer signals endless examples without naming them.
senses.whyCN: 在正式文体中，「不可数」的力量变成修辞手段：作者暗示例子无穷多，而不必逐一列出。

intro.en: Innumerable is built from the Latin prefix in- (not) and numerare (to count), with the English -able suffix added.
intro.cn: innumerable 由拉丁语前缀 in-（不）与 numerare（数）+ 英语后缀 -able 构成。

items.en: Numerus means a number, and numerare means to count or number.
items.cn: 拉丁语 numerus 意为数目，numerare 意为数、计数。

items.en: Innumerabilis already joins in- with numerare to mean not countable.
items.cn: 拉丁语 innumerabilis 已经把 in- 与 numerare 结合，表示「不可数的」。

items.en: Learned writers borrow the negative form with the suffix -bilis, meaning able to be.
items.cn: 中世纪的博学作者借用了带后缀 -bilis（可以……的）的否定形式。

items.en: The adjective enters English, replacing the older form, through the Latin channel.
items.cn: 这个形容词经由拉丁语渠道进入英语，取代了更早的形式。

items.en: Modern dictionaries give both innumerable and the shorter form innumerous for common use.
items.cn: 现代词典同时收录 innumerable 与较短的 innumerous 供日常使用。

items.en: Modern English keeps the word mostly in formal and literary prose.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个词主要保留在正式文体与文学文本中。

note.en: Innumerable shares the count root with a wide Latin family, and it belongs to a scale of number words ending in countless.
note.cn: innumerable 与一大族拉丁词共享「数」词根，并与从 countless 一路排开的数量词构成尺度。

entries.definition: many, though still countable
entries.definitionCN: 众多的（仍可数）

entries.definition: able to work with numbers
entries.definitionCN: 会算数的

entries.definition: to list items one by one
entries.definitionCN: 逐项列举

entries.definition: a shorter rare synonym
entries.definitionCN: 罕见的较简短同义词

entries.definition: too many to count
entries.definitionCN: 无数的；数不清的

entries.definition: an extremely large number
entries.definitionCN: 无数的；极大量

entries.definition: too many to number
entries.definitionCN: 数不清的

entries.definition: too great to measure or calculate
entries.definitionCN: 多得无法计算的

normalIntro.en: Innumerable is the negative of countable number: in plus numerable, not able to be numbered.
normalIntro.cn: innumerable 是「可数」的否定：in 加 numerable，即「无法被计数的」。

normal.en: Numerable means able to be counted; in- flips it to not countable.
normal.cn: numerable 意为可以计数的，in- 把它翻转为不可计数。

normal.en: Innumerable stars fill the dark sky over a desert.
normal.cn: 沙漠夜空被无数星星填满。

normal.en: The phrase innumerable times means far more often than anyone would count.
normal.cn: innumerable times 表示多到没人会去数的次数。

normal.en: Compare countless and numberless, which carry the same negative count idea.
normal.cn: 对比 countless 与 numberless：它们同样带有否定计数的意思。

normal.en: Keep the older innumerous in mind as a rare twin.
normal.cn: 记住更老的 innumerous 是它的罕见双胞胎。

abstract.en: Imagine trying to count raindrops on a window during a storm.
abstract.cn: 想象暴雨中试图数清窗上每一颗雨滴。

abstract.en: See a ledger whose last page never arrives, so the total can never be filled.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账册永远没有最后一页，总额永远填不完。

abstract.en: Hear a child asking why again and again without end.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子不断地问「为什么」，怎么数都数不完。

examples.en: The old manuscript contained innumerable marginal notes.
examples.cn: 这份古老手稿里有数不清的页边批注。

examples.en: Innumerable forms of life are hidden in a handful of soil.
examples.cn: 一把土里藏着无数种生命形式。

examples.en: She has been thanked innumerable times for her help.
examples.cn: 她因为帮助别人而被感谢过无数次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怒数」——气得数下去也数不完，就是无数；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 numerus（数目）+ numerare（数）→ numerabilis（可数的）→ 加否定前缀 in- 成 innumerabilis → 英语 innumerable，核心义「无法计数的」。

sensesIntro.en: Innumerable starts with things too many to count, then widens to quantities beyond calculation, repeated occasions, and examples too many to list.
sensesIntro.cn: innumerable 先从多到数不清的事物出发，再扩展到难以计算的量、重复的次数和不胜枚举的例子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sky packed with stars beyond any counting.
core.cn: 核心意象：星星挤满夜空，怎么数也数不完。

branches.en: Things too many to count are the core sense.
branches.cn: 多到无法计数的事物是核心义项。

branches.en: Sea microbes are the scientific beyond-calculation sense.
branches.cn: 海洋微生物是科学上的「难以估量」义项。

branches.en: Repeated occasions show counting stretched over time.
branches.cn: 重复发生的次数把计数延伸到时间上。

branches.en: Examples too many to list are the formal rhetorical sense.
branches.cn: 不胜枚举的例子是正式的修辞义项。

branches.en: Both stars and microbes defeat any attempt to number them.
branches.cn: 星星与微生物都让一切计数尝试失败。

intro.en: Innumerable pairs the negation in- with the counting stem numer; English adds -able and -ous to extend the family.
intro.cn: innumerable 把否定前缀 in- 与「数」的词干 numer 结合，英语再用 -able 与 -ous 扩充词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin numerus and numerare supply the counting root, and innumerabilis already carries the negative adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 numerus 与 numerare 提供「数」的词根，innumerabilis 本身已是带否定的形容词。

items.example: In- turns countable into uncountable.
items.exampleCN: in- 把「可数」变成「不可数」。

items.example: The noun is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的基础。

items.example: The verb supplies the counting action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供计数的动作。

items.example: The suffix makes numerable.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 numerable。

items.example: The English form keeps the sense of the suffix.
items.exampleCN: 英语形式保留了这个后缀的意思。

items.example: It forms innumerous.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 innumerous。

items.example: Numerous is the positive twin.
items.exampleCN: numerous 是肯定形式的双胞胎。

items.example: Numerate names a skill with numbers.
items.exampleCN: numerate 指数字方面的能力。

items.example: It forms innumerability.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 innumerability。

definition_zh: 过度的；过分的；无节制的；超出常限的；混乱无序的（古旧用法）
definition_en: far greater than is reasonable or normal, especially in strength, quantity, or size
core_image: 一座秤盘上堆着远远超出限度的重物，秤杆被压得翘不起来
scene: 学生事务处抱怨宿舍管理混乱无序。The student office complained about the inordinate conditions in the dormitory.
sceneCN: 这里 inordinate 是「混乱无序的」（第 5 个义项：缺乏秩序、不合规矩）；句意：学生事务处抱怨宿舍管理混乱无序。

pos.zh: 过度的；过分的；无节制的
不合规矩的；混乱无序的（古旧用法）

collocations.zh: 过大的胃口；无节制的欲望

derivatives.zh: 由 inordinate 加 -ly 构成，义为「过度地；格外地」
由 inordinate 加 -ness 构成，义为「过分；无节制」
较少用的名词，按拉丁构词方式形成，义为「失序；混乱」

senses.title: Excessive in amount
senses.definition: more than a reasonable or expected amount, especially of time, money, or effort
senses.definitionCN: 数量上超过合理或预期的限度，尤指时间、金钱或精力
senses.example: The repairs took an inordinate amount of time.
senses.exampleCN: 这次修理花了过多的时间。
senses.why: The in- prefix means not, and ordinatus means set in order, so what is not ordered runs beyond the normal measure.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 表示「不」，ordinatus 表示「按序排好」；没有排好的东西就会超出常理，数量上便漫溢过度。

senses.title: Excessive in feeling
senses.definition: too strong or too great in feeling, pride, or desire
senses.definitionCN: 在情感、骄傲或欲望上过于强烈或过于巨大
senses.example: He showed an inordinate pride in his son.
senses.exampleCN: 他对儿子表现出过分的骄傲。
senses.why: From quantity the word moves to intensity: a feeling that is not kept in order spills past its proper size.
senses.whyCN: 词义从数量转到强度：一种没有被管住的情感溢出它应有的分寸，于是变得过分。

senses.title: Beyond the usual limit
senses.definition: far beyond what is usual or natural, often in a way that is surprising
senses.definitionCN: 远远超出通常或自然的范围，常令人惊讶
senses.example: The cost of the wedding was inordinate for such a small family.
senses.exampleCN: 对这样一个小家庭来说，这场婚礼的花费大得离谱。
senses.why: The old Latin sense of ordered arrangement gives the idea of a proper limit; going past that limit is what inordinate describes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原义「按序排列」暗示存在合理的限度；越过这条限度正是 inordinate 所描述的情形。

senses.title: Uncontrolled in habit
senses.definition: not kept within limits, as of appetite, spending, or drinking
senses.definitionCN: 在胃口、开销或饮酒等方面不受限制
senses.example: Her inordinate appetite for sweets worried the doctor.
senses.exampleCN: 她对甜食过大的胃口让医生担忧。
senses.why: When something is not regulated, appetite and habit grow beyond need; this sense keeps the picture of an overflowing measure.
senses.whyCN: 当事物不受调节时，胃口与习惯便会超出需要；这个义项保留了「量器漫出」的画面。

senses.title: Lacking order, archaic
senses.definition: not kept in order or rule, as of conduct or a place; an older and less common sense
senses.definitionCN: 在行为或场所上缺乏秩序与规矩；较古老、较少用的义项
senses.example: The old chronicle describes the inordinate manners of the court.
senses.exampleCN: 这部旧编年史描述了宫廷里混乱无度的风气。
senses.why: The Latin root ordo means order, so the earliest literal sense is simply out of order; modern English prefers orderly or disorderly for this meaning.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根 ordo 意为秩序，因此最早的字面义就是「失序」；现代英语表达此义时更常用 orderly 或 disorderly。

intro.en: Inordinate comes from Latin inordinatus, meaning not arranged or not set in order, built on in- plus ordo.
intro.cn: inordinate 来自拉丁语 inordinatus（未排列的、无秩序的），由否定前缀 in- 与 ordo（秩序）构成。

items.en: The noun ordo means a row, a rank, or an arrangement.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 ordo 意为一排、一列或一种排列顺序。

items.en: The verb ordinare means to arrange or set in order, giving the participle ordinatus.
items.cn: 动词 ordinare 意为排列、整理，其分词为 ordinatus。

items.en: Inordinatus adds the negative in- to mean not ordered, not arranged.
items.cn: inordinatus 加上否定前缀 in-，意为未排序的、未整理的。

items.en: The word enters English from Latin and Old French with the sense of disorderly.
items.cn: 该词经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，义为「无秩序的」。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the meaning shifts from badly ordered toward excessive and beyond reasonable limits.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，词义从「秩序不良」逐步转向「过度、超出合理限度」。

items.en: Today the everyday sense is an unreasonably large amount, delay, or feeling.
items.cn: 如今日常义项多指数量、拖延或情感上不合理地大。

note.en: Inordinate sits in the order family beside ordain and co-ordinate, and near words for excess.
note.cn: inordinate 属于「秩序」词族，与 ordain、co-ordinate 同源；意义上则靠近各种表示「过度」的词。

entries.definition: the act of ordaining a priest or arranging
entries.definitionCN: 授予圣职；排列

entries.definition: an old rare word for lack of order
entries.definitionCN: 古旧罕用词，义为「失序」

entries.definition: not kept in good order
entries.definitionCN: 无秩序的；混乱的

entries.definition: much more than is reasonable
entries.definitionCN: 过度的；过多的

entries.definition: not fair or sensible
entries.definitionCN: 不合理的；过分的

entries.definition: not kept within sensible limits
entries.definitionCN: 无节制的；过度的

entries.definition: too large or small in relation to something else
entries.definitionCN: 不成比例的

normalIntro.en: Inordinate is order with a not in front: something that refuses to be measured is excessive.
normalIntro.cn: inordinate 是「秩序」前面加了一个「不」：拒绝被衡量的东西，就成了过度。

normal.en: In- plus the Latin root ordo gives the idea of not ordered.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 加拉丁词根 ordo（秩序），就是「没有秩序」。

normal.en: An inordinate amount means far too much of something.
normal.cn: an inordinate amount 表示某物多得出奇。

normal.en: An inordinate delay is a delay that is far longer than fair.
normal.cn: an inordinate delay 是远比合理更长的拖延。

normal.en: The adverb inordinately often pairs with adjectives like expensive or long.
normal.cn: 副词 inordinately 常与 expensive、long 等词搭配。

normal.en: Compare excessive: excessive means simply too much, while inordinate adds the flavour of going wildly past a limit.
normal.cn: 对比 excessive：excessive 只说过多，inordinate 添上「大大越过限度」的色彩。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with weights piled far above the marked limit.
abstract.cn: 想象一台秤，砝码被堆到刻度之上很远。

abstract.en: Imagine a ruler that runs out before the length you must measure.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子在你还没量完就先到头了。

abstract.en: Think of a garden hedge growing wildly past its trim line.
abstract.cn: 想象一道篱笆疯长，远远越过了修剪线。

examples.en: The essay took an inordinate amount of time to finish.
examples.cn: 这篇论文花了过多的时间才完成。

examples.en: Critics complained about the inordinate delay in publishing the report.
examples.cn: 评论者抱怨报告发布的过分拖延。

examples.en: They paid inordinate attention to tiny details rather than the main idea.
examples.cn: 他们对细枝末节投入了过度的注意力，而不是关注主旨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因诺丁内特」——心里嘀咕「因繁多」，东西多到最后，便成了过度。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ ordinare（排列；整理），源自 ordo（秩序、行伍）→ inordinatus（无秩序的）→ 英语 inordinate：不在秩序之内，因而「越过限度」。

sensesIntro.en: Inordinate starts from not ordered and grows into a quantity, intensity, limit, habit, and finally the older sense of disorder.
sensesIntro.cn: inordinate 从「没有次序」出发，依次长成数量过度、情感过分、越过常限、习惯无节制，最后是较古老的「失序」义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale weighted far beyond its marked limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台秤被压到远超刻度的程度。

branches.en: Quantity past the mark is the most common everyday sense.
branches.cn: 数量越过刻度，是最常见的日常义项。

branches.en: Feeling past its proper size is the emotional branch.
branches.cn: 情感超出应有分寸，是情感分支。

branches.en: Going past the usual limit is the general limit branch.
branches.cn: 越过通常限度，是通用限度分支。

branches.en: Both a huge amount and an unruly habit share the overflowing measure.
branches.cn: 数量巨大与习惯放纵都共享同一个「量器漫出」的画面。

branches.en: The old sense of disorder keeps the literal root meaning alive.
branches.cn: 古老的「失序」义项保留着字面词根的含义。

intro.en: Inordinate is built from the English prefix in- and the Latin order root ordo, and it has produced only a few adverbs and nouns.
intro.cn: inordinate 由表示否定的前缀 in- 和拉丁「秩序」词根 ordo 构成，派生出的主要是副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ordo means order or row, and ordinare means to arrange, so inordinatus means put out of order.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ordo 意为秩序、行列，ordinare 意为排列，因此 inordinatus 意为「被弄乱秩序的」。

items.example: The prefix in- negates the root in inordinate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 在 inordinate 中否定词根。

items.example: Ordo is the root of order words.
items.exampleCN: ordo 是 order 一族词的词根。

items.meaning: to arrange, to set in order
items.example: Ordinare supplies the participial stem.
items.exampleCN: ordinare 提供了分词词干。

items.example: Inordinatus is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: inordinatus 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Order and inordinate share the same root.
items.exampleCN: order 与 inordinate 同出一源。

items.example: Ordinance keeps the arranging sense.
items.exampleCN: ordinance 保留了「安排、规定」的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ate closes the adjective inordinate.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 完成了形容词 inordinate。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms inordinately.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 inordinately。

items.example: Inordinately modifies adjectives such as expensive.
items.exampleCN: inordinately 常修饰 expensive 等形容词。

items.example: Inordinateness is rare but regular.
items.exampleCN: inordinateness 较少见但构词规则。

latinEntries.meaning: to arrange, to set in order

definition_zh: 精神失常的；患精神病的；极其愚蠢的；狂热的；极度的（口语强调）
definition_en: seriously mentally ill, or too wild and foolish to be believed
core_image: 一个人头脑里的灯熄灭了，健康那条线整个断掉
scene: 他通宵改方案后做出了一连串极其荒唐的决定。After working all night, he made a string of insane decisions.
sceneCN: 这里 insane 是「极其荒唐、愚蠢到离谱的」（第 3 个义项：愚蠢到不合常理）；句意：他通宵改方案后做出了一连串极其荒唐的决定。

pos.zh: 精神失常的；患精神病的
极度的；狂热的（口语，用于强调）

derivatives.zh: 由 in- 与拉丁语 sanitas 构成，义为「精神失常；疯狂」
由 insane 加 -ly 构成，义为「疯狂地；极其」
由 in- 加 sanitas（健康）构成，指不卫生的；与 insane 共用「健康」类词根

senses.title: Seriously mentally ill
senses.definition: suffering from a serious mental illness, in law and medicine
senses.definitionCN: 在医学与法律上，患有严重精神疾病
senses.example: The man was declared insane and sent to a hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 那名男子被判定精神失常，送进了医院。
senses.why: Latin sanus means sound or healthy, so in-sanus is simply not healthy, and the notion narrows to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sanus 意为健全、健康，in-sanus 就是「不健全」，这个意思后来专注到精神方面。

senses.title: Wild and unreasonable in behaviour
senses.definition: acting in a way that is wildly out of control and hard to explain
senses.definitionCN: 行为举止狂乱失控，难以解释
senses.example: Insane drivers raced through the narrow streets.
senses.exampleCN: 疯狂的司机在窄街上飞驰而过。
senses.why: An unhealthy state of mind can show itself in behaviour, so the word grows from the mind to visible madness.
senses.whyCN: 不健康的心智会表现在行为上，于是词义从「心智」延伸到看得见的疯狂举动。

senses.title: Extremely foolish
senses.definition: so foolish or unreasonable that it seems mad
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢或不合情理到近乎发狂的地步
senses.example: It is insane to spend your whole salary on one pair of shoes.
senses.exampleCN: 把整月工资花在一双鞋上简直荒唐透顶。
senses.why: Everyday speech borrows the medical word: a plan so foolish looks like a mind that has stopped working.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语借用了医学词汇：一个太愚蠢的计划，就像一颗停止正常运转的头脑。

senses.title: Excited and wild
senses.definition: very great, wild, or intense in a way that excites or shocks
senses.definitionCN: 极其巨大、狂放或激烈，令人兴奋或震惊
senses.example: Things went insane near the finish of the race.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛临近结束时场面变得狂热失控。
senses.why: From a mind out of control the word slips to anything that seems to lose control, such as a crowd or a market.
senses.whyCN: 词义从「失控的心灵」滑向任何似乎失去控制的事物，比如人群或市场。

senses.title: Extreme in a casual way
senses.definition: used with nouns or verbs to mean extremely, in informal British and American speech
senses.definitionCN: 非正式英语中与名词或动词连用，强调「极其」
senses.example: The team played at an insane level in the final match.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍在决赛中打出了极其惊人的水平。
senses.why: The idea of madness becomes an amplifier of intensity: whatever is called insane is beyond the ordinary, so it simply means exceedingly.
senses.whyCN: 「疯狂」这一概念被用来放大强度：凡被称作 insane 的都超出常情，久而久之就只剩「极其」。

intro.en: Insane comes from Latin insanus, not sound in mind, built on the negative in- and sanus, healthy.
intro.cn: insane 来自拉丁语 insanus（心智不健全的），由否定前缀 in- 与 sanus（健康的）构成。

items.en: The adjective sanus means sound, healthy, and sane.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 sanus 意为健全的、健康的、清醒的。

items.en: Insanus means not sound in mind, mad, with the negative in- in front.
items.cn: insanus 意为心智不健全的、发狂的，前面加了否定前缀 in-。

items.en: Roman law and medicine use insanus for a legally mad person, with the related noun insania.
items.cn: 罗马法与医学用 insanus 指法律上发狂的人，相关名词为 insania。

items.en: The word enters English from Latin and is soon spelled in its modern form insane.
items.cn: 该词从拉丁语进入英语，拼写很快定型为现代形式 insane。

items.en: Medicine moves to psychiatric vocabulary, and the everyday word turns towards foolish or wildly exciting.
items.cn: 现代医学改用精神病学词汇，日常用语则转向「愚蠢」或「狂热」。

items.en: From about the mid twentieth century the word also works as a loose term for extremely.
items.cn: 大约二十世纪中叶以来，该词还常被当作「极其」的夸张用法。

note.en: Insane belongs to a small sane family and stands near the mad, crazy, and deranged words.
note.cn: insane 属于一个精简的「健全」词族，同时也靠近 mad、crazy、deranged 这一群词。

entries.definitionCN: 心智健全的；明智的

entries.definitionCN: 精神失常；疯狂
