entries.definitionCN: 不卫生的；有害健康的

entries.definition: mentally ill or extremely foolish
entries.definitionCN: 疯狂的；发疯的

entries.definition: informal word for mad or absurd
entries.definitionCN: 疯狂的；荒唐的

entries.definition: an old word for a mad person or a reckless act
entries.definitionCN: 精神失常者；疯狂之举（旧称）

entries.definition: mentally disturbed and out of control
entries.definitionCN: 精神错乱的；失去控制的

normalIntro.en: Insane is sane with a not in front: a mind that is not sound.
normalIntro.cn: insane 就是在 sane（健全）前面加一个「不」：一颗不健全的心。

normal.en: Sane means healthy in mind, and in- turns it into insane.
normal.cn: sane 意为心智健全，加 in- 就成了 insane（精神失常）。

normal.en: Drive someone insane is the usual phrase for making a person mad.
normal.cn: drive someone insane 是「把某人逼疯」的常用说法。

normal.en: The noun is insanity and the adverb is insanely.
normal.cn: 名词是 insanity，副词是 insanely。

normal.en: Insane asylum is an old name for a hospital for the mentally ill.
normal.cn: insane asylum 是精神病院的旧称。

normal.en: In conversation insane often means absurd, as in an insane idea.
normal.cn: 口语中 insane 常指荒唐，如 an insane idea。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp in a head flickering and going dark.
abstract.cn: 想象头脑里的一盏灯忽明忽暗，最后熄灭。

abstract.en: Imagine a road sign twisted so that every arrow points the wrong way.
abstract.cn: 想象一块路牌被扭弯，所有箭头都指着错的方向。

abstract.en: Think of a train speeding past the station because the brakes failed.
abstract.cn: 想象一列火车因刹车失灵而冲过车站。

examples.en: The court found him insane and unfit to stand trial.
examples.cn: 法庭判定他精神失常，不适宜受审。

examples.en: It would be insane to drive in this storm.
examples.cn: 在这种暴风雨里开车简直是疯了。

examples.en: The audience went insane when the singer appeared.
examples.cn: 歌手一出现，观众就陷入狂热。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因塞恩」——心里像被什么东西塞住，理不清了，于是发疯。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ sanus（健全、健康的）→ insanus（心智不健全的）→ 英语 insane，核心义「不健全」，先指心智，再泛指荒唐与狂热。

sensesIntro.en: Insane begins with the medical sense of an unsound mind and widens into wild behaviour, absurd plans, wild excitement, and finally intensifiers.
sensesIntro.cn: insane 从「心智不健全」的医学义出发，扩展到行为失控、计划荒唐、情绪狂热，最后沦为口语中的强调词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a light inside the head that goes out.
core.cn: 核心意象：头脑里那盏灯熄灭了。

branches.en: The medical and legal sense keeps the literal root meaning.
branches.cn: 医学与法律义项保留了字面词根含义。

branches.en: Visible loss of control forms the behavioural branch.
branches.cn: 看得见的失控构成行为分支。

branches.en: A foolish plan is read as a mind that has stopped working.
branches.cn: 愚蠢的计划被读作停止运转的头脑。

branches.en: Absurd and extreme share the idea of going far past the ordinary.
branches.cn: 「荒唐」与「极度」共享「远远超出常情」这一内核。

branches.en: Wild excitement and casual intensifying grow from the same overflow.
branches.cn: 狂热激动与口语强调都源自同一种溢出效应。

intro.en: Insane joins the negative prefix in- to the Latin health root sanus, the same root as sanitary.
intro.cn: insane 把否定前缀 in- 接到拉丁健康词根 sanus 上，与 sanitary 同根。

latinIntro.en: Latin sanus means sound or healthy, while insanus means not sound in mind.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sanus 意为健全、健康，insanus 则指心智不健全。

items.example: The prefix in- negates sanus in insane.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 在 insane 中否定 sanus。

items.example: Sanus is the health root of insane.
items.exampleCN: sanus 是 insane 的健康词根。

items.example: Sanitas lies behind sanity.
items.exampleCN: sanitas 是 sanity 的来源。

items.example: Insanus is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: insanus 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Sane is the positive partner of insane.
items.exampleCN: sane 是 insane 的肯定形式。

items.example: Insanity is the regular noun.
items.exampleCN: insanity 是规则的名词形式。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms insanity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 insanity。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms insanely.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 insanely。

items.example: Insanely pairs with adjectives for intensity.
items.exampleCN: insanely 与形容词搭配表示程度。

items.example: Sanitary shows the same health root in action.
items.exampleCN: sanitary 展示了同一健康词根的用法。

definition_zh: 缺乏自信的；没有安全感的；不牢靠的；不安全的；不稳固的
definition_en: not confident about yourself, or not safe and firmly held
core_image: 一把锁的锁舌没扣紧，门在风中来回晃动，随时会被推开
scene: 刚搬来的邻居总担心门外有动静，夜里睡不安稳。The new neighbor was insecure about her flat and checked the door every night.
sceneCN: 这里 insecure 是「没有安全感的」（第 1 个义项：缺乏自信、内心不安）；句意：刚搬来的邻居对新公寓感到不安全，每晚都要检查门锁。

pos.zh: 缺乏自信的；没有安全感的
不牢靠的；不安全的；有危险的

collocations.zh: 不安全依恋（心理学术语）

derivatives.zh: 由 insecure 加 -ity 构成（-e 变为 -i），义为「不安全感；不安的来源」
由 insecure 加 -ly 构成，义为「不牢靠地；不安地」
与 insecure 相对的肯定形式，义为「安全的；稳固的」

senses.title: Lacking confidence
senses.definition: not confident or certain about yourself, your abilities, or your worth
senses.definitionCN: 对自己、自己的能力或价值缺乏信心或把握
senses.example: She felt insecure among the older students.
senses.exampleCN: 在年长的学生中间，她感到很没有安全感。
senses.why: Latin se- means without and cura means care, so securus means free from care; a person who is not free from anxious care feels insecure.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 se- 意为「免于」，cura 意为「忧虑」，securus 即「无忧」；一个人若不能免于担忧，便是 insecure。

senses.title: Lacking emotional safety
senses.titleCN: 没有安全感的；不踏实的
senses.definition: not feeling safe, accepted, or loved by other people
senses.definitionCN: 在他人那里感到不安全、不被接纳或不被爱
senses.example: The team felt insecure and unsupported after the move.
senses.exampleCN: 搬迁之后，全队都感到缺乏支持、没有安全感。
senses.why: Security in psychology means feeling held by others; the same image of a firm grip turns into emotional attachment.
senses.whyCN: 心理学中的安全感指感到被他人托住；「牢牢握住」这一同一个画面转成情感上的依恋。

senses.title: Not firmly fixed
senses.definition: not firmly fastened or supported, and likely to move or fall
senses.definitionCN: 没有固定牢靠或支撑稳当，容易挪动或倒塌
senses.example: The rope holding the suitcase to the rack was insecure.
senses.exampleCN: 把手提箱绑在行李架上的绳子很不牢靠。
senses.why: The opposite of secure here is physical: a thing that is not held tight is insecure.
senses.whyCN: 这里的反义是物理层面的：没有被牢牢固定的东西就是不牢靠的。

senses.title: Not safe from harm
senses.definition: open to danger, attack, or loss
senses.definitionCN: 暴露于危险、攻击或损失之中
senses.example: A broken window left the whole building insecure at night.
senses.exampleCN: 一扇破掉的窗户让整栋楼夜里都不安全。
senses.why: Once the grip loosens, anything can walk in; the word shifts from poor fastening to real danger.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「扣紧」松动，任何东西都能进来；词义就从「固定不良」转向真正的危险。

senses.title: Unreliable or unstable
senses.definition: unstable and likely to change or fail, as of a job, system, or connection
senses.definitionCN: 不稳定，容易变化或失效，如工作、系统或连接
senses.example: Many graduates take insecure jobs for years.
senses.exampleCN: 许多毕业生多年来一直在做不稳定的工作。
senses.why: The metaphor widens from ropes and locks to things like jobs and data lines: whatever may slip away is insecure.
senses.whyCN: 这一隐喻从绳索、门锁扩展到工作与网络线路：任何可能溜走的东西都叫 insecure。

intro.en: Insecure is formed in English by adding the negative in- to secure, which comes from Latin securus, free from care.
intro.cn: insecure 是在英语内部给 secure 加上否定前缀 in- 构成的；secure 来自拉丁语 securus（无忧的）。

items.en: Cura means care or worry, and se-cura means without care.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cura 意为忧虑、关切，se-cura 则意为「无忧」。

items.en: Securus means free from care or fear, and later safely held.
items.cn: securus 意为无忧无虑，后来又有「安稳可靠」之义。

items.en: Securus passes into Old French as seur, and from there into English as the adjective secure.
items.cn: securus 进入古法语成为 seur，再进入英语成为形容词 secure。

items.en: The English negative prefix in- joins secure, and insecure first describes property that is not safe.
items.cn: 英语的否定前缀 in- 加到 secure 上，insecure 最初形容不牢靠的财物。

items.en: Psychology from the early twentieth century extends the word to personal confidence and attachment.
items.cn: 二十世纪初的心理学把该词扩展到个人自信与依恋关系上。

items.en: Technical use adds insecure connections and insecure systems in computing.
items.cn: 技术领域又增添了「不安全的连接」与「不安全的系统」等用法。

note.en: Insecure shares the cure root with secure and security, and stands near confident and safe words by contrast.
note.cn: insecure 与 secure、security 共享表示「忧虑」的词根，意义上通过对照靠近信心与安全两类词。

entries.definition: safe and firmly held
entries.definitionCN: 安全的；稳固的

entries.definition: a lack of confidence or safety
entries.definitionCN: 不安全感

entries.definition: in an unsafe way
entries.definitionCN: 不牢靠地

entries.definition: safety and protection
entries.definitionCN: 安全；保障

entries.definition: likely to cause harm
entries.definitionCN: 不安全的

entries.definition: not firm and likely to fail
entries.definitionCN: 不稳的；摇晃的

entries.definition: worried about what may happen
entries.definitionCN: 焦虑的；担忧的

entries.definition: likely to change or fall
entries.definitionCN: 不稳定的

normalIntro.en: Insecure is secure with a not in front: the grip of care has loosened.
normalIntro.cn: insecure 是在 secure（安稳）前面加一个「不」：那份安稳已经松动了。

normal.en: Secure means safe and firmly held, and in- reverses it to insecure.
normal.cn: secure 意为安稳牢靠，前缀 in- 把它变成相反的意思。

normal.en: Feel insecure about something is the usual personal pattern.
normal.cn: feel insecure about 某人或某事，是常见的个人用法。

normal.en: Insecurity is the noun and insecurely the adverb.
normal.cn: insecurity 是名词，insecurely 是副词。

normal.en: The same cura root gives security, accurate, and even cure itself.
normal.cn: 同一 cura 词根还构成 security、accurate，甚至 cure 本身。

normal.en: Insecure attachment is a set phrase in psychology for uneasy bonding.
normal.cn: insecure attachment 是心理学里指「不安的依恋」的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture a lock that will not catch and a door swinging in the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锁扣不上，门在风里来回摇晃。

abstract.en: Imagine walking a plank that bends under you with every step.
abstract.cn: 想象你走在一块每踩一步就往下弯的木板上。

abstract.en: Think of a kite whose string is only half tied.
abstract.cn: 想象一只风筝，线只系了一半。

examples.en: He was insecure about his accent in job interviews.
examples.cn: 他在求职面试中对口音很不自信。

examples.en: The ladder looked insecure, so we did not climb it.
examples.cn: 那梯子看起来不牢靠，所以我们没有爬上去。

examples.en: Critics say insecure passwords put users at risk.
examples.cn: 批评者认为不安全的密码让用户面临风险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因缺」——因为「缺」少了安全感，心里就不踏实。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 se-（无、免于）+ cura（忧虑），构成 securus（无忧的）→ 英语 secure → 加否定前缀 in- 构成 insecure：「不能免于忧虑」，既不自信，也不牢靠。

sensesIntro.en: Insecure starts with the loss of inner confidence, moves to emotional safety, then to physical fastening, danger, and finally unreliable systems.
sensesIntro.cn: insecure 先指内心自信缺失，再转到情感上的安全，然后是物理上固定不牢，再扩到危险与不可靠的系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lock that does not catch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把扣不上的锁。

branches.en: Inner self-doubt is the most familiar everyday sense.
branches.cn: 内心的自我怀疑是最常见的日常义项。

branches.en: Emotional safety is the psychological branch.
branches.cn: 情感安全是心理学分支。

branches.en: A loose fixing is the physical branch.
branches.cn: 固定不牢是物理分支。

branches.en: A poor fastening and real danger share one image of exposure.
branches.cn: 固定不牢与真实危险共享「暴露在外」的画面。

branches.en: Danger and unreliable systems both reach the public or technical registers.
branches.cn: 危险与不可靠系统分别连接公共与专业语域。

intro.en: Insecure combines the negative prefix in- with the Latin root cura meaning care, the same root as cure and accurate.
intro.cn: insecure 把否定前缀 in- 与拉丁语词根 cura（忧虑）结合起来，cure、accurate 同出此根。

latinIntro.en: Latin cura means care, and securus, built with se- meaning free from, means without care.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura 意为忧虑，加上表示「免于」的 se- 构成 securus，意为无忧。

items.example: The prefix in- negates secure in insecure.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 在 insecure 中否定 secure。

items.example: Se- in securus means free from care.
items.exampleCN: securus 中的 se- 意为免于忧虑。

items.example: Cura is the root of cure words.
items.exampleCN: cura 是 cure 一族词的词根。

items.example: Securus lies behind secure.
items.exampleCN: securus 是 secure 的来源。

items.example: Secure is the positive partner of insecure.
items.exampleCN: secure 是 insecure 的肯定形式。

items.example: Security is the usual noun.
items.exampleCN: security 是常用的名词。

items.meaning: a lack of confidence or safety
items.example: Insecurity is the noun of insecure.
items.exampleCN: insecurity 是 insecure 的名词形式。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms insecurity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 insecurity。

items.meaning: in an unsafe or unconfident way
items.example: Insecurely modifies verbs like fasten.
items.exampleCN: insecurely 修饰 fasten 等动词。

items.example: Accurate carries the cura root to care.
items.exampleCN: accurate 把 cura 词根带到「用心」。

definition_zh: 阴险的；暗中为害的；暗中进行的；狡猾的
definition_en: spreading or acting in a gradual, quiet way that is hard to notice, and feeling harmless while it causes real harm
core_image: 一条看不见的线从背后慢慢收紧，人还没有察觉
scene: 一种病起初只有轻微的疲倦，多年后才被发现已经伤到内脏。The illness was insidious, creeping forward for years before anyone noticed.
sceneCN: 这里 insidious 是「暗中为害的」（第 2 个义项：缓慢扩散、不易察觉却造成实际伤害）；句意：这种病是阴险的，在无人察觉前已悄悄发展了多年。

pos.zh: 暗中进行的；缓慢而不易察觉的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「阴险地；悄悄地」，强调动作不易察觉
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「阴险；隐匿性」，指暗中为害的性质
与形容词同出拉丁语 insidiae，是罕见的正式动词，义为「设伏谋害」

senses.title: Crafty and treacherous
senses.definition: cleverly treacherous in a way that is meant to trap or harm someone
senses.definitionCN: 狡猾老练、意在设套伤害他人的
senses.example: It was an insidious trick played on a trusting old man.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一个针对一位轻信的老人使出的阴险计谋。
senses.why: The Latin source insidiae means an ambush, so the adjective names a person or plan that lies in hiding and strikes unexpectedly.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头 insidiae 意为「埋伏」，所以这个词形容人或计划像伏兵一样潜伏，然后突然出击。

senses.title: Spreading quietly while causing harm
senses.titleCN: 暗中为害的；悄悄蔓延的
senses.definition: working or spreading slowly and unnoticed, so that the harm grows before it is seen
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢而无声地发挥作用或蔓延，危害在被人看见之前已经滋长
senses.example: The damage to the river was insidious and took a decade to show.
senses.exampleCN: 对这条河的损害是暗中累积的，过了十年才显现出来。
senses.why: From the hidden ambush comes the modern idea of a threat that does not announce itself but quietly gathers force over time.
senses.whyCN: 由隐藏的伏击引申出现代含义：威胁不宣告自己的到来，只是在时间里悄悄积蓄力量。

senses.title: Hard to notice at first
senses.definition: developing so gradually that the first signs are easy to miss
senses.definitionCN: 发展十分缓慢，最初的迹象很容易被忽略
senses.example: Doctors describe the onset of the disease as insidious.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把这种病的起病描述为隐匿性的。
senses.why: If an ambush waits quietly, its early stages leave almost no trace, so the word also names a slow start with faint symptoms.
senses.whyCN: 伏兵会静静地等待，起初几乎不留痕迹，所以这个词也指症状轻微、起步缓慢的病情。

senses.title: Secducing through slow influence
senses.titleCN: 潜移默化的；逐渐侵蚀的
senses.definition: gradually persuading or eroding a mind or habit until it has changed without awareness
senses.definitionCN: 逐步劝说或侵蚀一种思想或习惯，直到其在不自觉中改变
senses.example: Advertising can be an insidious influence on the way children view money.
senses.exampleCN: 广告可能对孩子看待金钱的方式产生潜移默化的影响。
senses.why: A trap closes step by step, so the word also describes pressure that works by small daily steps rather than one open attack.
senses.whyCN: 陷阱是一步一步收拢的，所以这个词也形容那种不靠公开攻击、而靠每天小步子施加的压力。

senses.title: Pleasant on the surface
senses.titleCN: 表面讨喜而内在有害的
senses.definition: looking or sounding pleasant and harmless while hiding a real danger
senses.definitionCN: 看起来或听起来令人愉快、无害，却隐藏着真实危险
senses.example: The app offered an insidious comfort that quietly took over her evenings.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用提供了一种表面讨喜的舒适感，悄悄占满了她的夜晚。
senses.why: An ambush is set on ground that looks safe, so the adjective can describe pleasures and conveniences that conceal their cost.
senses.whyCN: 伏击设在看起来安全的地方，所以这个词也能形容那些掩盖了代价的愉悦与便利。

senses.title: Stealthy in manner
senses.definition: moving or happening in a quiet, secret, almost stealthy way
senses.definitionCN: 以安静、隐秘、近乎鬼祟的方式移动或发生
senses.example: There was an insidious movement in the fog beyond the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 门外雾中有一阵悄无声息的移动。
senses.why: The plain visual core is the ambush party slipping forward unseen, which gives the adjective an openly stealthy shading.
senses.whyCN: 最直观的意象是伏兵在无人看见时悄悄逼近，这给这个词带上了直白的「鬼祟」色彩。

senses.title: Dangerous in small doses
senses.titleCN: 积小成患的；量小危害大的
senses.definition: harmful through many small repeated events, each too small to provoke alarm
senses.definitionCN: 通过大量重复的小事件造成伤害，每一次都小到不会引起警觉
senses.example: Scientists warn of the insidious effects of regular low-level noise.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家警告经常接触低强度噪音会带来积小成患的影响。
senses.why: The harm of a hidden trap is felt only when the trap is sprung, which fits a dose of danger that accumulates until it is serious.
senses.whyCN: 隐藏的陷阱只有在触发时才显出伤害，这正好契合一种危险量小却不断累积直至严重的用法。

senses.title: Unfelt by the person affected
senses.titleCN: 悄然不觉的；无声无息侵蚀的
senses.definition: taking hold of a person or thing without being felt until the effect is already deep
senses.definitionCN: 在不被当事人察觉的情况下占据人或物，直到影响已经很深
senses.example: Old habits form an insidious hold on the mind unless we question them.
senses.exampleCN: 如果不加审视，旧习惯就会在不知不觉中牢牢抓住人的头脑。
senses.why: The sufferer of an ambush never sees the trap, so the word can stress how the harm lands before awareness catches up.
senses.whyCN: 遭到伏击的人总是看不见陷阱，所以这个词可以强调伤害先到、意识后知。

intro.en: Insidious comes from Latin insidiosus, from insidiae, an ambush, which is built on insidere, to sit in or on.
intro.cn: insidious 来自拉丁语 insidiosus，源头是 insidiae（埋伏），它由 insidere（坐进去、伏在……之上）构成。

items.en: Insidiae means a lying in wait, an ambush, or a plot.
items.cn: insidiae 意为潜伏、埋伏或计谋。

items.en: Insidere joins in, on, with sedere, to sit, so the image is crouching in wait.
items.cn: insidere 由表示「在里、在上」的前缀与 sedere（坐）合成，画面是蹲伏着等待。

items.en: Insidiosus adds the adjectival ending to mean full of ambush, crafty, treacherous.
items.cn: insidiosus 加上形容词词尾，表示「充满埋伏的、狡诈的、奸诈的」。

items.en: French insidieux borrows the Latin form and passes it into English writing.
items.cn: 法语 insidieux 借入这一拉丁词形，并把它传入英语书面语。

items.en: English insidious first describes a plot or a disease that advances unnoticed.
items.cn: 英语 insidious 最初形容偷偷推进的计谋或疾病。

items.en: Today it is used most widely for quiet harm that spreads before anyone sees it.
items.cn: 今天它最常用的语境是那种在被人看见前已经蔓延开来的隐形危害。

note.en: Insidious looks and sounds like the insid- family, but its meaning side is close to stealthy and quietly harmful adjectives.
note.cn: insidious 在外形和读音上属于 insid- 词族，而在意义上更靠近「隐秘、暗中为害」一类形容词。

entries.definition: an ambush or a plot in Latin
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语「埋伏；计谋」，是 insidious 的直接源头

entries.definition: a person who belongs to a group and knows its secrets
entries.definitionCN: 内部人士；只是拼写相近，词源不同（insider 由 inside 加 -er 构成，与 insidiae 无关）

entries.definition: the quality of being quietly harmful
entries.definitionCN: 由形容词加 -ness 构成的名词，义为「阴险；隐匿性」

entries.definition: moving with quiet care so as not to be noticed
entries.definitionCN: 鬼鬼祟祟的；悄悄的，侧重动作没有声音

entries.definition: delicate or hard to notice
entries.definitionCN: 微妙的；不易察觉的，本身不含恶意

entries.definition: causing great harm in a gradual, hidden way
entries.definitionCN: 有害的；恶性的，最接近 insidious 的贬义语气

normalIntro.en: Insidious is the ambush adjective: something sits in wait, then shows its harm only when it is too late.
normalIntro.cn: insidious 是「伏击」形容词：某物潜伏在那里，等到为时已晚才露出危害。

normal.en: The Latin insidiae means an ambush, from insidere, to sit in wait.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 insidiae 意为埋伏，来自 insidere（蹲守、伏着）。

normal.en: An insidious disease is one whose first signs are easy to miss.
normal.cn: an insidious disease 指初起征兆容易被忽略的疾病。

normal.en: Doctors use the phrase insidious onset for symptoms that creep in slowly.
normal.cn: 医生用 insidious onset 表示症状慢慢侵入的起病方式。

normal.en: Swap the ending for -ly to get insidiously, the adverb of quiet harm.
normal.cn: 把词尾换成 -ly 就得到副词 insidiously，表示「悄悄地、阴险地」。

normal.en: Compare pernicious: both mean hidden harm, but insidious stresses the slow unnoticed start.
normal.cn: 对比 pernicious：两者都表示隐蔽的危害，但 insidious 更强调缓慢而不被察觉的开始。

abstract.en: Picture a rope placed across a dark stair, waiting for a careless foot.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子横放在昏暗的楼梯上，等着不留意的一只脚。

abstract.en: Imagine mould spreading behind the wallpaper, invisible until the wall is cut open.
abstract.cn: 想象霉斑在墙纸背后蔓延，直到墙被撬开才看见。

abstract.en: Think of a tap dripping behind the wall for years before the beam rots.
abstract.cn: 想象水龙头在墙内滴水多年，直到横梁腐烂。

examples.en: The attack on the village was insidious rather than open.
examples.cn: 对村庄的攻击是暗中进行的，而不是公开的。

examples.en: High blood pressure is often insidious and may give no warning.
examples.cn: 高血压常常是隐袭的，可能不发出任何警告。

examples.en: Insidiously, the habit spread through the whole team.
examples.cn: 这个习惯不知不觉地传遍了整个团队。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因死地而死」——踩进「死地」的埋伏里，就是阴险的坑；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（在……里、在……上）+ sedere（坐）→ insidere（蹲坐守候）→ insidiae（埋伏）→ insidiosus（阴险的）→ 英语 insidious，核心义「藏在暗处等待出击」。

sensesIntro.en: Insidious starts as the adjective of an ambush, then widens to quiet harm, a slow unnoticed onset, and hidden influence.
sensesIntro.cn: insidious 先是「伏击」的形容词，再扩展到暗中为害、缓慢难察的起病，以及潜移默化的影响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hidden line drawing tighter behind a person who does not notice.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条看不见的线在毫不知情的人背后慢慢收紧。

branches.en: The oldest sense is the treacherous ambush itself.
branches.cn: 最早的义项就是埋伏本身带来的奸诈。

branches.en: A trap that waits becomes a threat that spreads unnoticed.
branches.cn: 会等待的陷阱变成了悄悄蔓延的威胁。

branches.en: A silent ambush explains why the first signs stay invisible.
branches.cn: 无声的伏击解释了为什么最初的迹象看不见。

branches.en: A trap on pleasant ground becomes influence that feels comfortable.
branches.cn: 设在宜人之地的陷阱变成了一种令人舒适的操控。

branches.en: Small hidden doses and unnoticed effects both come from the unseen strike.
branches.cn: 隐蔽的小剂量与未被察觉的效果，都源自那次看不见的出手。

intro.en: Insidious is built from the Latin pair in plus sedere, with the abstract noun insidiae between the verb and the adjective.
intro.cn: insidious 由拉丁语 in 与 sedere 这一对成分组成，中间隔着抽象名词 insidiae。

latinIntro.en: Latin insidere means to sit in wait, and insidiae means an ambush or a plot.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 insidere 意为蹲守伏击，insidiae 意为埋伏或计谋。

items.example: The prefix in- in insidere marks the place of waiting.
items.exampleCN: insidere 中的前缀 in- 标出守候的位置。

items.example: Sedere supplies the crouching, still image.
items.exampleCN: sedere 提供蹲坐、静止的画面。

items.meaning: to sit in or on, to lie in wait
items.example: Insidere is the verb behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: insidere 是整个词族背后的动词。

items.example: Insidiae is the noun of attack from hiding.
items.exampleCN: insidiae 是「从隐藏处发动攻击」的名词。

items.meaning: full of, having the nature of
items.example: The suffix -iosus forms insidiosus.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -iosus 构成 insidiosus。

items.example: Insidiosus is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: insidiosus 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ous turns the Latin stem into insidious.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 把拉丁语词干变成 insidious。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb insidiously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成副词 insidiously。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms insidiousness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 insidiousness。

items.meaning: the quality of being quietly harmful
items.example: Insidiousness names the hidden quality itself.
items.exampleCN: insidiousness 指「隐蔽」这一性质本身。

definition_zh: 富有洞察力的；见解深刻的；有见识的
definition_en: showing a clear and deep understanding of what something really means or how it works
core_image: 一个人低头看向水面，看见了别人只看到波纹的深处
scene: 讨论结束后，那位年轻的研究者提出一个尖锐的问题，让所有人重新看待实验数据。Her comment was the most insightful of the evening.
sceneCN: 这里 insightful 是「富有洞察力的」（第 1 个义项：看穿了事物的深层含义）；句意：她的评论是当晚最有洞察力的一条。

pos.zh: 富有洞察力的；见解深刻的
有见识的；能洞悉内情的

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「洞察力；深刻见解」，形容词由它加 -ful 而来
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「有洞见地；深刻地」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「洞察力；见地深刻」

senses.title: Seeing beneath the surface
senses.titleCN: 富有洞察力的；见识深刻的
senses.definition: showing a clear understanding of the underlying truth of something
senses.definitionCN: 显示出对事物底层真相的清晰理解
senses.example: Her essay offered an insightful reading of the novel.
senses.exampleCN: 她的文章对这部小说作出了很有洞见的解读。
senses.why: The base noun insight is sight turned inward, so the adjective praises someone who looks through the surface into the cause.
senses.whyCN: 基础名词 insight 是「向内的看」，所以形容词用来称赞一个人透过表面看到了根源。

senses.title: Perceptive about people
senses.titleCN: 体察入微的；善解人意的
senses.definition: understanding other people and their feelings unusually well
senses.definitionCN: 异常善于理解他人及其感受
senses.example: Her memoir is patient and insightful about grief.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回忆录对悲伤的描写耐心而体察入微。
senses.why: Looking into the inside applies to minds as well as structures, so the adjective also praises emotional perception.
senses.whyCN: 「看向内部」既能用于结构，也能用于人心，所以这个词同样可以用来称赞情感上的敏锐。

senses.title: Clarifying through analysis
senses.titleCN: 分析透彻的；启人心智的
senses.definition: giving a clearer picture of a problem by explaining it well
senses.definitionCN: 通过良好的解释让一个问题呈现出更清晰的面貌
senses.example: The report gives an insightful account of why the scheme failed.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告对计划失败的原因作了透彻的分析。
senses.why: A person with inward sight can make a tangled subject plain, so the adjective also describes clarifying explanations.
senses.whyCN: 能向内看清的人可以把缠绕的问题讲清楚，所以这个词也形容能澄清问题的解释。

senses.title: Shrewd in judgment
senses.definition: judging people or situations with unusual accuracy
senses.definitionCN: 对人或者情势作出异常准确的判断
senses.example: His questions were insightful and made the whole team rethink.
senses.exampleCN: 他的提问很有见地，让整个团队重新思考。
senses.why: Seeing into a matter gives a reliable read on it, which is why questions and judgments can be called insightful.
senses.whyCN: 能看透一件事就能对它作出可靠的解读，因此提问和判断也可以用这个词形容。

senses.title: Valuably original
senses.definition: showing a fresh view that sheds useful light on a familiar topic
senses.definitionCN: 对一个熟悉的话题提出能带来有益启发的新视角
senses.example: The panel gave some insightful responses to a boring question.
senses.exampleCN: 专家组对一个无聊的问题给出了一些见解独到的回应。
senses.why: Inward sight often catches what everyone else missed, so the adjective also marks a comment as usefully fresh.
senses.whyCN: 向内的目光常能抓住别人漏掉的东西，所以这个词也标记一条评论「新颖且有用」。

intro.en: Insightful is the adjective built on insight, an old compound of in and sight, with the adjective ending -ful added in the early twentieth century.
intro.cn: insightful 是由 insight 加形容词词尾 -ful 构成的；insight 是 in 与 sight 的古老复合词，-ful 词尾在二十世纪初才广泛使用。

items.en: Sight comes from Old English siht, the power of seeing.
items.cn: sight 来自古英语 siht，指看的能力。

items.en: The compound insight appears with the sense of an inner sight.
items.cn: 复合词 insight 出现，带有「内在目光」的含义。

items.en: Insight is recorded meaning understanding of the inner nature of things.
items.cn: insight 有记载的用法开始表示「对事物内在本性的理解」。

items.en: Insight gains a technical sense in psychology, as the sudden grasp of a solution.
items.cn: insight 在心理学中获得技术性含义，指突然领悟到解决办法。

items.en: Insightful is formed with the ending -ful, meaning full of insight.
items.cn: insightful 由词尾 -ful 构成，意为「充满洞见的」。

items.en: In current use it is a frequent word in reviews, reports, and academic writing.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，它是书评、报告和学术写作里的高频词。

note.en: Insightful belongs to the sight family, and on the meaning side it sits next to words for sharp understanding.
note.cn: insightful 属于 sight 一词的词族，在意义上则与一批表示「敏锐理解」的词相邻。

entries.definition: a deep understanding of a complex thing
entries.definitionCN: 基础名词，义为「洞察力；深刻见解」

entries.definition: the power or act of seeing
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「视觉；看见」

entries.definition: in a way that shows deep understanding
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，义为「有洞见地」

entries.definition: quick to notice and understand things
entries.definitionCN: 敏锐的；善于觉察的，侧重观察得很快

entries.definition: showing a very clever understanding of a situation
entries.definitionCN: 精明的；机敏的，带有实务判断的味道

entries.definition: very deep or of great seriousness
entries.definitionCN: 深刻的；深远的，侧重深度而非敏锐

normalIntro.en: Insightful is easier once you see the word inside it: in plus sight, a seeing that reaches into things.
normalIntro.cn: 看清里面藏的词就好记了：insightful 等于 in 加 sight，一种一直看进事物内部的视力。

normal.en: Split it as insight plus -ful, meaning full of understanding.
normal.cn: 拆成 insight 加 -ful，意思是「充满洞见的」。

normal.en: The base noun is insight, so insightful only echoes an older idea.
normal.cn: 基础名词是 insight，形容词只是把旧有概念变成了一种描述。

normal.en: The -ful ending usually marks an adjective: careful, helpful, insightful.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ful 通常标记形容词：careful、helpful、insightful 都属这一类。

normal.en: Use it with comment, analysis, or question, all common partners.
normal.cn: 它常与 comment、analysis、question 搭配，这些都是它的常见伙伴。

normal.en: Compare perceptive: perceptive notices more quickly, insightful goes deeper.
normal.cn: 对比 perceptive：perceptive 是更快发现，insightful 则走得更深。

abstract.en: Picture someone leaning over a lake to see the stones below the ripples.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人俯身看向湖里，看清了波纹下面的石头。

abstract.en: Imagine reading a person as easily as a page of text.
abstract.cn: 想象读一个人就像读一页字那样轻松。

abstract.en: Think of a torch beam going through a wall of fog.
abstract.cn: 想象手电的光柱穿过一片大雾。

examples.en: The interview was strangely insightful and left her quiet for a while.
examples.cn: 这次采访出人意料地深刻，让她沉默了一会儿。

examples.en: Few critics have written so insightfully about the painter early years.
examples.cn: 很少有评论家如此富有洞见地写这位画家早年的事。

examples.en: His insight changed how the hospital treated patients.
examples.cn: 他的洞见改变了这家医院治疗病人的方式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因晒图」——晒图晒出真相的人，就是有洞察力的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 in（进入……之中）+ sight（看见，源自古英语 siht）→ insight（看向内部；洞见）→ insight + -ful（充满……的）→ insightful，核心义「看得进内部」。

sensesIntro.en: Insightful grows from inward sight into deep understanding of an issue, of other people, and of a tangled situation.
sensesIntro.cn: insightful 从「向内的目光」出发，长成对问题的深层理解、对他人的体察以及对复杂局势的敏锐判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: looking down through ripples and seeing the stones.
core.cn: 核心意象：透过波纹一直看到水底的石头。

branches.en: The core sense is understanding what lies under the surface.
branches.cn: 核心义项是理解表面之下的东西。

branches.en: Inward sight turns toward feelings and minds.
branches.cn: 向内的目光转向了情绪和人心。

branches.en: Deep understanding makes a complex subject clear.
branches.cn: 深层理解把复杂的话题变得清晰。

branches.en: Sharp judgment is insight turned into decisions.
branches.cn: 敏锐的判断是把洞见转化为决定。

branches.en: A fresh, clarifying view is what makes a remark worthwhile.
branches.cn: 新颖而澄清的视角让一条评论变得可贵。

intro.en: Insightful is transparent: sight plus the locating prefix in, wrapped by the adjective ending -ful.
intro.cn: insightful 的构词一目了然：sight 加表示「在内」的前缀 in，外面再套上形容词词尾 -ful。

latinIntro.en: Both in and sight are older than Latin in this use: sight goes back to Old English siht.
latinIntro.cn: 在这一用法上，in 与 sight 都比拉丁语更古老：sight 可以追溯到古英语 siht。

items.example: The prefix in- turns sight into sight of the inside.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把 sight 变成对内部的看法。

items.example: Siht is the Old English ancestor of sight.
items.exampleCN: siht 是 sight 的古英语祖先。

items.example: Sight keeps the plain visual core.
items.exampleCN: sight 保留了最直白的视觉核心。

items.example: Insight is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: insight 是整个词族的基础。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms careful and helpful.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ful 构成 careful、helpful 这样的词。

items.example: Insightful describes a remark that sees deeply.
items.exampleCN: insightful 形容一条看得深入的评论。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb insightfully.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成副词 insightfully。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms insightfulness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 insightfulness。

items.example: Insightfully marks how an act of understanding is done.
items.exampleCN: insightfully 说明理解这一动作是如何完成的。

items.example: Insightfulness names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: insightfulness 指这种品质本身。

definition_zh: 暗示；含沙射影地说；使逐渐混入；曲意巴结
definition_en: to suggest something unpleasant in an indirect way, or to get yourself into a place or favour slowly and by quiet means
core_image: 一条细线从缝隙里一点点钻进墙内的空隙
scene: 上司没有直说，只在会议结束时笑着问了一句。Are you insinuating that I made a mistake?
sceneCN: 这里 insinuate 是「暗示、含沙射影」（第 1 个义项：用间接方式说出一件令人不快的事）；句意：你是在暗示我犯了个错误吗？

pos.zh: 使悄悄进入；使逐渐混入
曲意巴结；渐渐获取好感

collocations.zh: 使自己悄悄融入；钻营进入

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ion 构成，义为「暗示；含沙射影的话」，也指悄悄混入的行为
现在分词转成形容词，义为「暗示的；曲意讨好的」
由动词加 -ive 构成，义为「带有暗示意味的；会婉转取悦的」

senses.title: To hint at something unpleasant
senses.definition: to suggest something bad or unwelcome in an indirect and often unpleasant way
senses.definitionCN: 以间接、常常令人不快的方式指出某件不好或不受欢迎的事
senses.example: He insinuated that the figures had been changed.
senses.exampleCN: 他暗示那些数字被人改动过。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to wind or push in sideways, so a charge is pushed in at an angle instead of stated straight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「弯曲着、斜着推进去」，所以指责是斜着推进去的，而不是直说的。

senses.title: To slip in slowly through small gaps
senses.definition: to pass slowly into a place or a body through a narrow opening
senses.definitionCN: 通过一条狭窄的通道缓慢地进入某个地方或体内
senses.example: Water insinuated itself between the bricks.
senses.exampleCN: 水悄悄渗进砖缝之间。
senses.why: The literal image of winding in sideways fits fluid or air creeping through a crack.
senses.whyCN: 「弯曲着从侧面进入」的字面意象，正好契合液体或空气顺着裂缝渗进去的情形。

senses.title: To work oneself into favour
senses.titleCN: 曲意巴结；渐渐获取好感
senses.definition: to make your way into a position of trust or favour by gradual, often cunning steps
senses.definitionCN: 以渐进的、往往狡猾的步骤进入被信任或被宠爱的位置
senses.example: She insinuated herself into the director confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 她渐渐取得了主任的信任。
senses.why: A side winding motion describes ambition too: moving around direct paths until a person ends up inside a trusted circle.
senses.whyCN: 「侧向绕行」也描述野心：绕开直接路径，直到人进入了一个被信任的圈子。

senses.title: To plant an idea gradually
senses.definition: to introduce an idea or doubt into a mind slowly and without open argument
senses.definitionCN: 不靠公开争论，把一种想法或怀疑慢慢引入某人的头脑
senses.example: Rumour had insinuated doubt into every neighbour.
senses.exampleCN: 谣言已经悄悄把怀疑植入每个邻居的心里。
senses.why: An indirect hint enters a mind the way water enters a wall, slowly and through unnoticed gaps.
senses.whyCN: 间接的暗示进入头脑的方式，就像水进入墙壁一样，缓慢而经由被忽略的缝隙。

senses.title: To edge in unobtrusively
senses.titleCN: 悄没声地插入；不引人注意地混入
senses.definition: to put yourself or something into a group or conversation without being asked
senses.definitionCN: 未经邀请把自己或某物放进一个群体或谈话之中
senses.example: A new clause had been insinuated into the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 一条新条款被悄悄地插进了合同。
senses.why: The core is entry by a side door, which explains why unannounced additions are called insinuated.
senses.whyCN: 核心是「从侧门进入」，这解释了为什么未经宣告的增补被称为 insinuated。

senses.title: To be flattering and seductive
senses.titleCN: 曲意逢迎的；婉转取悦的
senses.definition: cleverly flattering or charming in a way that wins people over
senses.definitionCN: 以巧妙奉承或讨喜的方式赢得人心
senses.example: His insinuating manner won over even the coldest reviewer.
senses.exampleCN: 他那种婉转逢迎的态度连最冷淡的评论家都赢了过来。
senses.why: To slide into favour smoothly is to smooth the way with charm, which is why the form also describes a flattering manner.
senses.whyCN: 顺利滑进别人好感之中，就是靠魅力把路铺平，所以这个词形也用来形容奉承逢迎的态度。

intro.en: Insinuate comes from the Latin verb insinuare, to wind in or push a way in, and it has carried both a physical and a social sense since the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: insinuate 来自拉丁语动词 insinuare（弯曲着进入、挤进去），从十六世纪起便兼有物理进入与社会交往两层含义。

items.en: Sinus means a curve, a fold, or a hollow, from the image of a bent line.
items.cn: sinus 意为弯曲、褶皱或凹陷，其意象是一条弯折的线。

items.en: Insinuare winds something into a fold, carrying a sense of quiet sideways movement.
items.cn: insinuare 表示把某物绕进褶皱里，带有「无声地侧向移动」的意味。

items.en: The verb also takes a self inserted into another party, the ancestor of the English phrase with oneself.
items.cn: 这个动词也用于「把自己挤进另一方」，即英语中带 oneself 的用法的祖先。

items.en: Insinuate is recorded meaning to creep into a person favour and to suggest indirectly.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语 insinuate 被记录为「爬进某人的好感」和「间接暗示」。

items.en: The word settles into public speech and legal writing as a term for a sly hint.
items.cn: 在十七至十八世纪，这个词作为「狡黠暗示」的用语进入公共演讲和法律文书。

items.en: Today the hinting sense is the most common, and the physical sense is mostly literary.
items.cn: 今天最常用的是「暗示」义，物理上的「渗入」义多保留在文学语言中。

note.en: Insinuate is the verb behind the insinu- family, and its nearest neighbours are verbs for implying and easing a way in.
note.cn: insinuate 是 insinu- 词族的动词，意义上最接近它的是一批表示「暗示」与「悄悄进入」的动词。

entries.definition: hinting or subtly flattering
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词形式，义为「暗示的；曲意逢迎的」

entries.definition: an indirect and unpleasant hint
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，义为「暗示；含沙射影的话」

entries.definition: having a flattering, hinting quality
entries.definitionCN: 由动词加 -ive 构成的形容词，义为「带暗示意味的；会婉转取悦的」

entries.definition: to suggest something without saying it directly
entries.definitionCN: 暗示；含有……的意思，语气中性，最常用

entries.definition: to suggest something slightly and indirectly
entries.definitionCN: 暗示；略微透露，最为轻松日常

entries.definition: an indirect remark, often about something rude or critical
entries.definitionCN: 影射；暗讽，多指带贬义的间接话

normalIntro.en: Insinuate is the verb of the winding-in image: something gets inside by a curve, not by a straight line.
normalIntro.cn: insinuate 是「弯曲着进入」这一意象的动词：某物靠曲线而非直线进入内部。

normal.en: The Latin sinus means a curve or hollow, which is why the word feels crooked.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 sinus 意为弯曲或凹陷，这就是它读起来有点「弯」的原因。

normal.en: Insinuate that is the everyday pattern for a sly hint.
normal.cn: insinuate that 是表达「含沙射影」的日常句型。

normal.en: Insinuate oneself into is the fixed phrase for working your way in.
normal.cn: insinuate oneself into 是「设法钻进某处」的固定搭配。

normal.en: Switch to -ion for the noun insinuation, a hint you can name.
normal.cn: 换成 -ion 得到名词 insinuation，指一条可以被点名的暗讽。

normal.en: Compare imply: imply is neutral, insinuate adds a sting of accusation.
normal.cn: 对比 imply：imply 是中性的，insinuate 则带上了指责的刺。

abstract.en: Picture smoke sliding under a closed door, thread by thread.
abstract.cn: 想象烟从关着的门底一寸一寸地滑进来。

abstract.en: Imagine a guest arriving early and sinking into every corner of the house.
abstract.cn: 想象一个很早到场的客人，一点点渗进屋子的每个角落。

abstract.en: Think of a small worm finding a crack in a stone wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一条小虫子找到了石墙上的裂缝。

examples.en: She did not accuse me, but she insinuated that I had known.
examples.cn: 她没有指控我，却暗示我早就知道。

examples.en: Cold air insinuated itself through the old window frame.
examples.cn: 冷空气从旧窗框的缝隙里悄悄钻了进来。

examples.en: Such an insinuation could damage her professional reputation.
examples.cn: 这样的含沙射影可能损害她的职业声誉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阴私牛艾特」——话里藏着阴私，再层层「委婉地暗示」出来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入……之中）+ sinus（弯曲、凹陷）→ insinuare（弯曲着推进去；设法挤进）→ 英语 insinuate，核心义「顺着弯缝悄悄进入」。

sensesIntro.en: Insinuate keeps one image through all its senses: something enters sideways by a curve, whether through a crack, into a group, or into a mind.
sensesIntro.cn: insinuate 在所有义项中保留同一个意象：某物顺着曲线从侧面进入，无论是穿过裂缝、钻进人群，还是溜进头脑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin line threading itself into a narrow gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条细线把自己穿进狭窄的缝隙。

branches.en: An indirect accusation is the most common sense today.
branches.cn: 间接指责是今天最常用的义项。

branches.en: The physical sense keeps the plain picture of creeping in.
branches.cn: 物理义项保留了「悄悄渗进」这一最直白的画面。

branches.en: Winding your way into favour is the social version of the same curve.
branches.cn: 钻营求宠是同一道曲线在社会交往中的版本。

branches.en: A planted doubt is a hint that has found a crack in the mind.
branches.cn: 被植入的怀疑就是一条找到了头脑裂缝的暗示。

branches.en: An added suggestion and a sly comment both slip in unnoticed.
branches.cn: 额外加入的提议与狡猾的评论，都是不引人注意地溜进去的。

intro.en: Insinuate is a Latin verb built from in plus a sinus stem, and English keeps the same members in its whole family.
intro.cn: insinuate 是由 in 加上 sinus 词干构成的拉丁语动词，英语整个词族都保留了这同一批成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin sinus means a curve or hollow, and insinuare means to wind in or work a way inside.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sinus 意为弯曲或凹陷，insinuare 意为弯曲着进入、设法挤进去。

items.example: The prefix in- sets the direction of entry.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 定下「进入」的方向。

items.meaning: a curve, a fold, a hollow
items.example: Sinus is also the source of the English sinus.
items.exampleCN: sinus 也是英语 sinus（窦；凹处）的来源。

items.meaning: to wind in, to work a way in
items.example: Insinuare is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: insinuare 是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: The ending -ate turns the Latin stem into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 把拉丁语词干变成动词。

items.meaning: to hint or work in indirectly
items.example: Insinuate keeps both the social and the physical sense.
items.exampleCN: insinuate 同时保留社会交往与物理两层含义。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms insinuation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 insinuation。

items.example: The ending -ing gives the participle insinuating.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 给出现在分词 insinuating。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms insinuative.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 insinuative。

items.example: The suffix -tion appears again in insinuation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tion 再次出现在 insinuation 中。

items.example: Insinuation names the hint itself.
items.exampleCN: insinuation 把那条暗示本身命名出来。

definition_zh: 灵感；启示；鼓舞人心的人或事；吸气
definition_en: a sudden good idea, a person or thing that stirs you to create, or the act of breathing in
core_image: 一口气被人吹进胸口，随即冒出一个念头
scene: 深夜画室里，画家盯着空白的画布发呆了很久。A walk along the river at dawn gave the painter fresh inspiration for the main scene.
sceneCN: 这里 inspiration 是「灵感」（第 1 个义项：突然出现的好想法）；句意：黎明时分沿河散步，让画家对主场景有了新的灵感。

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「激励；激发」，与 inspiration 同源
inspiration 加 -al 构成，义为「鼓舞人心的」
inspire 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人振奋的」
inspire 加 -ed 构成，义为「受到启发的；有灵感的」

senses.title: A sudden good idea
senses.definition: a sudden thought or feeling that helps you create or solve something
senses.definitionCN: 帮助你创作或解决问题时突然出现的想法或感受
senses.example: The design came to her in a sudden moment of inspiration.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计在灵光乍现的瞬间来到她脑中。
senses.why: Latin in- plus spirare, to breathe, pictures breath blown in; the ancients saw a thought entering a person like breath.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in-（进入）加 spirare（呼吸），描绘一口气被吹进来；古人把念头入脑视为像呼吸一样从外进入。

senses.title: A person or thing that stirs you
senses.definition: a person, work, or event that makes you want to create or do something new
senses.definitionCN: 使你想要创作或行动的人、作品或事件
senses.example: Her grandmother was the inspiration behind the whole novel.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖母是整部小说的灵感来源。
senses.why: If a thought enters from outside, the giver of that thought is the source, so the word also names the inspiring person or thing.
senses.whyCN: 既然念头是从外部进入的，那个把念头送来的人或物就是源头，于是这个词也指给人灵感的人或事。

senses.title: Divine prompting
senses.definition: the belief that an idea or a sacred text comes directly from God
senses.definitionCN: 认为某个想法或宗教经文直接来自神的说法
senses.example: Some poets claimed that their verses came from divine inspiration.
senses.exampleCN: 有些诗人声称自己的诗句来自神的启示。
senses.why: When the breacher is God rather than nature, the entering breath becomes revelation, which keeps the oldest layer of the word.
senses.whyCN: 当吹气的一方是神而不是自然时，进入的气息就变成启示，这保留了这个词最古老的一层意思。

senses.title: A sudden urge
senses.definition: a sudden strong feeling that pushes you to act, often not planned
senses.definitionCN: 突然出现、推着你行动的强烈感觉，往往不在计划之内
senses.example: On an impulse of inspiration, he quit his job that same afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 凭着突如其来的冲动，他当天下午就辞了职。
senses.why: The breath image is also the root of impulse and instigate, so inspiration can name the inward push to act at once.
senses.whyCN: 「吹气」意象也是 impulse（冲动）与 instigate（唆使）的词根，因此 inspiration 也可以指把那一下推力放进人心里。

senses.title: The act of breathing in
senses.definition: the physical act of drawing air into the lungs
senses.definitionCN: 把空气吸入肺部的生理动作
senses.example: Yoga teaches a slow inspiration followed by a long, even breath out.
senses.exampleCN: 瑜伽练习先缓缓吸气，再平稳地长呼气。
senses.why: The medical sense keeps the plain Latin meaning of spirare, to breathe, with the prefix in- meaning into.
senses.whyCN: 医学义保留了 spirare（呼吸）最朴素的意思，配上表示「进入」的前缀 in-，就是「吸进去」。

senses.title: The moment of creation
senses.definition: the event or experience from which a work of art or an invention develops
senses.definitionCN: 一部艺术作品或一项发明由此发展起来的事件或经历
senses.example: His travels in Morocco became the inspiration for a whole collection of paintings.
senses.exampleCN: 他的摩洛哥之旅成了整套画作的创作源泉。
senses.why: A single entering thought can grow into a long project, so the word also marks the starting point that later work follows.
senses.whyCN: 一个进入脑海的念头可以长成一整个项目，所以这个词也指后来作品所追随的起点。

intro.en: Inspiration goes back to Latin inspirare, to breathe into, built from in- plus spirare, to breathe. English took it through French in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: inspiration 可追溯到拉丁语 inspirare（向里面吹气），由 in- 与 spirare（呼吸）构成；英语一般认为经由法语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: spirare means to breathe or blow, as in spiritus, breath.
items.cn: spirare 意为呼吸、吹气，同族词 spiritus 意为气息。

items.en: inspirare means to breathe into, first used of God breathing life or knowledge into a mind.
items.cn: inspirare 意为向里面吹气，最初用于神把生命或知识吹进人的心灵。

items.en: The church text says God breathed the breath of life into man, an image that fixed the mental sense.
items.cn: 教会经文说神把生气吹进人的鼻孔，这个画面固定了「吹进心里」的心理义。

items.en: Old French inspiration carried the noun towards English with the sense of a prompting entering the mind.
items.cn: 古法语 inspiration 把名词带向英语，义为进入心灵的启示。

items.en: English first uses inspiration of a divine influence and of breathing in.
items.cn: 英语最早记录中 inspiration 既指神圣的影响，也指吸气。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the word also names a person or thing that sparks an artist, now its most common sense.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，这个词也指激起艺术家创作的人或物，今日这已成为最常用的义项。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on the Latin breathing root; the second gathers near ideas such as idea, motivation, and stimulus.
note.cn: 第一组收以拉丁「呼吸」词根构成的词；第二组收近义概念，如想法、动机与刺激。

entries.definition: to give someone the desire or idea to do something
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「激励；激发」，与 inspiration 同根

entries.definition: giving people the energy or ideas to do great things
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「鼓舞人心的」

entries.definition: the part of a person thought of as breath or soul
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「精神；灵魂」，与 spirare 同根

entries.definition: to breathe, especially in the technical or medical sense
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「呼吸」，用于技术或医学语境

entries.definition: a thought or plan formed in the mind
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「想法；主意」，泛指任何念头

entries.definition: the reason and energy that push a person to act
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「动机；积极性」，强调推动力

entries.definition: something that causes activity or a reaction
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「刺激物；促进因素」

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks work from the Latin breathing root and the main collocations; the abstract hooks picture breath entering and a spark catching.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点从拉丁「呼吸」词根与主要搭配出发；抽象记忆点想象一口气进入身体、一点火星被吹燃。

normal.en: spirare means to breathe, so inspiration is literally a breath breathed in.
normal.cn: spirare 意为呼吸，所以 inspiration 字面上就是被吸进去的一口气。

normal.en: Draw inspiration from is the key collocation for artists and writers.
normal.cn: draw inspiration from 是艺术家和作家最常用的搭配。

normal.en: The verb is inspire and the adjective is inspirational.
normal.cn: 动词是 inspire，形容词是 inspirational。

normal.en: A flash of inspiration is a sudden short moment of good ideas.
normal.cn: a flash of inspiration 指灵光一闪的短暂时刻。

normal.en: The word also means a person: she is an inspiration to us all.
normal.cn: 这个词也可指人：她是我们所有人的榜样与激励。

abstract.en: Picture a warm breath arriving at the back of your skull.
abstract.cn: 想象一口温热的气息抵达后脑。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny spark falling into dry paper and catching fire.
abstract.cn: 想象一点火星落进干纸里烧起来。

abstract.en: Picture a door opening in a dark room and letting in a beam of light.
abstract.cn: 想象暗室里一扇门打开，透进一束光。

examples.en: She often finds inspiration in ordinary street scenes.
examples.cn: 她常从普通的街景中找到灵感。

examples.en: The old teacher was an inspiration to several generations of students.
examples.cn: 这位老教师激励了好几代学生。

examples.en: After weeks of frustration, a sudden inspiration solved the problem.
examples.cn: 经过数周的苦恼，灵光一闪解决了问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「英斯匹瑞申」——别人把一口「气」吹进你心里，你就突然有了灵感；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 spirare（呼吸、吹气）加前缀 in-（进入）→ inspirare（吹进去）→ 名词 inspiratio → 英语 inspiration；核心义「一口气被吹进心里」。

sensesIntro.en: Inspiration starts as a thought breathed into the mind, moves to the people and works that supply such thoughts, then to revelation, sudden urges, and finally to the plain act of breathing in.
sensesIntro.cn: inspiration 起初指吹进心里的念头，再指提供这种念头的人与物，又引申为神启与突生的冲动，最后回到「吸气」这一本义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a breath blown into the chest, bringing a thought with it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一口气被吹进胸口，连同念头一同进来。

branches.en: The mental sense is the everyday one: a sudden good idea.
branches.cn: 心理义项是日常用法：突然出现的好想法。

branches.en: The giver of the breath becomes a person or work that inspires.
branches.cn: 吹气的一方转而成为给人启发的人或作品。

branches.en: A divine source turns the breath into revelation.
branches.cn: 源头若是神，吹进的气息就成了启示。

branches.en: An idea that arrives at once can become a strong urge to act.
branches.cn: 即刻到来的念头可以变成强烈的行动冲动。

branches.en: The physical breath and the creative spark keep the same root sense.
branches.cn: 生理的吸气与创作的契机共享同一个词根义。

intro.cn: inspiration 由拉丁语前缀 in- 与表示呼吸的词根 spir- 构成，英语词尾再把它变成形容词与动词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare means to breathe or blow; its family includes spiritus, breath, and inspirare, to breathe into.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spirare 意为呼吸、吹气，同族词包括 spiritus（气息）与 inspirare（吹进去）。

definition_zh: 瞬时的；即刻发生的；同时的
definition_en: happening at once, with no noticeable delay between cause and effect
core_image: 按下的瞬间，灯已经亮了
scene: 摄影师按下快门，闪光灯几乎在同一瞬间亮起。The camera records an instantaneous flash, so no frame is lost.
sceneCN: 这里 instantaneous 是「瞬时的」（第 1 个义项：几乎没有任何可察觉的延迟）；句意：相机记录到瞬时的闪光，因此没有错过任何一帧。

derivatives.zh: instantaneous 去 -eous 加 -ly 构成，义为「瞬时地」
加 -ness 构成，义为「瞬时性」
基础名词，义为「瞬间」，派生词与它共用同一个词根
instant 加 -ly 构成，义为「立刻」，与 instantaneous 近义

senses.title: Happening at once
senses.definition: happening without any delay that could be noticed
senses.definitionCN: 在几乎无法察觉的延迟内发生
senses.example: The new software gives an almost instantaneous reply to each click.
senses.exampleCN: 新软件对每次点击几乎都会立即回应。
senses.why: Latin in- plus a form of stare, to stand, pictures something standing right in front of you; nothing lies between now and the event.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 加 stare（站立）的派生形，描绘某物就立在眼前；此刻与事件之间没有任何停顿。

senses.title: Following a cause with no gap
senses.definition: produced by an action so quickly that cause and effect seem to coincide
senses.definitionCN: 由某个动作极快产生，快到原因与结果仿佛重合
senses.example: The drug had an instantaneous effect on the patient and the pain simply stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药对病人有立竿见影的效果，疼痛立刻止住了。
senses.why: The image of the thing already standing before you suits any reaction, so the word marks an effect that arrives with its cause.
senses.whyCN: 「东西已立在眼前」的画面同样适用于任何反应，因此这个词标记与原因一同到达的结果。

senses.title: Occurring in the same instant
senses.titleCN: 同时发生的；同一时刻的
senses.definition: taking place at exactly the same moment, viewed as one shared instant
senses.definitionCN: 在同一时刻发生，可视为共处一个瞬间
senses.example: In a still photograph we see the painting and the smile as one instantaneous whole.
senses.exampleCN: 在一张静物照片里，我们看到绘画与微笑同处一个瞬间的整体。
senses.why: Since an instant has no length, two things inside it cannot be ordered, so the word also names events that share one moment.
senses.whyCN: 既然瞬间没有长度，落在其中的两件事就无法分先后，因此这个词也指共享同一时刻的事件。

senses.title: Measured in an instant
senses.definition: relating to a moment so short that a value is read at one point of time
senses.definitionCN: 指短到只在一个时间点读取数值的时刻
senses.example: Engineers track the instantaneous speed of the wheel, not just its average.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师追踪车轮的瞬时速度，而不只是平均速度。
senses.why: When scientists stop the clock to read a single point, the everyday speed sense turns into a technical term.
senses.whyCN: 当科学家把时钟停在某一点来读数时，日常的「快」义就变成了技术术语。

senses.title: Pressing on the mind
senses.definition: pressing and impossible to ignore, as if standing over a person
senses.definitionCN: 紧迫、无法忽视，仿佛就立在某人跟前
senses.example: The chairman called the instantaneous danger to the whole harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 主席提醒大家港口正面临迫在眉睫的危险。
senses.why: Something that stands in front of you demands attention, so the same posture of stare also yields the idea of urgency.
senses.whyCN: 立在眼前的东西会强求注意，因此 stare 的同一个姿态也引申出了紧迫感。

intro.en: Instantaneous is a learned English formation from the Medieval Latin adjective instantaneus, built on instans, the participle of instare, to stand on or press upon.
intro.cn: instantaneous 是由中世纪拉丁语形容词 instantaneus 仿造的书面英语词，源自 instans（instare 的分词，意为立在……之上、逼近）。

items.en: stare means to stand; with the prefix in- it gives instare, to stand upon, to press, to be near.
items.cn: stare 意为站立；加前缀 in- 构成 instare，意为立于其上、逼近、紧迫。

items.en: The participle instans names what is standing before you, that is, the present moment.
items.cn: 分词 instans 指立在眼前的东西，也就是当下这一刻。

items.en: Instantaneus is recorded in medieval usage and is the model for the English adjective; its exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: instantaneus 见于中世纪用法，是英语形容词的模板；其确切首见年代存疑。

items.en: The learned adjective enters English in the middle of the seventeenth century, first in scientific writing.
items.cn: 这个书面形容词在十七世纪中叶进入英语，最初用于科学写作。

items.en: It spreads from physics into everyday speech, where it describes a reaction with no perceptible gap.
items.cn: 它从物理领域进入日常语言，用来描述没有可察觉间隔的反应。

items.en: Today it mainly describes speed in technology and science, and often takes the adverb almost.
items.cn: 今天它主要用于描述科技与科学里的速度，并常与副词 almost 连用。

note.en: The first group gathers the instant family and its close spellings; the second gathers adjectives of speed, each with a different strength.
note.cn: 第一组收 instant 词族及其形近词；第二组收表示速度的形容词，各自的强度不同。

entries.definition: a very short moment, or happening at once
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「瞬间」，也作形容词表示「立即的」，与 instantaneous 同根

entries.definition: at once, without delay
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「立刻」

entries.definition: in a way that takes no noticeable time at all
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「瞬时地」，比 instantly 更强调没有间隔

entries.definition: done from a natural inner impulse, not planned; it is only similar in spelling and has a different root
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「自发的、自然的」；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: happening right now, without anything in between
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「立即的；直接的」，强调中间没有隔层

entries.definition: happening or ready at the exact moment of use
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「速食的；即刻的」，如 instant coffee

entries.definition: done quickly and without delay, often praising a person
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「迅速的；及时的」，多用于赞许一个人的行动

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the stand root and the adverb ending; the abstract hooks all show two events arriving together.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点借助「站立」词根与副词词尾；抽象记忆点都让两个事件同时到达。

normal.en: stare means to stand, so instant means standing right here and now.
normal.cn: stare 意为站立，所以 instant 就是「就立在此刻」。

normal.en: The adverb is instantaneously, always written with -ly.
normal.cn: 副词是 instantaneously，结尾一定带 -ly。

normal.en: Almost instantaneous is the most common phrase, because real delays are never zero.
normal.cn: almost instantaneous 是最常见的说法，因为真实的延迟从来不是零。

normal.en: Compare instant, which is shorter and less formal than instantaneous.
normal.cn: 对比 instant：它更短、更口语，instantaneous 更书面。

normal.en: The noun instant means a point of time, not a length of time.
normal.cn: 名词 instant 指一个时间点，而不是一段时间。

abstract.en: Picture a light coming on in the same frame as the finger pressing the switch.
abstract.cn: 想象手指按下开关与灯亮起在同一帧里。

abstract.en: Picture two droplets hitting a pond at exactly the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两滴水在同一瞬间落进池塘。

abstract.en: Picture a camera freezing a splash in mid air.
abstract.cn: 想象相机把溅起的水花定格在半空。

examples.en: The explosion was instantaneous and almost silent.
examples.cn: 爆炸瞬间发生，几乎没有声音。

examples.en: Modern phone networks give users near instantaneous access to information.
examples.cn: 现代电话网络让用户几乎瞬间就能获取信息。

examples.en: Scientists measure the instantaneous speed of the particles.
examples.cn: 科学家测量粒子的瞬时速度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一瞬时太你饿死」——一瞬间短得夸张，只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 stare（站立）加 in- 构成 instare（立于其上、逼近）→ instans（当下的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 instantaneus → 英语 instantaneous；核心义「就立在此刻眼前」。

sensesIntro.en: Instantaneous begins with the thing standing right before you, passes on to an effect with no gap after its cause, then to events sharing one moment, to readings at a single point of time, and to danger standing close by.
sensesIntro.cn: instantaneous 先指「就立在眼前」，再指原因之后没有间隔的结果，继而指共享同一时刻的事件、单点时刻的测量，最后指逼近的危险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the switch is pressed and the light is already on.
core.cn: 核心意象：按下开关，灯已经亮了。

branches.en: The basic sense is an event with no perceptible delay.
branches.cn: 基本义项是没有可察觉延迟的事件。

branches.en: An effect that arrives with its cause is the causal sense.
branches.cn: 与原因一同到达的结果是因果义项。

branches.en: Events inside one instant cannot be ordered, hence the same-moment sense.
branches.cn: 同处一个瞬间的事件无法排序，于是有了同时义。

branches.en: Technology and science read speed at a single point in time.
branches.cn: 科技与科学在单一时间点上读取速度。

branches.en: An instant that will not wait becomes a pressing danger.
branches.cn: 一刻也不能等的瞬间就变成了紧迫的危险。

intro.en: Instantaneous is built from the prefix in-, the stand root st-, and the learned ending -aneous, with the adverb -ly and the noun -ness added in English.
intro.cn: instantaneous 由前缀 in-、词根 st-（站立）与书面词尾 -aneous 构成，英语里再加 -ly 与 -ness 构成副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare means to stand; instans and instantaneus carry the idea of standing on, pressing, and being present.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stare 意为站立；instans 与 instantaneus 带着「立其上、逼近、临在」之义。

definition_zh: 煽动；唆使；挑起；发起
definition_en: to urge someone on to do something, often something wrong, or to set an action in motion
core_image: 一只手从背后猛推一把，把人推向争执
scene: 班级群里有人悄悄联系几个同学，打算第二天一起去堵住另一位同学。A loud group instigated a fight outside the school gate at noon.
sceneCN: 这里 instigate 是「煽动、挑起」（第 1 个义项：煽动某种坏行为）；句意：中午一伙吵闹的人在学校门口挑起了一场斗殴。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ion 构成，义为「煽动；发起」
加 -or 构成，义为「煽动者；发起者」
加 -ive 构成，义为「煽动性的」
加 -ing 构成，义为「煽动性的；促成某事的」

senses.title: Urge someone to do wrong
senses.definition: to urge a person or group on to do something harmful or unlawful
senses.definitionCN: 鼓动某人或某群体去做有害或违法的事
senses.example: Two older boys instigated the fight in the playground.
senses.exampleCN: 两个较大的男孩挑起了操场上那场斗殴。
senses.why: Latin in- plus a root of sharp poking means to prick on; disapproval is already inside the image of a prod with a spike.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 加表示「用尖物戳」的词根，意为「用尖物往前戳」；「往前戳」的画面本身就带着不赞许的色彩。

senses.title: Set an action in motion
senses.definition: to start an activity or campaign, often as the first real cause of a chain of events
senses.definitionCN: 发动某项活动或运动，往往是事件链条上的第一个实际原因
senses.example: The students instigated a campaign against single-use plastic on campus.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们在校园里发起了一场反对一次性塑料的运动。
senses.why: The prodding image also fits any push that starts others moving, so the verb covers launching an action rather than only stirring trouble.
senses.whyCN: 「戳一下让它动」的画面同样适用于任何推动他人行动的情形，因此这个词也能指发动行动，而不只是挑事。

senses.title: Start an official process
senses.definition: to formally begin legal, disciplinary, or official proceedings
senses.definitionCN: 正式启动法律、纪律或官方的程序
senses.example: The company instigated legal proceedings against the former manager.
senses.exampleCN: 公司对前经理提起了法律诉讼。
senses.why: A formal process begins when one person prods it into existence, so the everyday push extends to the filing of papers.
senses.whyCN: 正式程序总要有一个人推动才能开启，于是日常的「推一把」延伸到了递交文件、启动程序。

senses.title: Stir up trouble indirectly
senses.titleCN: 暗中挑动；策划（使他人行动）
senses.definition: to cause trouble through others, especially by secrecy or persuasive words
senses.definitionCN: 通过他人制造麻烦，尤指暗中进行或靠言语说服
senses.example: The protests were instigated by a small group working in secret.
senses.exampleCN: 这些抗议是由一小群暗中行动的人煽动起来的。
senses.why: A poke from behind is felt but the poker is unseen, which is why the verb often implies a hidden hand at work.
senses.whyCN: 背后戳一下，能感觉到却看不见那只手，这就是这个词常含「幕后有人操纵」意味的原因。

senses.title: Spark a positive change
senses.definition: to be the person or cause that sets a good change or reform going
senses.definitionCN: 成为推动良好变化或改革的那个人或那个原因
senses.example: Her report instigated a complete reform of the school timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 她的报告促成了学校课表的全面改革。
senses.why: The same push can be aimed at good ends; once English widened the verb, it also came to name the first mover of a reform.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「推」的动作也可以朝向好的目标；英语把用法拓宽后，这个词便也指改革的第一推动者。

senses.title: Act as the prompt for a process
senses.definition: to trigger a natural, mechanical, or social process that then runs on its own
senses.definitionCN: 触发一个随后会自行运转的自然、机械或社会过程
senses.example: A single warm winter instigated the early flowering of the cherry trees.
senses.exampleCN: 一个暖冬诱发了樱花的提早开放。
senses.why: A prod only has to start the movement; after that the process carries itself, so the verb also names the first trigger of a chain.
senses.whyCN: 戳一下只需让事物动起来，其后过程会自行继续，因此这个词也指一连串变化的最初触发点。

intro.en: Instigate comes from Latin instigare, to prick on or incite, with in- plus a root connected to the idea of poking with a sharp point. English borrowed the verb in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: instigate 来自拉丁语 instigare（用尖物戳、煽动），由 in- 加一个与「用尖尖的东西戳」相关的词根构成；英语在十六世纪借入这个动词。

items.en: instigare means to prick on, to stimulate, and also to hunt down; the source of its second element is debated.
items.cn: instigare 意为往前戳、刺激，也有追逼之义；其第二部分的确切来源学界仍有争议。

items.en: Some connect the root with a verb meaning to prick or stick, such as the ancestor of stigmatize, but this is a hypothesis, not a certainty.
items.cn: 有说法把这个词根与表示「刺、扎」的动词（例如 stigmatize 的祖先）联系起来，但这只是假说，并非定论。

items.en: The noun instigatio names the act of urging someone on, and the root sense of a poke remains strong.
items.cn: 名词 instigatio 指鼓动他人的行为，「戳一下」的词根义仍然很强。

items.en: English borrows the verb in the 1540s, first in the sense of urging someone to an action.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪四十年代借入这个动词，最初义为鼓动某人采取行动。

items.en: In modern use the sense widens to starting campaigns, proceedings, and processes, not only stirring up trouble.
items.cn: 到近现代用法中，词义扩展到发起运动、启动程序与促成过程，不再只限于挑起麻烦。

items.en: Today the verb is mostly formal and often carries a tone of blame, especially in reports of violence or unrest.
items.cn: 今天这个词偏正式，常带责备语气，尤见于对暴力或骚乱的报道。

note.en: The first group gathers the in- words and near spellings; the second gathers verbs of pushing people to act, from the mild to the criminal.
note.cn: 第一组收以 in- 开头的词与形近词；第二组收推人行动的动词，从温和到犯罪的程度。

entries.definition: a person who urges others to cause trouble
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「煽动者；发起者」

entries.definition: the act of urging someone on or starting something
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「煽动；挑起」

entries.definition: to put an idea or feeling into a mind very gradually; it shares the prefix in- but not the poking root
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「逐渐灌输」，与 instigate 共用前缀 in-，但词根不同

entries.definition: to look into a matter carefully; it is only similar in spelling and has a different root
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「调查」；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to stir up public anger or violent action
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「煽动」，多指激起公众愤怒或暴行

entries.definition: to make someone angry on purpose or to bring about a reaction
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「激怒；引起」

entries.definition: to strongly encourage someone to act, with no hint of wrong
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「力劝；敦促」，本身不含坏的意味

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the poking root and the criminal collocations; the abstract hooks picture a hidden poke that sets things moving.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点借助「戳」的词根与犯罪类搭配；抽象记忆点想象一只看不见的手戳一下让事情动起来。

normal.en: The in- prefix plus a poking root gives the sense of being prodded forward.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 加「戳」的词根，给出了被人往前戳着走的感觉。

normal.en: Instigate a strike and instigate violence are the typical criminal collocations.
normal.cn: instigate a strike 与 instigate violence 是典型的犯罪类搭配。

normal.en: The noun is instigation and the person is an instigator.
normal.cn: 名词是 instigation，那个人则是 instigator。

normal.en: Compare incite: incite is close, while instigate can also mean simply to start something.
normal.cn: 对比 incite：两者很接近，但 instigate 还可单纯指「发起」。

normal.en: Instigate takes a person or an event as its object, never a machine.
normal.cn: instigate 的宾语是某人或某个事件，从不接机器。

abstract.en: Picture a finger in your back pushing you into an argument.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指顶着你的后背，把你推进一场争吵。

abstract.en: Picture a stone pushed off a cliff that starts a small landslide.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头被推下悬崖，引发一场小塌方。

abstract.en: Picture a hidden hand lighting a long fuse.
abstract.cn: 想象一只藏起来的手点亮了一根长长的引线。

examples.en: He was blamed for instigating the violence in the streets.
examples.cn: 他被指责煽动了街头的暴力事件。

examples.en: A single report instigated a full review of the safety rules.
examples.cn: 一份报告便促成了对安全规则的全面审查。

examples.en: Several officers were accused of instigating the riot.
examples.cn: 几名警员被指控挑起了那场骚乱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬是踢给他」——硬是踢给别人、让他去做，就是煽动；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（向前）+ stigare（用尖物戳，确切来源有争议）→ instigare（戳着往前、煽动）→ 英语 instigate；核心义「从后面戳一下，把人推向某事」。

sensesIntro.en: Instigate begins with urging people to do wrong, widens to starting actions, official proceedings, hidden agitation, positive reform, and finally to any first trigger of a process.
sensesIntro.cn: instigate 先用鼓动他人做坏事的义项，扩展到发起行动、启动程序、暗中挑动、促成好的改革，最后指任何过程的最初触发点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger in the back pushing a person into a quarrel.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指顶着后背，把人推向前方的争执。

branches.en: The core sense is urging someone towards harm.
branches.cn: 核心义项是鼓动他人去做有害的事。

branches.en: Starting an action or an official process keeps only the push towards motion.
branches.cn: 发起行动或启动程序，只保留了「推动前进」这一层。

branches.en: The hidden hand of the poker yields the sense of secret agitation.
branches.cn: 「戳的手看不见」带来暗中挑动的义项。

branches.en: A push towards good ends makes the verb neutral in tone.
branches.cn: 把推力朝向好的目标，这个词的语气就变得中性。

branches.en: Any first cause that sets a process going shares the same trigger image.
branches.cn: 任何启动过程的最初原因，都共享同一个触发意象。

intro.en: Instigate is built from the prefix in- and a poking root stig-, with English endings adding noun, adjective, and agent forms.
intro.cn: instigate 由前缀 in- 与表示「戳」的词根 stig- 构成，英语词尾再加出名词、形容词与施动者形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin instigare means to prick on or incite; the first element in- is clear, while the second element has more than one proposed origin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 instigare 意为往前戳、煽动；第一部分 in- 很明确，第二部分则有不止一种来源假设。

definition_zh: 起重要作用的；有助益的；乐器的；器乐的；仪器（测量）的；（语法）工具格的
definition_en: helping to cause something to happen, or relating to musical instruments, measuring devices, or the grammatical instrumental case
core_image: 一只看不见的手握着一件工具，把它伸进事情里，事情因此被推动起来
scene: 一场筹款晚会上，主持人在台上特别感谢了几位关键人物。The young doctor was instrumental in setting up the village clinic.
sceneCN: 这里 instrumental 是「起关键作用的」（第 1 个义项：对某事的成功起重要作用）；句意：那位年轻的医生在建立村诊所一事中起了关键作用。

pos.zh: 形容词：起重要作用的；有助益的
形容词：仪器的；用仪器测量的

collocations.zh: 在做某事上起了推动作用
关键作用；推动性的角色
工具格（语法中的格范畴）

derivatives.zh: 由 instrumental 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「中介作用；工具性；手段」
由 instrumental 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「作为手段地；借助工具地」
由 instrumental 加表示人的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「器乐演奏者；工具主义者」
由 instrument 加 -ation 构成，与 instrumental 同族，义为「配器法；仪器配置；测量装置」

senses.title: Playing a key part in bringing something about
senses.definition: having an important effect in making something happen or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的发生或成功起重要作用
senses.example: She was instrumental in getting the new library built.
senses.exampleCN: 她在促成新图书馆建成一事上起了关键作用。
senses.why: An instrumentum was a tool used to get work done, so a person described as instrumental is like that tool in someone else hands: the result comes through them.
senses.whyCN: instrumentum 原来指干活用的工具，所以被称为 instrumental 的人就像别人手里的一件工具：结果是通过他实现的。

senses.title: Relating to musical instruments
senses.definition: performed by or written for musical instruments rather than voices
senses.definitionCN: 由乐器演奏、为乐器所写，而非用人声演唱的
senses.example: The album includes twelve instrumental tracks and two vocals.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑包含十二首器乐曲和两首带人声的歌。
senses.why: A musical instrument is literally the tool of a musician, so music made with those tools rather than the voice is instrumental music.
senses.whyCN: 乐器本来就叫乐器，也就是乐手的工具；用这些工具而非人声演奏的音乐，自然就是 instrumental music。

senses.title: Relating to instruments used for measuring or operating
senses.definition: connected with scientific or technical devices that measure, record, or control something
senses.definitionCN: 与测量、记录或控制某物的科学或技术装置有关的
senses.example: The pilots reported an instrumental failure during the flight.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员报告说飞行中仪表出现了故障。
senses.why: In aviation and science the noun instrument names a measuring device, so the adjective moves from the general tool to the calibrated tool that gives readings.
senses.whyCN: 在航空与科学里，名词 instrument 专指测量装置；形容词也随之从泛指的「工具」转到能给出读数的「仪器」。

senses.title: The grammatical case of means or agent
senses.definition: in grammar, the case that marks the means, tool, or companion by which something is done
senses.definitionCN: 语法中标记做某事所借助的手段、工具或伴随者的格
senses.example: In Russian the instrumental answers the question with what.
senses.exampleCN: 在俄语中，工具格回答用什么的提问。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word from logic, where an instrument is the means to an end, so the instrumental case marks exactly that means.
senses.whyCN: 语法从逻辑学借来这个词，逻辑里 instrument 指达到目的的手段，工具格标记的正是这种手段。

senses.title: Serving as a tool of something else
senses.definition: existing or valued only as a means for reaching a further goal
senses.definitionCN: 仅为达到进一步目的而存在或被看重的
senses.example: The company treats its staff as merely instrumental to profit.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把员工仅仅当作获取利润的工具。
senses.why: Stretching the tool image abstractly gives a philosophical use: instrumental value belongs to a thing because it helps to reach another value, not because it is good in itself.
senses.whyCN: 把「工具」这一意象抽象化，就得到哲学里的用法：某物有价值是因为它能帮助达到别的价值，而不是因为它本身就好。

senses.title: Music written for instruments, as a genre
senses.definition: in music criticism, a piece or style that has no words and relies entirely on instruments
senses.definitionCN: 音乐评论中指没有歌词、完全依靠乐器的作品或风格
senses.example: The orchestral interlude is purely instrumental, with no voice at all.
senses.exampleCN: 这段管弦乐间奏纯属器乐，完全没有声音。
senses.why: Once instrumental means without the voice, it becomes a label for a genre and for whole compositions, so the adjective turns into a descriptive noun.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 instrumental 表示「没有人声」，它就成了一个体裁标签，可以用来指整部作品，形容词由此带上了名词性的描述功能。

senses.title: Helpful in bringing about an outcome
senses.definition: being a useful contributing factor rather than the main cause
senses.definitionCN: 作为有益的促成因素，而非主要原因
senses.example: A quiet room is instrumental to getting homework done quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的房间有助于快速完成作业。
senses.why: The sense of key role can be toned down: instead of the decisive tool, the word names the helpful one among several conditions.
senses.whyCN: 「关键作用」也可以弱化：这时它不是决定性的工具，而是几个条件中起帮助作用的那个。

intro.en: Instrumental comes from Medieval Latin instrumentalis, formed from the noun instrumentum, a tool or piece of equipment.
intro.cn: instrumental 来自中世纪拉丁语 instrumentalis，由名词 instrumentum（工具、设备）加形容词后缀构成。

items.en: Latin instruere means to build, equip, or arrange, literally to pile things up.
items.cn: 拉丁语 instruere 意为建造、装备、安排，字面义是「堆叠起来」。

items.en: The noun instrumentum means a tool, a piece of equipment, or a document that equips an argument.
items.cn: 名词 instrumentum 意为工具、设备，也可指使论证「装备齐备」的文件。

items.en: Instrumentalis is built from instrumentum and the adjective suffix -alis, meaning relating to.
items.cn: instrumentalis 由 instrumentum 加形容词后缀 -alis（与……有关的）构成。

items.en: Grammar takes the term for the case that marks the means, and philosophers use it for value that merely serves another end.
items.cn: 语法学借这个词表示「手段格」，哲学家也用它指只为别的目的服务的价值。

items.en: The first recorded eras of the word in English are uncertain in place, but instrumental is used in its older Latin senses before the musical one.
items.cn: 该词进入英语的最早年代与出处尚不确定；一般认为它先在拉丁语涉及的原义上使用，音乐义出现较晚。

items.en: From about the eighteenth century instrumental also describes music played on instruments, and later the instruments of science.
items.cn: 大约从十八世纪起，instrumental 也用来形容用乐器演奏的音乐，后来又用来形容科学仪器。

note.en: Instrumental borrows the shape of instrument, and it is close to words that describe help, tools, and musical performance.
note.cn: instrumental 借用了 instrument 的词形，与表示帮助、工具和音乐演奏的一批词彼此相邻。

entries.definition: a tool, a measuring device, or a musical instrument
entries.definitionCN: 工具；仪器；乐器（同根名词）

entries.definition: a person who plays a musical instrument, or a person who holds a purely pragmatic view
entries.definitionCN: 器乐演奏者；持实用主义观点的人（派生名词）

entries.definition: the arrangement of a piece for particular instruments, or the set of instruments in a system
entries.definitionCN: 配器法；一套测量仪器或系统装置

entries.definition: extremely important for a particular result
entries.definitionCN: 至关重要的（比「起帮助作用」更强）

entries.definition: being the central point on which something turns or depends
entries.definitionCN: 关键的；起核心支点作用的

entries.definition: making a particular outcome more likely or easier
entries.definitionCN: 有助于……的；促成……的

normalIntro.en: Instrumental is the adjective of instrument, the Latin tool or equipment that makes work possible, and it has spread from tools to music and to grammar.
normalIntro.cn: instrumental 是 instrument 的形容词，原指让工作得以完成的拉丁语工具或装备，后来从工具扩展到音乐和语法。

normal.en: The collocation be instrumental in takes a noun or a doing form: instrumental in the decision, instrumental in shaping policy.
normal.cn: be instrumental in 后面接名词或动名词：instrumental in the decision、instrumental in shaping policy。

normal.en: Instrumental music is the opposite of vocal music, because instruments replace the voice.
normal.cn: instrumental music 与 vocal music 相对，因为乐器取代了人声。

normal.en: The root comes from Latin instruere, to equip or arrange, which also gives the English verb instruct.
normal.cn: 词根来自拉丁语 instruere（装备、安排），英语动词 instruct 也出自同一词根。

normal.en: Keep the suffix -ment in mind: instrument, instrumentation, instrumentalist are one family of words.
normal.cn: 记住 -ment 这一部分：instrument、instrumentation、instrumentalist 属于同一词族。

normal.en: In grammar the instrumental case marks the tool or means used to perform an action.
normal.cn: 语法中工具格（instrumental case）标记的是完成动作所用的工具或手段。

abstract.en: Picture a stage version of cause and effect: one hand holds a lever, the other pulls the load, and the lever is the instrumental part of the chain.
abstract.cn: 想象一个因果的舞台：一只手握着杠杆，另一只手拉货物，杠杆就是整条链中「起关键作用」的那一环。

abstract.en: Imagine a band without a singer, only strings, brass and drum, and the space where the voice would be is called instrumental.
abstract.cn: 想象一支没有主唱的乐队，只有弦乐、管乐和鼓，本该由歌声占据的位置就被称为 instrumental。

abstract.en: Think of a laboratory bench full of dials and needles: the readings they give are instrumental measurements rather than guesswork.
abstract.cn: 想象一张摆满表盘和指针的实验台：它们给出的读数是仪器测量结果，而不是猜测。

examples.en: Her donation was instrumental in keeping the shelter open through winter.
examples.cn: 她的捐款在让收容所撑过冬天这件事上起了关键作用。

examples.en: The band played an instrumental version of the song while the singer was ill.
examples.cn: 主唱生病期间，乐队演奏了这首歌的器乐版本。

examples.en: The report found that climate change was instrumental to the spread of the disease.
examples.cn: 报告发现气候变化对疾病传播起了推动作用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因司戳门徒」——手握工具往门上一戳，事就成了：起关键作用的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 instruere（建造、装备、安排，字面义「堆叠起来」）→ instrumentum（工具、器械、文书）→ 中世纪拉丁语 instrumentalis（与工具有关的）→ 英语 instrumental，核心义「作为工具去促成」。

sensesIntro.en: Instrumental keeps its core tool meaning in all seven senses: a person who is a tool of a result, an object that plays music, a device that measures, a case that marks means, a value that merely serves an end, a piece written without voice, and a factor that merely helps.
sensesIntro.cn: instrumental 的七个义项都保留着「工具」这一核心：成为结果的工具的人、演奏音乐的物件、测量的装置、标记手段的格、只为其目的服务的价值、无人声的作品，以及只是起帮助作用的因素。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unseen hand holds a tool and pushes it into the task, and the task moves forward because of the tool.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只看不见的手握着工具伸进事情里，事情因为这件工具而向前推进。

branches.en: THE CONTRIBUTOR: a person or condition that makes a result happen, either as the decisive force or as a helpful one.
branches.cn: 促成线：让人或条件促成结果，或作为决定力量，或只是提供帮助。

branches.en: THE MUSIC: the instrument as the tool of the musician, so music without voice becomes instrumental and even a genre label.
branches.cn: 音乐线：乐器是乐手的工具，于是没有人声的音乐被称为 instrumental，甚至成了一个体裁标签。

branches.en: THE DEVICE: in science and aviation the instrument is the calibrated tool that measures or controls.
branches.cn: 装置线：在科学与航空中，instrument 是用于测量或控制的校准过的工具。

branches.en: THE GRAMMAR: the case that marks the means is named after the very word for means.
branches.cn: 语法线：标记手段的格，直接用表示「手段」的词来命名。

branches.en: THE PHILOSOPHY: value that only exists as a means, never as an end in itself.
branches.cn: 哲学线：只作为手段存在、从不作为目的本身的价值。

intro.en: Instrumental is a Latin adjective built from a Latin verb and two Latin noun and adjective formations; English then adds ordinary suffixes to make its family.
intro.cn: instrumental 是由拉丁语动词及其两个名词、形容词构形打造的拉丁形容词；英语再普通后缀扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin instruere, instrumentum and instrumentalis are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 instruere、instrumentum 与 instrumentalis 均有文献记录，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The prefix sits inside instruere and gives the sense of building into something.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀嵌在 instruere 里，带出「往里搭建」的意思。

items.example: The verb is the building root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族「营造」的词根。

items.example: The noun turns the act of equipping into the tool itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把「装备」的动作转成了工具本身。

items.example: It forms instrumentalis.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 instrumentalis。

items.example: It forms instrumental.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 instrumental。

items.example: It forms instrumentally.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 instrumentally。

items.meaning: a person who does or supports
items.example: It forms instrumentalist.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 instrumentalist。

items.example: It forms instrumentality.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 instrumentality。

items.example: It forms instrumentation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 instrumentation。
