definition_zh: 不足的；不够的；不充分的；不能胜任的
definition_en: not enough in amount, strength, or quality for a particular need or purpose
core_image: 一只水桶里的水面远低于桶壁上的所需刻度线
scene: 山区小村里，几个孩子挤在一张旧课桌前写作业。The school has insufficient chairs for the new students.
sceneCN: 这里 insufficient 是「数量不足的」（第 1 个义项：数量上不够用）；句意：学校为新来的学生准备的椅子数量不够。

pos.zh: 形容词：不足的；不够的；不充分的

derivatives.zh: 由 insufficient 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「不够地；不充分地」
由 insufficient 换名词后缀 -cy 构成，义为「不足；不充分；机能不全」
去掉否定前缀 in- 得到的肯定形式，义为「足够的；充分的」
与 sufficient 同根的动词，义为「足够；满足需要」

senses.title: Not enough in amount
senses.definition: existing in an amount that is too small for what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 现有的数量太小，满足不了需要
senses.example: There is insufficient food for the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 食物不够整个团队吃。
senses.why: Latin sufficere means to be equal to the task, so the in- prefix simply denies it: the supply does not reach the level demanded.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sufficere 意为「足以应对」，前缀 in- 只是把它否定掉：供给没达到所需的水准。

senses.title: Adequate in strength, quality, or detail
senses.definition: not good enough or thorough enough to serve the purpose
senses.definitionCN: 质量或细致程度上达不到目的要求
senses.example: The evidence was insufficient to support the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 这项证据不足以支持该主张。
senses.why: Sufficient answers whether something measures up to a standard, so insufficient also names shortfalls in quality, effort, or proof, not just in number.
senses.whyCN: sufficient 回答的是某事是否达到标准，所以 insufficient 也指质量、努力或证据上的欠缺，而不只是数量多少。

senses.title: Not capable of meeting the need
senses.definition: not able in practice to do the job demanded, as of a person or an arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 人或安排在实际上无力承担所需工作
senses.example: The old system proved insufficient for a city of this size.
senses.exampleCN: 对这样规模的城市来说，旧系统证明不够用。
senses.why: When the standard is capability rather than quantity, the same word shifts to mean that the thing cannot carry the load it was set for.
senses.whyCN: 当衡量标准是能力而不是数量时，同一个词就转指该事物承受不了原本要它承担的负担。

senses.title: Medical shortage of a substance or function
senses.definition: in medical contexts, a deficiency of a substance, organ function, or supply in the body
senses.definitionCN: 医学语境中指体内某种物质、器官功能或供给的缺乏
senses.example: The test showed insufficient blood flow to the heart.
senses.exampleCN: 检查显示流向心脏的血流量不足。
senses.why: Medicine borrows the general shortfall for a measurable deficit in the body, such as flow, hormones, or organ output.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了「量不足」的一般用法，用来指体内可测量的缺失，例如血流、激素或器官产出。

senses.title: Procedural failure because a requirement is unmet
senses.definition: in law and administration, failing to meet a formal requirement, such as procedure, notice, or documentation
senses.definitionCN: 法律与行政中未满足程序、通知或文件等正式要求
senses.example: The appeal was dismissed for insufficient notice.
senses.exampleCN: 上诉因通知手续不全而被驳回。
senses.why: A rule sets a minimum, and falling below that line makes the act invalid, so the same shortage now refers to procedure rather than to goods.
senses.whyCN: 规则设了一条最低线，低于这条线行为就无效；于是「欠缺」不再指物品，而转指程序。

senses.title: Not enough for comfort or hospitality
senses.definition: failing to reach the usual standard of providing for a guest or a household
senses.definitionCN: 未达到招待客人或支撑家庭所需的一贯水准
senses.example: The food was plentiful, but the lodging was insufficient.
senses.exampleCN: 食物很充足，但住处不够像样。
senses.why: Hospitality has its own idea of enough, so the word can judge a welcome or a household that falls short of that standard.
senses.whyCN: 款待本身有一套「够了」的标准，所以这个词也可以评判一份热情的、或一家的条件未达这一标准。

senses.title: Not equal to a challenge
senses.definition: of a person, not having the ability needed to meet a task or expectation
senses.definitionCN: 指人缺乏完成任务或达到期望所需的能力
senses.example: The committee judged him insufficient for the position.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会认为他不能胜任这一职位。
senses.why: Sufficere literally meant to stand under a burden, so a person who is insufficient is someone unable to bear the weight placed on them.
senses.whyCN: sufficere 字面义是「在重担之下站稳」，所以 insufficient 的人就是扛不住压在身上的分量的人。

intro.en: Insufficient is Latin in- not plus sufficient, from Latin sufficere to be enough.
intro.cn: insufficient 是拉丁语否定前缀 in-（不）加 sufficient 构成，而 sufficient 来自拉丁语 sufficere（足够）。

items.en: Sufficere is built from sub- under and facere to make, literally to put under, and so to stand under a burden or be equal to it.
items.cn: sufficere 由 sub-（在下方）和 facere（做）构成，字面义是「放在下面」，引申为承得起、足以应对。

items.en: The adjective sufficiens describes something that is enough or adequate for a purpose.
items.cn: 形容词 sufficiens 描述足以应对某一目的的事物。

items.en: The negative form insufficientem places the prefix in- in front of the adjective to deny adequacy.
items.cn: 否定形式 insufficientem 把前缀 in- 放在该形容词前面，用来否定「足够」。

items.en: French passes the adjective on to English in a shortened form suited to French spelling.
items.cn: 法语把这一形容词以适合法语拼写的缩短形式传给英语。

items.en: The exact first appearance in English is uncertain, but the adjective is recorded in several Middle English sources.
items.cn: 它在英语中的确切首见年代不确定，但这一形容词在中古英语的多种文献中已有记录。

items.en: The word now covers shortfalls of money, evidence, sleep, blood supply, and formal procedure.
items.cn: 现代英语里，这个词覆盖了资金、证据、睡眠、供血以及正式程序等方面的欠缺。

note.en: Insufficient sits in the sufficere family and is close to ordinary words for not enough.
note.cn: insufficient 位于 sufficere 词族中，与日常表示「不够」的一批词相邻。

entries.definition: as much as is needed
entries.definitionCN: 足够的；充分的（去掉否定前缀 in- 的肯定形式）

entries.definition: to be enough
entries.definitionCN: 足够；满足需要

entries.definition: the state of not being enough
entries.definitionCN: 不足；不充分；机能不全

entries.definition: not good enough or not enough for the purpose
entries.definitionCN: 不合适的；不充分的（更强调达不到标准）

entries.definition: barely enough, almost too little
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅够的；偏少的

entries.definition: lacking something needed, especially in amount or quality
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏的；有缺陷的

normalIntro.en: Insufficient is the negative twin of sufficient, and the pair comes from Latin sufficere, to stand under a load.
normalIntro.cn: insufficient 是 sufficient 的否定形式，这一对词来自拉丁语 sufficere（在重担之下站稳）。

normal.en: Insufficient is formal; in speech people often say not enough when they mean the same thing.
normal.cn: insufficient 较正式；口语里人们常用 not enough 表达同样的意思。

normal.en: Bank notices use insufficient funds when an account lacks the money for a payment.
normal.cn: 银行通知里用 insufficient funds 表示账户余额不足以支付。

normal.en: Legal English pairs insufficient with evidence, notice, or grounds to describe a case that cannot go forward.
normal.cn: 法律英语把 insufficient 与证据、通知或理由搭配，形容无法继续推进的案件。

normal.en: The pair insufficient and sufficient share the Latin verb sufficere, and both use the -icient ending for enough.
normal.cn: insufficient 与 sufficient 共用拉丁语动词 sufficere，两者都用 -icient 结尾表示「够不够」。

normal.en: A useful pattern is insufficient noun, as in insufficient sleep, or be insufficient for noun.
normal.cn: 常用句式是 insufficient 加名词（如 insufficient sleep），或 be insufficient for 加名词。

abstract.en: Picture a measuring cup filled only halfway while the recipe line sits far above the liquid.
abstract.cn: 想象一只量杯只装了半杯，而食谱的刻度线远远高于液面。

abstract.en: Imagine a single thin plank offered as a bridge across a wide ditch: the length is fine, the proof is not.
abstract.cn: 想象有人用一块薄木板去架过一条宽沟：长度也许够，但证明力不够。

abstract.en: Think of a rope tested with a load far beyond what it was made to hold, and it begins to strain.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子承受远超其设计能力的重物，开始绷紧吃力。

examples.en: The relief team found insufficient water for the whole village.
examples.cn: 救援队发现村里的水不够全体村民使用。

examples.en: His explanation was insufficient to convince the panel.
examples.cn: 他的解释不足以说服评审小组。

examples.en: Insufficient sleep can affect memory and mood.
examples.cn: 睡眠不足会影响记忆和情绪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因子费心」——经费不够，才要费心去凑：不足的、不够的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sufficere（置于下方，引申为承得起、足够：sub-「在下方」+ facere「做」）→ 形容词 sufficiens（足够的）→ 加否定前缀 in- 得 insufficiens / insufficientem → 英语 insufficient，核心义「没有达到承起所需的程度」。

sensesIntro.en: Insufficient starts from a denied enough and spreads over quantity, quality, capability, medicine, procedure, hospitality, and personal ability, always naming a shortfall against a standard.
sensesIntro.cn: insufficient 从「足够」的被否定出发，进而覆盖数量、质量、能力、医学、程序、待客与个人才干，始终在说某项未达标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a container filled only partway, while the required mark stays higher than the surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只容器只装了一部分，而要求的刻度仍高过液面。

branches.en: THE HOLDING: a quantity below what a task requires is the plainest sense.
branches.cn: 存量线：数量低于任务所需，是最直白的义项。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: standards of quality, thoroughness, or hospitality decide whether the shortfall shows.
branches.cn: 标准线：质量、细致或待客的标准决定欠缺是否显现出来。

branches.en: THE CAPACITY: when the shortfall is in ability, the word describes a thing or a person that cannot bear the load.
branches.cn: 能力线：当欠缺在能力上时，这个词描述的是承受不住负担的事物或人。

branches.en: THE BODY: medicine counts deficits in flow, hormones, or organ output.
branches.cn: 身体线：医学计量的是血流、激素或器官产出的欠缺。

branches.en: THE RULE: law and administration turn the shortfall into a formal defect that stops an act.
branches.cn: 规则线：法律与行政把欠缺变成让行为无法成立的程序瑕疵。

intro.en: Insufficient is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin verb, with an -ent adjective ending in place; English adds its ordinary noun and adverb endings.
intro.cn: insufficient 由拉丁语前缀和拉丁语动词构成，带有 -ent 形容词结尾；英语再普通的名词与副词结尾扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere, sufficere and sufficiens are all recorded, so only the earliest sense of putting under a burden is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere、sufficere 与 sufficiens 均有文献记录，只有「置于重担之下」这一最早语义属于重构。

definition_zh: 岛国性；与世隔绝；狭隘；闭塞；偏狭心态
definition_en: the state of being an island or island-like, and by extension the narrow outlook of a group cut off from others
core_image: 一座被海水围住的小岛，四周只有自身岸线，看不到对岸
scene: 老渔村里的人世代只认识本村的面孔，对外面的事情了解很少。Her insularity kept her from hearing about life beyond the village.
sceneCN: 这里 insularity 是「与世隔绝、闭塞」（第 2 个义项：与外界缺乏交流的孤立状态）；句意：她的闭塞使她听不到村子以外的生活。

pos.zh: 名词：岛国性；与世隔绝；狭隘

由形容词 insular 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「以封闭的方式；狭隘地」
由 insular 加 -ism 构成的同义名词，义为「岛国心态；封闭倾向」
由拉丁语 insula 加 -ate 构成的同根动词，义为「使隔离；使绝缘」
由拉丁语 paene（几乎）加 insula 构成，义为「半岛」

senses.title: The quality of being an island
senses.definition: the physical condition of being an island, or of having the character of one
senses.definitionCN: 是一个岛、或具有岛屿性质的物理状态
senses.example: The insularity of the country shapes its shipping and farming.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家的岛国性塑造了它的航运和农业。
senses.why: Latin insula simply means island, so the noun first names the plain fact of being surrounded by water.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 insula 就是「岛」，所以这个词起初只说出「四周是水」这一朴素事实。

senses.title: Isolation from other people or places
senses.definition: the state of being cut off from outside contact, as an island is cut off by the sea
senses.definitionCN: 与外界接触被切断的状态，如同被海水隔开的岛屿
senses.example: The town struggled for decades with its insularity.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小镇几十年来一直为与世隔绝而苦恼。
senses.why: Once the island image is applied to people, the sea becomes the missing contact and the word names being shut off from the world.
senses.whyCN: 把岛屿的意象用在人身上时，海水就成了缺失的联络，这个词于是指与外界被隔断。

senses.title: Narrowness of outlook in a group or person
senses.definition: a limited and self-centred way of thinking that ignores outside ideas
senses.definitionCN: 自我中心、忽视外来观念的有限思维方式
senses.example: Critics accused the department of intellectual insularity.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者指责该系在学术上思想狭隘。
senses.why: A community closed to contact cannot compare its own ways with others, so isolation turns into a narrow viewpoint.
senses.whyCN: 一个不与外界交流的群体无法把自身做法与他人比较，孤立因此变成狭隘的视野。

senses.title: The state of being disconnected in a technical system
senses.definition: in technical writing, the condition of a component, network, or device being cut off from the rest of a system
senses.definitionCN: 技术文献中指部件、网络或设备与系统其余部分断开的状态
senses.example: Engineers tested the insularity of the backup grid.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师测试了备用电网的隔离性。
senses.why: Since the Latin source can mean a detached house as well as an island, the technical sense keeps the same shape: a component stands alone.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词源除了「岛」也能指「独立的房屋」，技术义保留同一形态：某个部件独自立着。

senses.title: The condition of an isolated economy or market
senses.definition: the state of an economy that trades little with others and relies on its own resources
senses.definitionCN: 与其他经济体贸易很少、依靠自身资源的经济状态
senses.example: Trade barriers increased the insularity of the regional market.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易壁垒加剧了该区域市场的封闭性。
senses.why: Economics reads the island image as a closed market bounded by tariffs the way an island is bounded by water.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把岛屿意象读作被关税围住的封闭市场，正如岛屿被海水围住。

senses.title: The condition of an organism that is hard to reach
senses.definition: in biology, the state of a population or species living apart from others, often on an island and developing separately
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中种群或物种与同类分离、常在岛上独自演化的状态
senses.example: The insularity of the island population produced unusual forms.
senses.exampleCN: 岛上种群的孤立性造就了不寻常的形态。
senses.why: Here the island is literal and the isolation is evolutionary: a small population cut off from the mainland changes on its own path.
senses.whyCN: 这里岛屿是字面本义，孤立是演化意义上的：与大陆隔断的小种群会沿自己的路径变化。

senses.title: The habit of a self-contained household or institution
senses.definition: the self-contained character of a household, school, or organisation that keeps its own rules and little exchange with the world outside
senses.definitionCN: 家庭、学校或机构自成一套规则、与外界少有往来的自足性质
senses.example: The old boarding school was famous for its insularity.
senses.exampleCN: 那所老寄宿学校以自成一体、与外界隔阂而闻名。
senses.why: The Latin adjective can describe a house standing alone, so insularity also names an institution that keeps to itself like such a house.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词原可形容独自立着的房屋，所以 insularity 也指像那样独守自身的机构。

intro.en: Insularity comes from Latin insularis, of an island, formed from insula, island.
intro.cn: insularity 来自拉丁语 insularis（岛屿的），由 insula（岛）加形容词后缀构成。

items.en: Insula is the Latin word for an island, and in cities also for a block of rented flats.
items.cn: insula 是拉丁语中表示「岛」的词，在城市里也指一整排出租房。

items.en: The adjective insularis means relating to an island, formed with the ending -aris.
items.cn: 形容词 insularis 意为「与岛屿有关的」，由词尾 -aris 构成。

items.en: The root is related to the word for salt, salt water, and the sea, so the image is land close to the sea.
items.cn: 这个词根与表示盐、盐水和大海的词相关，意象是紧挨着海的土地。

items.en: Latin grammarians extend insularis to things that stand alone in style or position.
items.cn: 拉丁语法学家把 insularis 扩展用来形容在风格或位置上独自成立的事物。

items.en: The Latin adjective appears in English as the noun insularity and later as the adjective insular.
items.cn: 这个拉丁形容词以名词 insularity 的形式进入英语，形容词 insular 出现稍晚。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word becomes common in discussion of national character and narrow outlook.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，这个词在讨论民族性格与狭隘视野的语境中变得常见。

note.en: Insularity is the noun of insular and belongs to the insula island family, and it is close to words for isolation and narrowness.
note.cn: insularity 是 insular 的名词，属于 insula（岛）词族，与表示孤立和狭隘的词相邻。

entries.definition: of an island, or isolated and narrow in outlook
entries.definitionCN: 岛屿的；与世隔绝的；狭隘的（同根形容词）

entries.definition: the Latin word for an island
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中「岛」一词，是本词的词根

entries.definition: land almost surrounded by water
entries.definitionCN: 几乎被水包围的陆地；半岛（同为 insula 词族）

entries.definition: the state of being apart from other people
entries.definitionCN: 与世隔绝；隐居（偏中性）

entries.definition: a narrow interest limited to one small area or group

entries.definition: the condition of being separated from others

normalIntro.en: Insularity is built on the Latin word insula, island, and it carries that image outward from geography into society and habit.
normalIntro.cn: insularity 建立在拉丁词 insula（岛）之上，并把这一意象从地理扩展到社会和习惯。

normal.en: The suffix -ity makes nouns of states, so insular plus -ity gives the state of being insular.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ity 用来表示状态，所以 insular 加 -ity 就得到「处于岛屿式孤立」的状态。

normal.en: Keep insular and insulate apart: both go back to insula, but insulate is the act of cutting off, and insularity is the condition.
normal.cn: 要分清 insular 与 insulate：二者同样追溯到 insula，但 insulate 是「隔绝」的动作，insularity 是隔绝的状态。

normal.en: The related adjective insular is often used for closed political or cultural attitudes.
normal.cn: 相关形容词 insular 常用于形容封闭的政治或文化态度。

normal.en: The Latin base insula also gives the English noun for a narrow strip of land joined to a mainland.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 insula 也派生出英语中表示与大陆相连狭长陆地的名词。

normal.en: A common pairing is cultural insularity, meaning a community that looks inward rather than outward.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 cultural insularity，指只顾向内看、不向外看的社群。

abstract.en: Picture a small round island ringed by waves, and the far shore is never visible from any hill.
abstract.cn: 想象一座被海浪围住的小圆岛，站在任何小山上都看不到对岸。

abstract.en: Imagine a room whose doors are never opened, so what happens outside never gets in.
abstract.cn: 想象一间房门从未打开的房间，外面发生的事永远进不来。

abstract.en: Think of a tight circle of friends who trust only their own jokes and their own news.
abstract.cn: 想象一小圈朋友，只相信自己圈内的笑话和消息。

examples.en: Some island languages preserve old words because of their insularity.
examples.cn: 有些岛屿语言因与世隔绝而保留了古老词语。

examples.en: The new exchange programme was designed to reduce insularity among students.
examples.cn: 新的交流项目旨在减少学生之间的封闭心态。

examples.en: Critics worried about the cultural insularity of the national film industry.
examples.cn: 评论者担心本国电影业在文化上变得封闭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因思欧拉里提」——躲在小岛上只顾自己思量，便与世隔绝：闭塞、狭隘；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 insula（岛，也指整排出租房）→ 形容词 insularis（岛屿的）→ 英语形容词 insular → 加名词后缀 -ity 成 insularity；词根一般认为与表示「盐、海水」的词同源，因岛是被海水围住的陆地。

sensesIntro.en: Insularity begins as the plain fact of being an island and then spreads to the isolation, narrowness, and self-contained character that islands suggest, from networks and markets to species and schools.
sensesIntro.cn: insularity 起初只指「是一座岛」这一事实，随后扩展到岛屿所暗示的孤立、狭隘与自成一体，涉及网络、市场、物种和学校。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small island surrounded by sea, whose only outline is its own shore.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座被海水围住的小岛，视野里只有自己的岸线。

branches.en: THE GEOGRAPHY: the physical fact of being land in water is the source of every other use.
branches.cn: 地理线：陆地被水围住这一物理事实，是其他用法的源头。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY: missing contact, whether between people or markets, is the sea turned into a closed border.
branches.cn: 边界线：缺了联系，无论发生在人与人之间还是市场之间，都是海水变成了封闭的边界。

branches.en: THE OUTLOOK: a group that keeps to itself develops a narrow, self-centred view.
branches.cn: 视野线：自成一体、不与外界往来的群体，会形成狭窄而自我中心的看法。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: a component that stands alone in a technical design repeats the island shape.
branches.cn: 系统线：技术设计中独自成立的部件，重复着岛屿的形状。

branches.en: THE SPECIES: biology keeps the literal island, where a cut-off population evolves apart.
branches.cn: 物种线：生物学保留字面意义的岛屿，那里与外界隔断的种群独自演化。

intro.en: Insularity is a Latin island root plus an English state ending; the same root also yields insular, insulate, and peninsula.
intro.cn: insularity 是拉丁语「岛」这一词根加英语表示状态的后缀；同一词根还派生 insular、insulate 与 peninsula。

latinIntro.en: Latin insula and insularis are recorded, so the island root itself is solid; only the deeper Indo-European link to words for salt and the sea is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 insula 与 insularis 均有文献记录，「岛」这个词根是可靠的；只有它与「盐、海」相关词之间更早的印欧语联系属于不确定来源。

definition_zh: 使隔热；使隔音；使绝缘；使隔离（免受影响）；（古）使成岛屿
definition_en: to cover or surround something so that heat, sound or electricity cannot pass through, or to keep a person or group apart from outside influences
core_image: 一座小岛：海水把岛与四周的陆地隔开，热量、声音和电流都难以越过那道水
scene: 老房子的屋顶一到夏天就热得像蒸笼，冬天又冷得刺骨。They spent two weeks insulating the roof so that heat would stay inside in winter.
sceneCN: 这里 insulate 是「给……做保温、隔热」（第 1 个义项：用材料包住某处，阻止热量进出）；句意：他们花了两周给屋顶做保温，好让冬天时热量留在屋内。形象就是一座被水围住的小岛。

pos.zh: 动词：使隔离，使免受影响

collocations.zh: 保温良好的；绝缘良好的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -ion 构成，义为「绝缘；隔热；隔音；绝缘材料」
由本词加施事后缀 -or 构成，义为「绝缘体；绝缘子；隔绝物」
由本词加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「绝缘的；隔热的」
与「岛」词根同源，不经过 insulate，义为「岛屿的；偏狭的」

senses.title: To stop heat from passing
senses.definition: to cover a building or container with material that slows the movement of heat
senses.definitionCN: 用材料覆盖建筑或容器，减缓热量的传递
senses.example: The walls were insulated to keep the farmhouse warm.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁做了保温处理，好让这座农舍保持温暖。
senses.why: A house stands on a piece of land like an island, and insulation turns the island wall into a thermal barrier.
senses.whyCN: 房子像一块被围住的岛，保温层把围栏变成一道阻挡热流的墙，所以「隔热」就是给人造的岛筑堤。

senses.title: To stop sound from passing
senses.definition: to make a room or part of a building less able to pass sound to or from its neighbours
senses.definitionCN: 使房间或建筑某部分不易把声音传到外面或让外面的声音传进来
senses.example: The studio is insulated so that traffic noise cannot reach the microphone.
senses.exampleCN: 录音棚做了隔音处理，所以马路上的噪声传不到麦克风里。
senses.why: Sound is another kind of flow, so the same island wall that stops heat also stops noise.
senses.whyCN: 声音也是一种流动的能量，挡住热量的那道堤当然也能挡住噪声，「隔音」由此而来。

senses.title: To stop electricity from passing
senses.definition: to cover a wire or conductor with a material that electricity cannot easily pass through
senses.definitionCN: 用电流不易通过的材料包住导线或导体
senses.example: The cable is insulated with thick plastic to prevent shocks.
senses.exampleCN: 电缆包着厚塑料层以防触电。
senses.why: An uncovered wire is a land bridge to the current; the insulating layer cuts that bridge like the sea around a real island.
senses.whyCN: 裸露的电线像一条通往电流的陆桥，绝缘层把这条桥切断，正如海水切断通往小岛的路。

senses.title: To protect from outside influence
senses.definition: to keep a person, group or activity away from the influence of the surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 使人、群体或活动远离周围环境的影响
senses.example: Parents often try to insulate children from bad news.
senses.exampleCN: 父母常常尽量让孩子免受坏消息的影响。
senses.why: Here the island is made of people rather than land, and the barrier is influence rather than heat.
senses.whyCN: 这里的岛不是陆地而是人，围栏不是挡热而是挡住影响；岛的心理很早就从地理挪到了人际关系上。

senses.title: To make into an island
senses.definition: an old and rare sense: to form land into an island or to set it apart like an island
senses.definitionCN: 罕用的古义：把陆地变成岛屿，或像岛一样把某地隔开
senses.example: An older geographical use of the verb described land that had been insulated by rising water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个动词有一种较早的地理用法，描述被上涨的水隔成岛屿的陆地。
senses.why: This is the skeleton of the word made visible again, after the thermal and social senses had grown over it.
senses.whyCN: 这是词骨本身重新露出来：隔热义和社会义一层层长上去之后，「成岛」这个最原始的画面又露了出来，所以放在最后。

intro.en: Insulate rests on Latin insula, island. The verb itself is later, and the word moved from making an island to cutting off, then to blocking heat, sound and electricity. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: insulate 的基础是拉丁语 insula（岛）。这个动词本身出现得较晚，它从「使成岛」走到「隔开」，再走到阻挡热、声与电。年代均为约数。

items.en: Insula meant an island and also a block of flats in Rome; both images involve something enclosed by a boundary.
items.cn: insula 意为「岛」，也指罗马城里的一栋公寓楼；两种形象都是被边界围住的某物。

items.en: Insulatus, made like an island, described something cut off from what surrounds it.
items.cn: insulatus 意为「被造成岛屿那样」，描述与周围隔开的某物。

items.en: The English verb is generally dated to the sixteenth century, at first meaning to make into an island or to set apart. The first attestation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语动词一般定在十六世纪，最初意为「使成岛」或「使分开」；确切首见年份不确定。

items.en: Eighteenth-century experimenters began to write of materials that cut off charge, and the physical sense of blocking heat, sound or electricity became established.
items.cn: 十八世纪的实验者开始用这个词表示「把电荷隔开」，阻挡热、声、电的物理义由此固定下来。

items.en: Steam pipes, telegraph wires and heated buildings gave the verb its ordinary use, and insulation and insulator followed as everyday nouns.
items.cn: 蒸汽管道、电报线和供暖建筑让这个动词进入日常用途，insulation 与 insulator 随之成为常用名词。

items.en: Psychology and journalism extended it to shielding people from trouble, bad news or outside pressure.
items.cn: 心理学与新闻写作把它扩展到让人免受麻烦、坏消息或外界压力。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the island root and its English offspring; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of shielding, buffering and cutting off, which separate different things.
note.cn: 形近组收「岛」词根及其英语后代；近义组收表示保护、排除、隔离的动词，它们分开的对象各不相同。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of blocking heat or sound, or for the material used; it names the result, not the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「绝缘、隔热、隔音」或所用的材料；指结果是围栏，而不是筑围栏的动作。

entries.definition: The thing that does the blocking: a material, a shaped ceramic part, or any barrier.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「绝缘体、绝缘子」；指执行阻挡的那个物件，可以是一种材料或一个成形零件。

entries.definition: Built directly on insula plus -ar, without the verb; it means of or like an island, and by extension narrow in outlook.
entries.definitionCN: 由 insula 直接加 -ar 构成，不经过动词；义为「岛屿的」，引申为「偏狭的」。

entries.definition: To keep something safe from harm; wider than insulate and implies an active agent or barrier against danger.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「保护」，使某物免受伤害；范围更宽，强调的是对危险的主动防护。

entries.definition: To place a physical object between a person and a risk, as a shield does; more visual and more personal than insulate.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「遮挡、庇护」；把实物挡在人前，比 insulate 更具体、更有人情味。

entries.definition: To soften a shock or a blow before it lands; often abstract, as in buffer a community from price rises.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「缓冲、减轻冲击」，在打击到来之前减弱它；常用于抽象场合，如让社区免受涨价冲击。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root insula and the phrases the word actually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 insula，以及这个词实际会带的搭配。

normal.en: insula is island: to insulate is literally to make something an island.
normal.cn: insula 是「岛」：insulate 字面上就是「使某物成为岛」。

normal.en: The same root gives peninsula, insular and isolate, all of them about being cut off.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 peninsula、insular、isolate，都与「被隔开」有关。

normal.en: Insulate against works for danger, cold and noise; insulate from works for people and influences.
normal.cn: insulate against 接危险、寒冷与噪声；insulate from 接人和影响。

normal.en: Insulation is the noun for the material, insulator for the part that does the job.
normal.cn: insulation 是材料或过程的名词，insulator 指执行隔绝的零件。

normal.en: A well insulated house is one whose walls slow heat down, not one whose walls are merely thick.
normal.cn: well insulated 指墙体拖慢热量传递，而不只是墙厚。

abstract.en: Picture a ring of warm water around a small house, and every degree of cold has to swim across it.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈温水围着小房子，每一分寒冷都得游过这圈水才能进来。

abstract.en: Hear a room go quiet: the music playing next door is the same music, just unable to cross the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象房间突然安静：隔壁的音乐仍是同一首歌，只是过不了那堵墙。

abstract.en: Imagine a wire wearing a plastic coat; under the coat the current stays in the copper and cannot jump out.
abstract.cn: 想象电线穿着一件塑料外套：外套里面电流仍在铜芯里，跳不出去。

examples.en: Old houses are expensive to insulate because the walls are hard to reach.
examples.cn: 旧房子做保温很贵，因为墙体难以触及。

examples.en: Thick curtains insulate the room against winter draughts.
examples.cn: 厚窗帘能挡住冬天的穿堂风，为房间保温。

examples.en: Managers should not insulate staff from honest feedback.
examples.cn: 管理者不该让员工与真实的反馈隔绝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因水累它」——小岛四周全是水，水把热和声都拦在岸边；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关（真正的词源是拉丁语 insula，岛）。

root: 拉丁语 insula（岛）→ insulatus（被造成岛屿那样的）→ insulare（使成为岛）→ 英语 verb，16 世纪意为「使成岛、使分开」→ 17 到 18 世纪用于阻拦电荷、热量与声音 → 现代引申为「使人免受外界影响」。核心义「把人或物变成一座被围住的岛」。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses put something inside a boundary so that a flow cannot cross: heat, sound, electricity, influence, or the original island itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都是把某物圈在边界里，让某种流动过不去：热量、声音、电流、外界影响，以及最原始的岛本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an island, cut off from the mainland by a ring of water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座岛，被一圈海水与大陆隔开。

branches.en: THE WALL: heat and sound are flows, and insulation is the layer that slows them.
branches.cn: 墙体线：热与声都是流动，保温层就是拖慢它们的那一层。

branches.en: THE WIRE: the coat around a conductor is a miniature island wall against charge.
branches.cn: 电线线：导线外的一层皮，就是挡住电荷的微型岛堤。

branches.en: THE PERSON: people can be turned into islands too, shielded from news and pressure.
branches.cn: 人物线：人也可以被变成岛，挡住消息与压力。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN: the geographical sense keeps the literal picture the other senses borrow.
branches.cn: 本源线：地理义保留着其他义项所借用的那个本义画面。

branches.en: ONE VERB, THREE FLOWS: heat, charge and influence all rail against the same boundary.
branches.cn: 一个动词、三种流动：热、电荷与影响撞上的都是同一道边界。

intro.en: Insulate is the island root turned into a verb; English then adds ordinary suffixes to make insulation, insulator and the adjective insulating.
intro.cn: insulate 是把「岛」词根变成动词；英语再加普通后缀，派生出 insulation、insulator 与形容词 insulating。

latinIntro.en: Latin insula is attested, and insulatus is a real Latin adjective; the earlier origin of the island word itself is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 insula 有文献记录，insulatus 是真实的拉丁形容词；而「岛」这个词更早的来源不确定。

items.example: Insula gives the core picture of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: insula 提供整个词族的核心画面。

items.example: Insulatus already means cut off from the surroundings.
items.exampleCN: insulatus 已经带有「与周围隔开」的意思。

items.example: The suffix turns the island idea into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「岛」的观念变成动词。

items.example: It forms insulation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 insulation。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: It forms insulator.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 insulator。

items.example: It forms the adjective insulating.
items.exampleCN: 它构成形容词 insulating。

items.example: It forms insular from the noun stem.
items.exampleCN: 它与名词词干组合构成 insular。

items.example: It forms insularity.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 insularity。

items.structure: form of Latin insula in Italian
items.example: The first letter changed when isolate came through Italian.
items.exampleCN: isolate 经意大利语传来时，首字母已经改变。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被分离的（isolate 的意大利语环节）
latinEntries.example: It is the link that changed the first letter.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是让首字母改变的那个环节。

definition_zh: 起义；暴动；叛乱；（部队等）反抗；反叛
definition_en: a violent attempt by a group of people who are not in power to take over a government or state, or to break away from it
core_image: 一群人从下方猛然掀翻那张象征着权力的桌子
scene: 粮价又涨了一倍，城里的人夜里聚在广场，把哨所围了起来。The governor sent troops to crush the insurrection before it could spread.
sceneCN: 这里 insurrection 是「起义、暴动」（第 1 个义项：无权者用武力推翻政府或夺取政权）；句意为总督派兵在起义蔓延之前将其镇压下去。画面是一群人从下方把权力的桌子掀翻。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加施事后缀 -ist 构成，义为「起义者；叛乱者」
由本词加后缀 -al 构成，义为「起义的；叛乱的」
由本词加后缀 -ary 构成，义为「起义的；与起义有关的」
与本词同出一词根，义为「起义者；反叛者」
由此逆构的动词，义为「起义；造反」，在现代英语中罕用

senses.title: An armed rising against a government
senses.definition: a violent rising by people with little power against the government that rules them
senses.definitionCN: 无权者以武力反抗统治自己的政府
senses.example: The insurrection began in the northern hills and reached the capital in a month.
senses.exampleCN: 起义在北方山区爆发，一个月后便蔓延到首都。
senses.why: Nothing is in charge of the insurrection: a table that was upright is being tipped over from below by many hands.
senses.whyCN: 掀桌之人为多得数不清，所以这是一场没有总指挥的暴动；桌子原本立着，被众人合力掀翻，「起义」由此得名。

senses.title: A rising to throw off a foreign power
senses.titleCN: 起义叛乱；武装反抗外族统治
senses.definition: an uprising aimed at freeing a region or a group from the control of a foreign ruler
senses.definitionCN: 旨在使某个地区或群体摆脱外来统治者控制的起义
senses.example: The colonial insurrection of the 1770s divided the empire.
senses.exampleCN: 十八世纪七十年代的殖民地起义令帝国分裂。
senses.why: The tipping power comes from outside the ruling table, so the hands belong to a people that sees itself as a separate island of its own.
senses.whyCN: 掀桌的力量来自权力桌之外，那些手属于一个自视为独立岛屿的族群；岛的意象天然适用于「脱离外族统治」。

senses.title: Local disorder, broadly
senses.definition: a less organised outbreak of violent protest, often local and without a clear plan for power
senses.definitionCN: 组织程度较低、常局限于一地、对夺权没有明确计划的暴力抗议
senses.example: Shops were boarded up during the insurrection in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 首都暴动期间，商店都钉上了木板。
senses.why: The tipping can be clumsy and local: a single street table is knocked over rather than the whole ruling house.
senses.whyCN: 掀翻可以很笨拙、很局部：只推倒街边一张桌子，而不是整座权力大厦，「骚乱」是这一条线的较轻端。

senses.title: Mutiny within an army or fleet
senses.definition: an open refusal of discipline by soldiers or sailors, who turn against their own commanders
senses.definitionCN: 士兵或水手公开拒绝服从纪律，转而反抗自己的指挥官
senses.example: The admiral was hanged for an insurrection on board his own ship.
senses.exampleCN: 这位海军上将因自己船上的哗变而被处以绞刑。
senses.why: The hands now belong to people inside the table, so tipping it over is mutiny rather than a wider rising.
senses.whyCN: 掀桌的手如今来自桌子内部，属于自己人，于是掀翻就成了哗变而不是更大范围的起义。

senses.title: Any rising in a rhetorical or religious register
senses.titleCN: （宗教、修辞）起而反抗；抗拒权威
senses.definition: a rising or revolt against a person or power in a broad, sometimes figurative register
senses.definitionCN: 在各种较宽泛的语境中奋起反抗某人或某种权力，有时为比喻用法
senses.example: Milton placed the insurrection against heaven at the centre of his epic.
senses.exampleCN: 弥尔顿把对天庭的叛逆放在了这部史诗的中心。
senses.why: Once the picture is the table being tipped, even a poet can put it in heaven and describe the same gesture.
senses.whyCN: 一旦画面成了掀翻桌子，诗人也可以把它搬到天上，描述同一个动作，比喻义由此打开。

senses.title: A wild rush in old usage
senses.definition: a rare older use in which the noun describes a sudden violent rush of water or of people against a barrier
senses.definitionCN: 罕用的古义，指水流或人群骤然猛烈地冲向屏障
senses.example: An insurrection of the tide battered the sea wall in some older sources.
senses.exampleCN: 在一些较早的文献中，一场潮水的猛冲拍打着海堤。
senses.why: The same surge that tips a table can crash against a wall, and old English kept that rushing sense beside the political one.
senses.whyCN: 掀桌的那股猛劲也可以拍打在墙上，早期英语就把这层「猛冲」和政治义并排放着。

intro.en: Insurrection is built from the Latin verb insurgere, rise up. The prefix in- is not negative here; it makes the rising happen on or against something, which gives the family its two faces.
intro.cn: insurrection 由拉丁动词 insurgere（奋起）构成。这里的前缀 in- 不是否定，而是把「弹起」落在某物之上或对抗它，这使这一词族长出两副面孔。

items.en: The verb stage in Latin is generally derived from a root behind sursum, the adverb meaning upwards. The deeper reconstruction is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语这个动词来自 sursum（向上）背后的词根；更早的重构形式不确定。

items.en: surgere meant to get up, rise or stand; it also gives surge and resurrection.
items.cn: surgere 意为「起身、起立、上升」，还给出 surge 与 resurrection。

items.en: in- plus surgere meant to rise up on something or rise up against something; the prefix is local, not negative.
items.cn: in- 加 surgere 意为「在某物之上竖起」或「对某物奋起」，前缀表示方位，不是否定。

items.en: The participle insurgens, rising up, was used of rebels; its modern descendant insurgent still names people, while the noun names the act.
items.cn: 分词 insurgens（正在竖起）被用来指反叛者；其现代后代 insurgent 指人，而名词 insurrection 指事件。

items.en: The stem insurrection- belonged to a late Latin noun formed from the verb, carried through French into English.
items.cn: 词干 insurrection- 属于由该动词构成的晚期拉丁名词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: English took the noun in the fifteenth century, at first for any rising and later mainly for armed revolts of the people.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个名词，最初泛指任何起来反抗，后来主要用于民众的武装暴动。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words formed on the same surging root; the near-meaning group gathers risings of very different scale and legality.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「弹起」词根构成的词；近义组收各种规模不同、合法程度不同的起事，彼此不可互换。

entries.definition: The person, not the event: a member of a group fighting a government; the participle gave the noun its human face.
entries.definitionCN: 指人而不指事件：参加反政府武装的一方；分词形给出的是人这一面。

entries.definition: Rising again after a setback; the prefix re- adds again, so the picture is a second rise.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「复兴的、再度兴起的」；前缀 re-「再」使画面变成第二次弹起。

entries.definition: A person who takes part in an insurrection, usually in American legal and journalistic usage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指参加暴动的人，多见于美国法律与新闻用语。

entries.definition: An organised attempt to change or remove a government, often with leaders; more structured than insurrection and sometimes used in international law.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的反抗或颠覆政府，常有领袖；比 insurrection 更有结构，国际法中也常用。

entries.definition: A refusal to obey, often from soldiers, sailors or a whole population; it also covers moral disgust, which insurrection does not.
entries.definitionCN: 拒绝服从，常出自士兵、水手或全体民众；还可指道德上的厌恶，insurrection 没有这一层。

entries.definition: A word built on exactly the same picture of rising up; it is somewhat less formal and more common in journalism.
entries.definitionCN: 与 insurrection 意思最接近，同样取「起来」的画面；语气较不正式，新闻中更常用，暗示有些自发。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root surgere and the pairs that make the word easy to confuse.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 surgere，以及让这个词容易混淆的配对。

normal.en: surgere is to rise: insurrection is a rising, the same rise as in surge.
normal.cn: surgere 是「上升」：insurrection 就是一次上升，和 surge 里的上升同源。

normal.en: Here in- is not negative, as in insecure, but directional, as in incline.
normal.cn: 这里的 in- 不是 insecure 那种否定，而是 incline 那种方向。

normal.en: The noun names the event, insurgent names the person.
normal.cn: 名词指事件，insurgent 才指人。

normal.en: resurgent adds re- again and means rising a second time.
normal.cn: resurgent 加 re-「再」，指再次兴起。

normal.en: The verb at the root of that family is surgere, the same one behind resurrection.
normal.cn: 这一词族词根上的动词是 surgere，resurrection 也出自它。

abstract.en: Picture many hands reaching under the edges of a heavy stage and lifting it all at once.
abstract.cn: 想象许多只手同时伸到一座沉重舞台的边缘下，一起把它抬起来。

abstract.en: Picture the same table tipped over instead of raised: a rising can also mean a fall for whoever was sitting on top.
abstract.cn: 再想象那张桌子被掀倒而不是抬走：对坐在上面的人来说，所谓起事也可能是他们的垮台。

abstract.en: Picture a sea wall under a surging tide, the rushing image the old speech kept inside this word.
abstract.cn: 想象海堤迎着一阵涌潮，那是早期英语留在这个词里的「猛冲」画面。

examples.en: The insurrection was put down by the army within three days.
examples.cn: 起义在三天之内就被军队镇压了。

examples.en: Historians still debate whether the insurrection had leaders or grew on its own.
examples.cn: 历史学家仍在争论这场暴动是有人领导的，还是自行发展起来的。

examples.en: Fearing an insurrection, the council closed the city gates.
examples.cn: 担心发生暴动，议会关闭了城门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「引撒乱克迅」——一群人在倒灌的乱潮里迅速起来造势；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关，真正的词根是拉丁语 surgere（起来）。

root: 拉丁语 surgere（起身、上升）具体来自 sursum（向上），更早的印欧词根一般认为与 *sor-（跳跃）相关但不确定 → 前缀 in-（在上、对抗）+ surgere → insurgere（奋起、对某人奋起）→ 分词 insurgens（正在起义的，指人）→ 晚期拉丁名词 stem → 古法语 → 英语 insurrection。核心义「从下往上猛然顶起」。

sensesIntro.en: The six senses keep the same surging rush but change who owns the power it attacks: a people, a colony, a street, a crew, heaven, a tide.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项保留同一股上冲的劲，只是改变了它攻击的权力归谁：一个民族、一块殖民地、一条街、一船人、天庭，或一场潮水。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many hands push up from under a table of power and tip it over.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多只手从权力之桌的下方往上推，把桌子掀翻。

branches.en: THE STATE: the table being tipped is a government, at home or foreign.
branches.cn: 国家线：被掀的桌子是国内或外来的政府。

branches.en: THE STREET: a single table knocked over locally, more noise than plan.
branches.cn: 街面线：只推倒街边一张桌子，声大谋少。

branches.en: THE SHIP: the hands now come from inside the crew, so it is mutiny.
branches.cn: 舰船线：出手的人来自船员内部，于是成为哗变。

branches.en: THE HEAVENS: the gesture moves into rhetoric and scripture, where it can even be holy or damned.
branches.cn: 天界线：动作进入修辞与经文，在那里可以属于神圣，也可以属于堕落。

branches.en: THE WAVE: the same rush crashes against stone, with no politics at all.
branches.cn: 潮水线：同一股猛劲拍向石头，没有任何政治含义。

intro.en: Insurrection is a Latin prefix plus the verb surgere, with a noun-forming suffix on top; the family then grows insurgent, resurge and surge.
intro.cn: insurrection 由拉丁前缀加动词 surgere 构成，再套上名词后缀；这一族随后生出 insurgent、resurge 与 surge。

latinIntro.en: Surgere and its compounds such as insurgere and resurgere are all attested in Latin; only the older Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: surgere 及其 insurgere、resurgere 等复合词在拉丁语中都有文献记录，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: Here the prefix gives the direction of the rising.
items.exampleCN: 这里这个前缀给出「弹起」的方向。

items.example: The verb is the surging root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族表示「弹起」的词根。

items.example: The prefix and the verb join into one gesture.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与动词合成同一个动作。

items.example: It forms insurrection.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 insurrection。

items.example: It forms insurgent.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 insurgent。

items.example: It forms insurrectionist.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 insurrectionist。

items.example: It forms insurrectionary.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 insurrectionary。

items.example: It forms resurgent, rising again.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 resurgent，义为「再次兴起」。

items.example: It forms resurgence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 resurgence。

latinEntries.example: It gave the English word for the people who rise.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它给出了英语中指反叛者的那个词。

definition_zh: 完好无损的；未受损伤的；完整的；原封不动的；未受损的（如声誉、体系等）
definition_en: complete and not damaged or changed, especially after something dangerous or difficult has happened
core_image: 一件瓷瓶从桌上摔下又被人稳稳接住，瓶身一道裂纹也没有
scene: 地震过后，人们以为老城会是一片废墟，走近才发现城墙几乎完好。The temple stood intact after the earthquake, though everything around it had fallen.
sceneCN: 这里 intact 是「完好无损的」（第 1 个义项：物体未受损伤、保持完整）；句意为地震之后这座神庙依然完好，尽管周围的一切都已倒塌。画面是摔下又被接住的瓷瓶。

pos.zh: 形容词：完好无损的；未受损伤的
形容词：完整的；原封不动的

collocations.zh: 不动某物；让某物保持原状

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -ness 构成，义为「完好；完整性」
与 intact 同以一个表示「触碰」的拉丁词根为核心，义为「无形的；难以捉摸的」
与 intact 共享拉丁语 tangere「触碰」的来源，前缀改为 com-，义为「接触」
与 intact 共享 tangere「触碰」的来源，义为「切线；正切」

senses.title: Not damaged
senses.titleCN: 完好无损的；未受损伤的
senses.definition: complete and unharmed by what has happened around it; used of buildings and other objects
senses.definitionCN: 周围发生变故之后仍然完整、未受损伤，多用于建筑与物品
senses.example: The old bridge was still intact after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，这座老桥仍然完好无损。
senses.why: The Latin participle means not touched, so a bridge the flood never reached is intact; this sense stays almost literal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词意为「未被碰过」；洪水没有碰到的桥就是 intact，这几乎就是「没被手摸到」的本义直接落地。

senses.title: Complete, with nothing missing
senses.definition: having all its parts, with nothing removed or broken off
senses.definitionCN: 各个部分都在，没有缺失或折断
senses.example: The manuscript survived intact, although three pages were loose.
senses.exampleCN: 手稿虽然有三页松动，但完整地保存了下来。
senses.why: Intact means still one piece, not merely undamaged, so completeness is the second face of the same image.
senses.whyCN: intact 意味着仍是整体一块，而不只是没坏；「齐全」是同一张画面的第二个侧面。

senses.title: Unchanged, left as it was
senses.definition: kept in its original state, with no part altered, moved or interfered with
senses.definitionCN: 保持在原来的状态，没有部分被改动、挪动或干预
senses.example: He left the sealed letter intact and told nobody what it said.
senses.exampleCN: 他没有拆开那封封好的信，也没有告诉任何人里面写了什么。
senses.why: An untouched object is also an unaltered one, so the same hand-that-did-not-reach becomes a picture of leaving things alone.
senses.whyCN: 未被碰过的物品同时也是未被改动的，所以同一个「手没有伸过来」的画面就成了「不去动它」。

senses.title: Undamaged by criticism or scandal
senses.definition: still respected and unspoiled after attack, criticism or a scandal
senses.definitionCN: 在遭受攻击、批评或丑闻之后仍然受人尊重、没有污点
senses.example: The judge emerged from the enquiry with her reputation intact.
senses.exampleCN: 调查结束后，这位法官的声誉未受损害。
senses.why: Reputation is treated as a fragile vessel in English, so an untarnished name is pictured as an unbroken one.
senses.whyCN: 英语把声誉当作易碎的器皿，所以名声没有污点就被画成器皿没有裂纹，「未受损」从器物延伸到名誉。

senses.title: Unchanged in structure or order
senses.definition: still functioning with its structure and relations unchanged
senses.definitionCN: 结构与关系都未改变，仍在照原样运转
senses.example: The treaty left the frontiers intact.
senses.exampleCN: 这条条约使边界保持原状。
senses.why: A system that holds its shape without breaking is the same image drawn in lines instead of clay.
senses.whyCN: 一个体系保持着形状没有折断，就是同一张画换个材料来画：从器皿换成线条，于是有了「制度照旧」的用法。

intro.en: Intact is the Latin participle intactus, not touched, made of in-, meaning not, plus tactus from tangere, to touch.
intro.cn: intact 是拉丁分词 intactus（未被触碰的），由 in-（不）加 tangus「触碰」的过去分词 tactus 构成。

items.en: A root reconstructed as to touch is generally thought to lie behind Latin tangere. The star marks a reconstruction.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁 tangere 背后有一个重构词根，表示「接触」；星号表示这是重构形式。

items.en: tangere meant to touch; its participle tactus produced contact, tactile and tangent in modern languages.
items.cn: tangere 意为「触碰」；它的分词 tactus 在后世语言中产生 contact、tactile 与 tangent。

items.en: in- not plus tactus formed intactus, untouched or unspoiled; compare integer, where the same in- attaches to the verb itself.
items.cn: in-「不」加 tactus 构成 intactus，意为「未被触碰的、未受损的」；可对比 integer，那里的 in- 直接加在动词上。

items.en: The adjective reached Middle French already meaning whole and unharmed, with the physical sense of not being touched in the lead.
items.cn: 这个形容词传入中古法语时已意为「完整、未受损」，领先的仍是「未被碰过」的物理义。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the fifteenth century, chiefly for bodies, buildings and documents that had come through danger whole.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个形容词，主要用于经历危险之后依然完整的身体、建筑与文书。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word was increasingly said of reputations, institutions and relationships rather than of solid objects.
items.cn: 二十世纪以来，这个词越来越多用于声誉、制度与关系，而不只是固体物件。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same tactile root but with different prefixes; the near-meaning group gathers words for whole, undamaged and unchanged things.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「触碰」词根、但前缀各异的词；近义组收表示完好、未损、未变的词，它们的着重点并不相同。

entries.definition: Touch itself: com- together plus tactus touched; the prefix says together, not not.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「接触」；com-「一起」加 tactus「被碰」，前缀说的是「在一起」，而 intact 说的恰好是「没有」。

entries.definition: Relating to the sense of touch; the ancient element stands alone without a prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「触觉的、有触感的」，古代词根前没有前缀，直接做形容词。

entries.definition: The noun meaning the state of being whole and unharmed; abstract where intact is an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「完好状态」；形容词 intact 描述状态，它把这一状态抽象成名词。

entries.definition: Plainly stating that harm has not happened; no connotation of completeness, which intact carries.
entries.definitionCN: 直白地表示「没有受到损害」，但不带 intact「另外还完整」的意思。

entries.definition: Never broken as a whole, especially of sleep, silence or a line; stronger about continuity than about damage.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「未被打破的」，多用于睡眠、沉默或线条；强调连续不断，而不只是没被弄坏。

entries.definition: All in one piece, complete; the plain English word behind the Latin one, with no sense of having come through danger.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「完整的、整个的」，正是这套拉丁词背后的日常英语，不强调经历过危险。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin in- plus tactus, and the partner says what intact is compared with.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语 in- 加 tactus，并用对手告诉你是已读还是未读。

normal.en: tactus is touched: intact is in- not plus touched, so untouched.
normal.cn: tactus 是「被碰过」：intact 就是 in-「不」加「被碰过」，也就是「没被碰过」。

normal.en: The same touch root gives contact, tactile, tangent and tact.
normal.cn: 同一个「触碰」词根还给出 contact、tactile、tangent 与 tact。

normal.en: tact and intact both begin with tact, but tact is skill and intact is wholeness.
normal.cn: tact 与 intact 都以 tact 开头，但 tact 是得体，intact 是完好。

normal.en: remain intact and stay intact are the two most common phrases.
normal.cn: remain intact 与 stay intact 是最常见的两个搭配。

normal.en: Intactness is the noun; intact itself is a single adjective without a plural.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 intactness，而 intact 本身只有一个形容词形式，没有复数。

abstract.en: Picture every touch leaving a fingerprint, and picture something with no fingerprints at all.
abstract.cn: 想象每次触碰都会留下指纹，再想象一样完全没有指纹的东西。

abstract.en: In physics an intact object has not reacted; in ordinary talk it has simply come through trouble unchanged.
abstract.cn: 在物理里，intact 表示没有发生反应；在日常话语里，它只是说经历过麻烦却原样不变。

abstract.en: Picture a glass that falls but lands on carpet and settles without a scratch.
abstract.cn: 想象一只玻璃杯摔下去，却落在厚地毯上，安安静静地躺稳，连一道划痕都没有。

examples.en: Despite the long journey, the porcelain vase arrived intact.
examples.cn: 尽管旅途漫长，瓷瓶运到时仍完好无损。

examples.en: The agreement became a joke, but the friendship remained intact.
examples.cn: 协议成了笑柄，可友谊仍完好如初。

examples.en: Only a strong roof can be left intact in such heavy snow.
examples.cn: 在这样的大雪中，只有结实的屋顶才能保持完好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因泰克特」——泰坦般结实，怎么碰都不坏；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。真正拆开来看，intact 就是「没被碰过」。

root: 原始印欧语重构词根 *tag-（接触）→ 拉丁语 tangere（触碰），过去分词 tactus → 拉丁形容词 intactus = in-（不）+ tactus（被碰过的），义为「未被触碰的、未受损的」→ 中古法语 intact → 英语 intact。核心义「一样东西没被任何人碰过，所以完好如新」。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses apply the same untouched picture to different things: a bridge, a manuscript, a letter, a reputation, a treaty.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项把同一张「没被碰过」的画用到不同对象上：一座桥、一叠手稿、一封信、一份名誉、一条条约。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass knocked off a table lands in a deep sofa and settles without a scratch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只玻璃杯从桌上被碰落，却稳稳陷进沙发，一道划痕都没有。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the most literal survival of the Latin meaning, a thing that came through danger untouched.
branches.cn: 物件线：最贴近拉丁本义，指经历危险却没有被碰坏的东西。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: intact means still one piece, so nothing has been removed.
branches.cn: 整体线：intact 意味着仍是一整块，所以什么也没被拿掉。

branches.en: THE SEAL: leaving something intact is simply not reaching for it.
branches.cn: 封口线：让某物保持 intact，就是把手缩回来不去碰它。

branches.en: THE ABSTRACT: reputations and treaties are treated as fragile vessels that can still be unbroken.
branches.cn: 抽象线：声誉与条约被当作还能保持不碎的易碎器皿。

branches.en: ONE PICTURE THREE HOLDS: a glass, a letter and a treaty are all judged by whether they are still whole.
branches.cn: 一张画、三种写法：玻璃杯、信件与条约都用「是否仍完整」来衡量。

intro.en: Intact is a Latin adjective made of a negative prefix and the participle of tangere, touch; English suffixes can build a noun from it but not a verb.
intro.cn: intact 是拉丁形容词，由否定前缀与 tangere（触碰）的分词构成；英语后缀能由它造出名词，却造不出动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tangere and its participle tactus are attested, and intactus is a real Latin adjective; the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tangere 及其分词 tactus 都有文献记录，intactus 也是真实的拉丁形容词；更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The prefix denies the touch in intact.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀在 intact 里否定了「触碰」。

items.example: The verb is the tactile root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族表示「触碰」的词根。

items.example: It supplies the second half of intact.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 intact 的后半部分。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: It forms intactness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intactness。

items.example: With tactus it forms contact, the opposite idea.
items.exampleCN: 与 tactus 组合构成 contact，意思正好相反。

items.example: It forms tactile, the sense of touch.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tactile，即触觉。

items.example: It forms tactile in one older spelling and other words of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tactile 的旧式写法以及同族的其他词。

definition_zh: 摄入量；一次摄入的东西；招收人数；进气管；吸收
definition_en: the amount of food, drink, or air that goes into the body, or the number of people admitted to an organization at one time
core_image: 一条管道把外面的东西吸进里面
scene: 医生建议她每天减少甜食的摄入量。The doctor advised her to reduce her daily intake of sugar.
sceneCN: 这里 intake 是「摄入量」（第 1 个义项：吃进或喝进身体的分量）；句意：医生建议她减少每天食用的糖量，也就是降低甜食摄入。

pos.zh: 摄入量；摄入的东西；招收人数；进气管；吸入

derivatives.zh: 由 intake 加 valve 构成的复合词，义为「进气阀」
由前缀 re-（再次）加 intake 构成，义为「再次摄入」，较少使用
与 intake 共享 in（进入）的方位核心，但 inlet 强调「入口」，词根不同

senses.title: Amount taken into the body
senses.definition: the amount of food, drink, or a drug that a person takes into the body
senses.definitionCN: 一个人吃进、喝进或服进身体的分量
senses.example: Doctors recommend a daily intake of two litres of water.
senses.exampleCN: 医生建议每天摄入两升水。
senses.why: The compound joins in (into) and take (to receive), so intake is literally what is taken in, and the body is the first place where things are taken in.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词由 in（进入）和 take（拿）合成，字面就是「拿进去的东西」，而身体正是人们最先「拿进去」东西的容器。

senses.title: The act of taking something in
senses.definition: the process of taking something such as food, drink, or air into the body
senses.definitionCN: 把食物、饮料或空气等吸进身体的过程
senses.example: Tobacco intake slows the healing of the throat.
senses.exampleCN: 吸入烟草会减慢喉咙的愈合。
senses.why: From the result, the word moves back to name the process itself: the act that produces the measured amount.
senses.whyCN: 从结果回推到过程，这个词又用来指「吸进去」这个动作本身，即产生那个测量量的过程。

senses.title: The air going into an engine
senses.definition: the point or pipe through which air enters an engine or machine
senses.definitionCN: 空气进入发动机或机器的入口或管道
senses.example: One air intake was blocked by leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 一个进气口被树叶堵住了。
senses.why: Machines also take things in; the word then names not the amount but the opening that lets the air in.
senses.whyCN: 机器同样要「吸入」东西，于是这个词不指分量，而指让空气进入的那个口子。

senses.title: People admitted at one time
senses.definition: the number of people accepted into a school, company, or organization at one time
senses.definitionCN: 学校、公司或机构一次接收的人数
senses.example: The university plans to raise its student intake next year.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学计划明年提高招生人数。
senses.why: An institution takes people in as it takes fuel in: the new members are the human substance flowing through the same gate.
senses.whyCN: 机构接收人就如同机器吸入燃料，新成员就是流经同一入口的「人」，所以 intake 也指一批新招收的人。

senses.title: Absorbing something into a system
senses.definition: the absorbing of ideas, information, or anything else into a group or system
senses.definitionCN: 把观念、信息或其他事物吸收进一个团体或系统
senses.example: The intake of new ideas is slowed by red tape.
senses.exampleCN: 繁文缛节拖慢了新观念的吸收。
senses.why: The pipeline image widens from the body and the engine to any system that takes material in and makes room for it.
senses.whyCN: 管道意象从身体、发动机扩展到任何「吸入」并容纳外来事物的系统，于是 intake 有了「吸收、领会」的抽象义。

intro.en: Intake is an English compound of in and take, formed to name what is taken in; it may have been calqued on Dutch inname, and its first certain English use as a noun is recorded in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: intake 是英语用 in 与 take 合成的复合词，用来指「被拿进去的东西」；一般认为它是对荷兰语 inname 的仿译，作为名词的确定首用记录见于十六世纪。

items.en: Inname pairs in (in) with nemen (to take), and is already used for the act of taking something in.
items.cn: 荷兰语 inname 由 in（进入）与 nemen（拿、取）构成，已经用来表示「摄入」这一动作。

items.en: Intake is recorded as an English noun in the sixteenth century; the date is firm but any claim that it was borrowed directly from Dutch is uncertain.
items.cn: intake 作为英语名词在十六世纪已有记录；年代较可靠，但「直接借自荷兰语」的说法属于推测。

items.en: The builders needed no Latin: in and take are both common English words with Germanic roots.
items.cn: 造词者并不需要借助拉丁语：in 与 take 都是源自古日耳曼语的普通英语词。

items.en: Intake is applied to the openings of engines and machines, where air is taken in.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，intake 被用来指机器和发动机上吸入空气的开口。

items.en: Modern English extends it to people admitted to institutions and to the absorption of ideas.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到机构招收的新人，以及对外来观念的吸收。

note.en: Intake belongs to the small English compound family built on in, and its closest neighbours are words for taking in.
note.cn: intake 属于英语中以 in 构成的小型复合词家族，最接近的词都是表示「拿进来」的动词和名词。

entries.definition: the act of taking something in, such as nutrients or knowledge
entries.definitionCN: 吸收；摄取（与 intake 同构，方向朝上）

entries.definition: a part of a recording left out of the final version
entries.definitionCN: 舍弃片段；未采用的选段

entries.definition: the pipe that carries air or liquid into a machine
entries.definitionCN: 进气管

entries.definition: the act of eating, drinking, or using something up
entries.definitionCN: 消耗；消费

entries.definition: the act of allowing a person to enter a place or group
entries.definitionCN: 准入；录取

entries.definition: a narrow opening through which liquid or air enters
entries.definitionCN: 进水口；入口

normalIntro.en: Intake is a gate: the word is built from in plus take and names whatever is taken in.
normalIntro.cn: intake 像一道入口：它由 in 与 take 拼成，指被「拿进去」的东西。

normal.en: Daily intake counts what you eat and drink in a day.
normal.cn: daily intake 统计一天里吃进、喝进的东西。

normal.en: A calorie intake is measured in units of energy.
normal.cn: calorie intake 以能量单位来计算。

normal.en: An air intake is the mouth of an engine.
normal.cn: air intake 是发动机的「嘴」。

normal.en: Student intake is the number of people let in.
normal.cn: student intake 就是被「放进去」的人数。

normal.en: Compare uptake: uptake is closer to the body and to learning, intake is wider.
normal.cn: 对比 uptake：uptake 更偏向身体吸收与学习，intake 范围更宽。

abstract.en: Picture a river flowing through a narrow mouth into a tank.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河从窄口流进一只水箱。

abstract.en: Imagine a mouth counting each spoon of sugar.
abstract.cn: 想象一张嘴在数每一勺糖。

abstract.en: See a gate where a line of students walks in on one morning.
abstract.cn: 想象清晨一道门，让学生鱼贯而入。

examples.en: A high salt intake is linked to high blood pressure.
examples.cn: 盐摄入量过高与高血压有关。

examples.en: The air intake of the engine had to be cleaned.
examples.cn: 发动机的进气口必须清洗。

examples.en: The school recruits a small intake of pupils each year.
examples.cn: 这所学校每年招收少量学生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in + take」——往身体里「拿」食物，就是摄入；只是拆字联想，与这个词的英语复合词来源不同，词源上它更像荷兰语 inname 的仿译。

root: 英语 in（进入）+ take（拿、取）构成的复合词，一般认为是对荷兰语 inname（摄入）的仿译，字面义「拿进去的东西」，由身体的摄入引申到进气口与招收人数。

sensesIntro.en: Intake starts as the amount a body takes in, grows into the act itself, the engine port, the people admitted, and finally the absorption of ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: intake 从「身体吃进的分量」出发，扩展为吸人的动作、发动机的进气口、机构招收的人，最后落到对观念的吸收。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pipe pulling what is outside into a closed space.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根管道把外面的东西吸进闭合的空间。

branches.en: The measured amount in the body is the plainest sense.
branches.cn: 身体内的测量分量是最朴素的义项。

branches.en: The act of taking in is the process sense.
branches.cn: 「吸人」这个动作是过程义项。

branches.en: A machine port reuses the same gate image for air.
branches.cn: 机器进气口把同一种入口意象用在空气上。

branches.en: Institutions take people in as bodies take in food.
branches.cn: 机构「吸入」人，正如身体摄入食物。

branches.en: Counting intake and absorbing ideas both measure what a system lets in.
branches.cn: 计算摄入量与吸收观念都在衡量系统「让进来」多少。

intro.en: Intake is a native English compound; in supplies the direction, take supplies the verb, and each makes its own word family.
intro.cn: intake 是英语本族复合词：in 提供方向，take 提供动作，两者各自都有自己的词族。

latinIntro.en: Intake rests on Germanic English words, so its Latin links are not root connections but parallels such as incipere (to begin) and accipere (to take to oneself).
latinIntro.cn: intake 建立在日耳曼语源的英语词汇上，与拉丁语的关联不是同源，而是 incipere（开始）与 accipere（取为己有）这类结构上的平行。

items.example: In marks the direction of the compound.
items.exampleCN: in 标出这个复合词的方向。

items.example: Take is the verb the noun is built on.
items.exampleCN: take 是构成这个名词的动词。

items.example: Intake is written as one word.
items.exampleCN: intake 写作一个词。

items.example: Two intakes were recorded in one day.
items.exampleCN: 一天记录到两次摄入。

items.example: A worn intake valve lets air leak.
items.exampleCN: 磨损的进气阀会漏气。

items.example: The uptake of iron is slow.
items.exampleCN: 铁的吸收很慢。

items.example: The outtake was never broadcast.
items.exampleCN: 那段未采用的片段从未播出。

items.example: The inlet of the lake is narrow.
items.exampleCN: 湖的入口很窄。

latinEntries.meaning: to take to oneself, to receive
